# Factory agents

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/configuration/agents.md

Each agent is a file at `agents/<name>/agent.md` with YAML frontmatter for its role and execution settings, followed by its instructions in Markdown.

## An agent file

```markdown
---
description: Implements one approved change with tests
agentType: IMPLEMENT
harness: { type: claude-code, model: claude-sonnet-5-5 }
runner: linux-node
---
Write failing tests first, then implement.
Keep the change to what the acceptance criteria ask for.
```

The directory name is the agent's name. Other files refer to the agent by that name, for example `agent: implement` in an automation or `agents: [implement]` in a scorer.

## Frontmatter keys

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string | none | Shown in listings. |
| `agentType` | enum | `CUSTOM` | The role. See below. |
| `spawnableBy` | list of agent names | `[foreman]` | Every name must be an agent in the tree. |
| `idleTimeoutMinutes` | integer 1–60 | 10 | |
| `harness` | object | inherited | `type` (`claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`), optional `model`, optional `reasoningLevel` (`low`, `medium`, `high`), optional `auth`. See [Harness credentials](../infrastructure/harnesses.md#credentials). |
| `model` | string | inherited | A model name, or `router:<name>` for a router in `routers/`. |
| `runner` | string | inherited | A file name in `runners/`, without `.yaml`. |
| `secrets` | list | inherited | Names of Kiln secrets. A raw secret that is set is passed to the run as an environment variable with the same name. A typed secret passes its provider variables. See [Secrets](../management/secrets-mcps-environments.md#secrets). |
| `mcpServers` | list | inherited | Names or ids of the team's MCP servers, or built-in ids such as `linear` and `github`. See [MCP servers](../management/secrets-mcps-environments.md#mcp-servers-mcps-and-apps). |
| `environmentId` | string | inherited | A team environment (id or name): image, repositories, setup commands and secrets. See [Environments](../management/secrets-mcps-environments.md#environments). |
| `workerHost` | string | inherited | Run on a [self-hosted worker](../infrastructure/self-hosted-workers.md) with this id. `""` or `null` runs on the Kiln server. |
| `computerUse` | boolean | `true` | Computer use: a browser the agent drives, with annotated video recordings and screenshots. See [Computer use](#computer-use). |
| `computerUseModel` | string | automatic | The model for computer use, for example `claude-fable-5-1` or `claude-sonnet-5-5`. |
| `credentialStrategy` | `EXECUTOR` or `CREATOR` | factory's, else `EXECUTOR` | Whose forge identity the run acts as: the agent, or the person who started the work. |
| `networkPolicy` | object | factory's | `allowedHosts` (added to the runner's egress) and `deniedHosts` (always blocked). Literal hosts or IPs only. `null` turns an inherited policy off. |
| `required_repos` | list | none | Repositories (`owner/name` or `{owner, name}`) prepared for every run even when marked `deferred`. |

Unknown keys are errors. Every key can also be changed through the API: `PUT /api/v1/factories/{id}/agents/{name}` with the keys above plus `prompt` (a pull request for config-repo factories).

## Roles

| `agentType` | What Kiln uses it for |
| --- | --- |
| `FOREMAN` | Coordinates work items. Decides whether a spec is needed when the typed decision is unsure. A factory needs exactly one. |
| `TRIAGE` | Classifies kind and size when the `triage` decision is not confident. |
| `SPEC` | Writes the spec with numbered acceptance criteria (`AC1`, `AC2`, …) and user stories, as a draft pull request. |
| `IMPLEMENT` | Makes the change on the work item's `kiln/*` branch. |
| `VERIFY` | Checks each acceptance criterion and records a Playwright video per criterion. |
| `REVIEW` | Reviews the pull request and reports a verdict and findings. Kiln, not the agent, posts them. |
| `PLAN` | Turns a goal or PRD into a roadmap. See [Planning](../product-owners/planning.md). |
| `PO_ASSISTANT` | Reserved for spec interviews with product owners. Kiln has no built-in behavior for it yet; it runs like `CUSTOM`. |
| `CUSTOM` | Anything else. An automation can send work straight to a custom agent. In a pipeline, a custom agent's stage runs like a build stage. |

When the foreman builds the default path, it picks the first agent of each type. If there is no `IMPLEMENT` agent, it uses a `CUSTOM` agent, then the foreman. See [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md).

## Choosing a harness and model

Set exactly one of `harness` or `model` in a file, not both. `factory.yaml` must set one of them in `agentDefaults`.

- `harness` picks the program and, optionally, its model: `harness: { type: codex, model: gpt-5-codex }`.
- `model` keeps the inherited harness and changes only its model, e.g. `model: claude-fable-5-1` (Claude Fable 5.1, the most capable), `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` or `claude-haiku-5-5`.
- `model: router:by-task` picks a model per run with `routers/by-task.yaml`.

If nothing sets a harness, the run uses `claude-code`.

### Routers

A router picks a model for each run.

```yaml
# routers/by-complexity.yaml
type: complexity
default: claude-sonnet-5-5
routing:
  easy: claude-haiku-5-5
  hard: claude-fable-5-1
```

A `complexity` router asks the `model-router` decision. Its built-in policy picks `easy` when `complexity.easy >= 0.8`, `hard` when `complexity.hard >= 0.6`, and `medium` otherwise. A missing entry falls back to `default`.

```yaml
# routers/by-task.yaml
type: prompt
default: claude-sonnet-5-5
routing:
  - { description: front-end styling tasks, model: claude-haiku-5-5 }
  - { description: database migrations, model: claude-opus-5-5 }
```

A `prompt` router picks the entry whose description shares the most words (four letters or longer) with the run's prompt, or `default` when none match. [Benchmarks](../measure-and-improve/benchmarks.md) can propose a prompt router for you.

## Inheritance

Execution settings (`harness`, `model`, `runner`, `secrets`, `mcpServers`, `environmentId`) are layered:

1. `agentDefaults` in `factory.yaml`
2. the agent's frontmatter
3. the automation's frontmatter, for work that automation starts

A later layer overrides an earlier one. Setting a key to `null` clears the inherited value. Setting `harness` replaces the inherited harness and model. Setting `model` keeps the inherited harness and changes its model.

## What an agent receives

Each run gets:

- the agent's instructions,
- matching [memories](skills.md#memories) for work runs,
- every shared skill plus the agent's own skills,
- a "Reporting back to Kiln" section that tells the agent to write `.kiln/result.json` in a shape for its role, commit on the current branch, and never push, open pull requests or merge.

See [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md#the-result-file) for each role's result shape.

## Computer use

Claude Code agents get a browser, the `browser` MCP server (Playwright MCP, headless, in the sandbox). They are told to check UI changes in it: record a video per acceptance criterion with annotated clicks and typing and a chapter card per criterion (`browser_start_video`, `browser_video_show_actions`, `browser_video_chapter`, `browser_stop_video`), and take a screenshot of each change. Files go to `.kiln/artifacts/browser/`; Kiln uploads them to the run, where the video viewer plays them, and lists them under **Evidence** in the pull request.

Set `computerUse: false` on an agent (or in `agentDefaults`) to leave the browser out. `KILN_COMPUTER_USE=0` turns it off for the whole server. The sandbox image `runners/images/node` has the browser server and its Chromium installed; with the local backend Kiln starts it with `npx`. In Docker sandboxes the network is internal, so the browser is meant for the app the agent runs on `localhost`, not for browsing the web.

# Automation triggers

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/configuration/automation-triggers.md

Generated from `packages/schema/src/triggers.ts`. A trigger names a `provider` and an `event`; its `filter` accepts only the keys listed for that pair. Every key must match (AND); any value in a list matches (OR). See [Automations](automations.md) for the matcher grammar, alias resolution and bot policy.

| `issue_created` | `assignee_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `creator_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `labels` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `mentioned_user_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `project_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `projects` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `state_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `states` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `team_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `teams` (list of names (resolved on apply)) |
| `issue_labeled` | `assignee_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `creator_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `labels` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `mentioned_user_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `project_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `projects` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `state_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `states` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `team_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `teams` (list of names (resolved on apply)) |
| `issue_state_changed` | `assignee_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `creator_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `labels` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `mentioned_user_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `project_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `projects` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `state_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `states` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `team_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `teams` (list of names (resolved on apply)) |

## schedule

| Event | Filter keys |
| --- | --- |
| `cron_fired` | `schedule_ids` (list or `{in}`) |

## slack

| Event | Filter keys |
| --- | --- |
| `app_mention` | `channel_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `channels` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `keywords` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `user_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `users` (list of names (resolved on apply)) |
| `message_dm` | `channel_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `channels` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `keywords` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `user_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `users` (list of names (resolved on apply)) |

| `message_mpim` | `channel_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `channels` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `keywords` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `user_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `users` (list of names (resolved on apply)) |
| `message_posted` | `channel_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `channels` (list of names (resolved on apply)), `keywords` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `user_ids` (list or `{in, not_in}`), `users` (list of names (resolved on apply)) |

| --- | --- |

| --- | --- |
| `received` | `webhook_ids` (exactly one webhook), `payload` (payload pattern) |

Server-managed keys are rejected in definitions: GitLab `bot_mentioned` fills `mentioned` with the factory's bot, and `schedule_ids` is set from each inline schedule.

# Automations

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/configuration/automations.md

An automation is a file at `automations/<name>/automation.md` (or `automations/<name>.md`) that starts a work item when one of its triggers matches an incoming event.

## An automation file

```markdown
---
agent: foreman
triggers:
  - provider: github
    event: issue_labeled
    filter:
      repos: [acme/web]
      labels: [kiln-ready]
---
Take the labeled issue through the factory.
```

The body is the automation's prompt. Kiln appends it to the work item's body as `Automation "<name>": <prompt>`.

| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Disabled automations never fire. |
| `agent` | the foreman | When this is the `FOREMAN` agent, the work item takes the foreman's path. Any other agent runs directly on the work item. |
| `displayName` | none | |
| `triggers` | required | At least one. |

### Execution overrides

These apply to every run of work this automation starts, over the agent's own settings.

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `harness`, `model` | Set one: `harness` replaces the agent's harness and model, `model` keeps the harness. See [Inheritance](agents.md#inheritance). |
| `runner` | A file in `runners/`. |
| `secrets` | Extra secret names, resolved from the vault like the agent's own and added to them. |
| `mcpServers` | MCP servers from the team's registry, replacing the agent's list. |
| `environmentId` | A team environment (id or name): its image, repositories, setup commands and secrets. Also passed as `KILN_ENVIRONMENT_ID`. |
| `workerHost` | A self-hosted worker, passed as `KILN_WORKER_HOST`. |
| `computerUseModel` | Accepted for compatibility. |
| `idleTimeoutMinutes` | 1–60, passed as `KILN_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`. |
| `required_repos` | `owner/name` repositories prepared for every run, even when `deferred` in `factory.yaml`. |

## Triggers

Each trigger has a `provider`, an `event` and an optional `filter`. The providers are `github`, `gitlab`, `azure_devops`, `bitbucket`, `slack`, `teams`, `discord`, `linear`, `jira`, `webhook`, `schedule` and `factory`. Each event accepts its own filter keys, and validation rejects unknown events and keys. The full list is in [Automation triggers](automation-triggers.md).

- One event can match several automations; each starts its own work item.
- An automation fires at most once per delivery, even when several of its triggers match. A GitHub comment with a mention is both `issue_commented` and `issue_mentioned`, but starts one work item per automation.
- Two automations can still both fire for one action: an app mention plus a channel message on the same channel, or a Linear session plus `comment_created`. Pick one.

Ready-made automations for every connected tool, and suggestions such as auto-fixing CI failures, auto-reviewing pull requests or auditing dependencies, are listed by `GET /api/v1/automation-templates` (`?factory=<id>` fills in the alias, Linear teams and Jira projects). `POST /api/v1/factories/<id>/automations/from-template` adds one to a Kiln-managed factory.

## Filters

```yaml
filter:
  repos: [acme/web]                       # bare list: any of these
  labels: { in: [bug], not_in: [wontfix] }
  base_branches: [main, "release/*"]
  skip_bots: self
```

- Every key must match (AND). Within a key, any listed value matches (OR).
- A bare list means `in`. `{ in, not_in }` adds exclusions: `not_in` fails when any of its values is present.
- A missing or empty list adds no restriction, but provider defaults still apply.
- Matching ignores case. `keywords` matches text in the title, body or message. `paths`, `branches` and `base_branches` accept globs (`api/**`, `release/*`).
- Teams `team_ids` and `channel_ids` take only `in`.
- camelCase `baseBranches` and `prNumbers` are accepted, but not next to their snake_case twins.
- Filters decide what starts work. They do not control access.

### Bots

`skip_bots` is `all`, `self` or `none`.

| Value | Skips |
| --- | --- |
| `all` | Events from any bot. The default for GitHub. |
| `self` | Only events from Kiln's own apps. The default everywhere else. |
| `none` | Nothing. Admitting Kiln's own events can cause loops. |

### Alias filters

`teams`, `projects`, `states`, `channels`, `users` and `itemUsers` take plain names instead of IDs, and `issues` takes Linear issue numbers:

```yaml
filter: { teams: [Engineering], states: [Todo] }
```

Kiln resolves the names against the connected provider's directory when you apply the definition, and the apply fails on a name it can't resolve, so connect the provider first. A name list and its ID key (`teams` and `team_ids`) can't be used together. See [Connections](../integrations/connections.md#alias-directory).

## Stage changes

A `factory` trigger reacts when a work item in the same factory changes stage. Filter on `stages`, with task stages or Kiln's states:

| Stage | States |
| --- | --- |
| `TRIAGE` | `received`, `triaging` |
| `SPEC` | `planning`, `awaiting_spec` |
| `IMPLEMENT` | `building`, `awaiting_preview` |
| `REVIEW` | `reviewing`, `handed_off` |
| `COMPLETE` | `complete` |
| `CANCELLED` | `cancelled`, `failed` |

```markdown
---
agent: notifier
triggers:
  - provider: factory
    event: work_item_stage_changed
    filter: { stages: [handed_off] }
---
Summarize the handed-off work for the release notes.
```

- Only automations of the factory where the change happened fire. Other factories never see it.
- The new work item's title is the original title followed by `→ <state>`, and its body is the original body.
- Work started this way has the automation name `stage:<name>` as its source. Its own state changes do not trigger stage automations again, so there are no loops.

## Schedules

```yaml
triggers:
  - provider: schedule
    event: cron_fired
    schedule: { cron: "0 9 * * 1", name: weekly }
```

- `cron` takes five fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week), one of `@hourly`, `@daily`, `@midnight`, `@weekly`, `@monthly`, `@yearly`, `@annually`, or `@every <duration>` such as `@every 5m` or `@every 1h30m` (at least one minute).
- Schedules are always UTC. A `CRON_TZ=` or `TZ=` prefix and six-field (seconds) expressions are rejected.
- Fields accept `*`, numbers, ranges (`1-5`), lists (`1,15`) and steps (`*/15`). Day of week runs 0–6 from Sunday; 7 also means Sunday.
- `schedule` is only valid on `schedule`/`cron_fired` triggers. At most one schedule per automation may omit `name`.
- `name` is the schedule's identity (`<factory>/<automation>/<name>`). Changing only `cron` keeps it and its last fire time; changing `name` makes a new schedule. `schedule_ids` is managed by Kiln and can't be set in a definition.
- Kiln checks schedules on each timer tick. A schedule fires once when it is due, even if several due times passed since the last check. The first due time is counted from when Kiln first saw the schedule.

## Webhooks

To accept events from any other system, add a webhook and an automation that names it in `webhook_ids` (exactly one: a file name, a managed webhook's name, or its UID), with an optional `payload` filter on the body:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: webhook
    event: received
    filter:
      webhook_ids: [sentry]
      payload: { data: { issue: { level: [fatal] } } }
---
Investigate the alert in the payload.
```

The older `filter: { webhook: sentry }` is still accepted. Authentication, delivery rules and the payload filter reference are on [Custom webhooks](../integrations/custom-webhooks.md).

## Test filter

Kiln keeps a log of recent provider deliveries (`GET /api/v1/deliveries`, admins) and of custom webhook deliveries. `POST /api/v1/factories/<id>/automations/<name>/test-filter` with `{ "deliveryId": "<id>" }` evaluates the automation's triggers against one of them and returns `wouldTrigger` with every check's outcome.

## Run now

`POST /api/v1/factories/<id>/automations/<name>/run` (the **Run now** button) starts an enabled automation by hand, with its prompt and execution overrides, as the person who asked. It needs `send` on the factory, answers `{ "workItemId": "…" }`, and refuses a disabled automation with 409.

## Dedupe and follow-ups

Providers retry deliveries. Kiln remembers each delivery ID (GitHub's `X-GitHub-Delivery`, Slack's `event_id`, Linear's `Linear-Delivery`, Jira's `X-Atlassian-Webhook-Identifier`, GitLab's `X-Gitlab-Event-UUID`, and so on) for 7 days and ignores repeats, across restarts.

Before it starts new work, Kiln checks whether a comment, reply or session message belongs to a work item in flight: the same Slack, Teams or Discord thread, the same Linear session or issue, the same Jira issue, or the same issue or pull request on any forge. If so, the event continues that item. In chat, a plain thread reply continues the work only while the factory's `autoRespondToThreadReplies` is on (the default); otherwise it needs a mention.

- "approve", "approved", "lgtm", "ship it" or "accept" approves an open spec or preview gate.
- "reject", "changes:" or "request changes" rejects it, with the rest of the message as feedback.
- Other text answers an open question. If there is none and an agent is running on the work item, the text steers that run. Otherwise it is added to the conversation for the next agent run.

### Who may decide from a reply

Text in a thread or comment is content, not authority. A reply approves, rejects or answers a gate only when its author is one of the gate's assignees, or the gate has no assignees. Otherwise the reply is treated like any other message.

Gate assignees are people, such as `po@acme.test`, while chat tools and forges report their own user IDs. [Linked accounts](../integrations/connections.md#linked-accounts) map them, and so does the server option `identities`, keyed by `<provider>:<user>`:

```json
{ "slack:U024BE7LH": "po@acme.test", "github:alice": "alice@acme.test" }
```

A mapped reply is recorded under the person's name. An unmapped reply is recorded under the provider's user ID.

Labels, pushes and state changes never continue existing work. A merged pull request, on any forge, completes its work item.

A factory with no automations still answers direct mentions of its alias by starting foreman work.

# Typed decisions

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/configuration/decisions.md

A typed decision sends a few fields of program state and a set of typed questions to a fast decision model, gets back a probability for each answer, and turns them into an action with thresholds you write in `decisions/<name>.yaml`.

## Why typed decisions

A factory makes many small yes/no and pick-one choices per work item: is this command destructive, does this request need a spec, is this pull request risky. Kiln sends these to a decision model instead of a coding agent. The thresholds live in Kiln, so changing a policy means editing a number, not a prompt.

The primary provider is Jev from TypeSafe AI. When Jev fails or is slow, Kiln falls back to structured output from your LLM gateway. Offline and in tests, a built-in rule set answers instead.

## A decision file

```yaml
# decisions/command-guard.yaml
state: [command, cwd, repo, branch]
questions:
  risk_level: { type: choice, options: [safe, risky, destructive] }
  remote_exec: { type: probability }
  deletes_files: { type: probability }
  touches_prod: { type: probability }
policy:
  block: "risk_level.destructive >= 0.8 or remote_exec >= 0.8 or touches_prod >= 0.8"
  ask_human: "risk_level.risky >= 0.3 or risk_level.destructive >= 0.3"
on_error: llm
timeout_ms: 800
```

| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | none | |
| `provider` | `jev` | `jev`, `llm` or `fake`. Accepted by the schema; today every decision uses the providers the server is configured with. |
| `state` | required | The fields sent to the model. Only these leave Kiln. |
| `questions` | required | Named questions. See below. |
| `policy` | required | Action name to expression. See below. |
| `on_error` | `llm` | What to do when the provider fails or times out: `llm`, `allow` or `deny`. |
| `timeout_ms` | 800 | Time to wait for the primary provider. |

A file named like a built-in decision replaces it for that factory.

### Question types

| Type | Answer | Use in a policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `choice` with `options` (at least two) | A probability per option | `risk_level.destructive >= 0.8` |
| `probability` | One number from 0 to 1 | `remote_exec >= 0.8` |
| `score` with `min` (default 0) and `max` (default 1) | One number | `urgency >= 0.8` |

### How the policy picks an action

1. Kiln asks the primary provider, with `timeout_ms`.
2. If that fails and `on_error` is `llm`, Kiln asks the LLM fallback, with a timeout of at least 15 seconds.
3. Kiln evaluates the policy entries in the order they are written. The first one that is true is the action.
4. If none is true, the action is `allow`.
5. If no provider answered, the decision fails closed: the action is the first policy entry, unless `on_error` is `allow`.

Validation checks every policy expression, that it only reads questions and state fields, and that each `question.option` names a real option.

## Built-in decisions

| Name | Questions | Policy | How Kiln uses the action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command-guard` | `risk_level` (safe, risky, destructive), `remote_exec`, `deletes_files`, `touches_prod` | `block` and `ask_human` as in the example above | See [Command guard](#command-guard). |
| `triage` | `kind` (feature, bug, chore, incident, question), `size` (xs, s, m, l, xl), `duplicate_of_recent` | `duplicate: duplicate_of_recent >= 0.85` | Kiln uses kind and size when both top answers are at least 0.6; otherwise the triage agent decides. `duplicate` adds a note to the thread. |
| `foreman-routing` | `next_stage`, `needs_spec`, `needs_human` | `ask_human: needs_human >= 0.85`, `skip_spec: needs_spec <= 0.15` | Kiln reads `needs_spec` directly: 0.85 or more means a spec, 0.15 or less means none, anything else goes to the foreman agent. |
| `spec-check` | `is_testable`, `is_ambiguous` per acceptance criterion | `reject: is_testable < 0.5 or is_ambiguous >= 0.5` | Rejected criteria are sent back to the spec agent once, and any that still fail are listed on the spec gate. |
| `review-risk` | `risk_tier` (low, medium, high), `touches_sensitive_area`; sees the PR's changed files and line counts | `code_owners: risk_tier.high >= 0.5 or touches_sensitive_area >= 0.7`, `skip_review: risk_tier.low >= 0.8 and touches_sensitive_area < 0.3` | `code_owners` assigns the review to the `code-owners` role instead of the requester. `skip_review` (when the reviewer agent also accepts) opens no review item; the PR waits under Ready to merge. If the check fails, `code_owners` applies. |
| `model-router` | `complexity` (easy, medium, hard) | `easy: complexity.easy >= 0.8`, `hard: complexity.hard >= 0.6` | Picks the model of a `complexity` router. |
| `failure-category` | `failure_category` (instructions, skills, tooling, model, app_code, flaky) | none | Groups failed runs before self-improvement. |
| `inbox-urgency` | `urgency` (score 0–1) | `urgent: urgency >= 0.8` | Orders the inbox. |

All built-ins use `on_error: llm` and `timeout_ms: 800`.

## Command guard

Every shell command an agent runs is checked before it runs:

- Claude Code runs a `PreToolUse` hook on its Bash tool that sends the command to Kiln. Kiln installs the hook when its public URL is configured.
- Commands that go through the sandbox's command API are checked by the sandbox itself.
- Kiln's own setup, clone and push commands are trusted and are not checked.

The verdict:

| Action | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `allow` (no entry matched) | The command runs. |
| `ask_human` | Kiln opens a `command-approval` question for the requester and the `admins` role, and the run waits. Approve runs the command; reject, or no answer within 30 minutes, blocks it. |
| `block` | The command does not run. The agent sees "Blocked by the Kiln guardrail". |

If the Claude Code hook cannot reach Kiln, it blocks the command.

Codex and OpenCode run their own shell tools with their approval prompts turned off, and the current adapters do not install a guard hook for them. Rely on the sandbox's isolation for those harnesses.

## Logs

Every decision is logged with its name, the state that was sent, the answers, the action, the provider, whether it fell back, and the latency. The log links to the work item or run, so you can audit a decision and use past cases to compare providers.

## Data that leaves the cluster

Only the fields listed in `state` are sent. The Jev provider can apply a redaction function before sending. Confirm the provider's data retention and region terms before you send production data.

## Expression language

Pipelines (`skip_if`), gates (`rule`) and decision policies share one small expression language. It has no side effects.

| Element | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Field reference, with dots for nesting | `triage.size`, `risk_level.destructive` |
| Numbers, quoted strings, `true`, `false` | `0.8`, `'xs'`, `"bug"` |
| Comparisons | `==`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` |
| List membership | `triage.size in ['xs', 's']`, `work_item.source not in ['slack']` |
| Logic | `and`, `or`, `not`, parentheses |

Rules:

- `and` binds tighter than `or`.
- `>`, `>=`, `<` and `<=` are false unless both sides are numbers.
- `in` and `not in` are false unless the right side is a list.
- A missing field has no value. Number comparisons with it are false, and `==` only matches another missing field.
- Field names may contain letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`.

Validation reports syntax errors with the file and line.

## Related pages

- [Pipelines and gates](pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [Sandboxes](../infrastructure/sandboxes.md)
- [Architecture and security](../infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md)
- [Scorers](../measure-and-improve/scorers.md)

# Definitions as code

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/configuration/definitions-as-code.md

A factory is defined by a tree of files rooted at `factory.yaml`, which Kiln validates as a whole and applies whole or not at all.

## Layout

```text
factory.yaml
agents/<name>/agent.md                    # frontmatter + instructions
agents/<name>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md
automations/<name>/automation.md          # triggers + prompt (or automations/<name>.md)
pipelines/<name>.yaml                     # optional stage graph
gates/<name>.yaml                         # gate rules
policies/<name>.yaml                      # protected paths, approvals
decisions/<name>.yaml                     # typed decisions
runners/<name>.yaml
routers/<name>.yaml
scorers/<name>/scorer.md
benchmarks/<suite>/suite.yaml
benchmarks/<suite>/tasks/<task>.yaml
skills/<skill>/SKILL.md
webhooks/<name>.yaml
memories/<slug>.md
```

This layout matches the v1alpha1 factory definition format, with `pipelines/`, `gates/`, `policies/`, `decisions/` and `memories/` added. Files ending in `.md` have YAML frontmatter between `---` lines and a Markdown body. A file's name (or its directory's name) is the resource's name.

`README.md` and `.gitkeep` files are ignored. Any other file Kiln does not recognize, such as `.github/workflows/validate.yml`, produces an `unknown-file` warning but does not fail validation.

## factory.yaml

```yaml
schemaVersion: kiln/v1
name: web-app
alias: webapp                     # @webapp in Slack, Linear, Jira
project: customer-portal
repositories:
  - { forge: github, owner: acme, name: web-app }
  - { forge: github, owner: acme, name: design-system, deferred: true }
integrations:
  - type: slack
    slack: { autoRespondToThreadReplies: true }
  - linear
github: { factoryConfigChecks: main }
cloudProviders:
  aws: { roleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/kiln-runs }
agentDefaults:
  harness: { type: claude-code, model: router:by-task }
  runner: linux-node
selfImprovement: { failedRunThreshold: 15, reviewers: { type: team } }
defaultPipeline: feature          # omit to let the foreman choose
budgets: { perWorkItemUsd: 40, monthlyUsd: 6000 }
```

| Key | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | Must be `kiln/v1`. A `v1alpha1` tree is converted first; see [Importing v1alpha1 definitions](../overview/importing-definitions.md). |
| `name` | 1–100 characters. |
| `alias` | Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, 1–60 characters. Also the factory's ID in Kiln. When missing, the ID is `name` turned into a slug. |
| `description`, `project` | Optional. |
| `repositories` | At least one. `forge` is `github` (default), `gitlab`, `azure_devops` or `bitbucket`. With several repositories, triage picks the one each work item belongs to (from the issue and each repository's optional `description`) and every stage works in it; with one, agents work in it. `deferred: true` repositories are not cloned into sandboxes unless an automation's `required_repos` names them. |
| `integrations` | The workspace integrations this factory opts into: `slack`, `microsoft-teams`, `discord`, `linear`, `jira`, as names or as `{ type, <type>: settings }` objects. Linear and Jira are exclusive. Forges come from `repositories`. See [Connections](../integrations/connections.md#per-factory-opt-in). |
| `github` | `factoryConfigChecks`: `main` (default) or `all`. See [GitHub](../integrations/github.md#the-kilnfactory-config-check). |
| `automations` | `githubOnboardingNotices` (default `true`): once your workspace links GitHub accounts, a person who mentions `@kiln-factory` without a linked account gets one comment saying how to link it. Work still starts. `false` turns the comment off for this factory's repositories. |
| `cloudProviders` | Cloud identity federation for runs. `providers` is accepted as its older name. See below. |
| `agentDefaults` | Execution settings every agent inherits. Must set `harness` or `model`. |
| `selfImprovement` | `failedRunThreshold` 1–50 (default 25), `maxAgeDays` 1–90 (default 7), `reviewers.type` `admins` (default), `team`, `custom` or `none`, and `reviewers.emails` for `custom`. |
| `defaultPipeline` | A file name in `pipelines/`. |
| `budgets` | `perWorkItemUsd`, `monthlyUsd`. See [Policies and budgets](policies-and-budgets.md). |

### Cloud identity federation

```yaml
cloudProviders:
  aws: { roleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/kiln-runs }
  gcp:
    projectNumber: "123456789012"        # quote it
    workloadIdentityFederationPoolId: kiln
    workloadIdentityFederationProviderId: kiln-runs
    serviceAccountEmail: runs@acme.iam.gserviceaccount.com   # optional
```

Runs get these environment variables:

| Setting | Variables |
| --- | --- |
| `aws.roleArn` | `AWS_ROLE_ARN`, `AWS_ROLE_SESSION_NAME` (`kiln-run`) |
| `gcp` | `GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER`, `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_POOL_ID`, `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER_ID`, `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` (the full `projects/…/providers/…` name), `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` |

Set `cloudProviders` or the older `providers`, not both.

The other file kinds are covered on their own pages: [agents](agents.md), [skills](skills.md), [automations](automations.md), [pipelines and gates](pipelines-and-gates.md), [policies](policies-and-budgets.md), [decisions](decisions.md), [runners](../infrastructure/sandboxes.md#runner-files), [scorers](../measure-and-improve/scorers.md) and [benchmarks](../measure-and-improve/benchmarks.md). The full key reference is generated from the schema.

## Validation

Kiln validates a tree in three steps: parse each file, check it against its schema, then check references across files. Unknown keys are errors.

Cross-file rules:

- Exactly one agent has `agentType: FOREMAN`.
- `agentDefaults` sets `harness` or `model`. No file sets both.
- Every `runner` names a file in `runners/`, and every `router:<name>` model names a file in `routers/`.
- `defaultPipeline` names a file in `pipelines/`.
- `spawnableBy`, automation `agent`, scorer `agents` and benchmark `agent` name agents that exist.
- `webhook` triggers have `filter.webhook` naming a file in `webhooks/`.
- Pipeline stage IDs are unique, `agent` and `gate` exist, and `on_fail` names an earlier stage.
- Scorer label values and benchmark configuration names are unique.
- Every task a suite lists has a file in its `tasks/` folder.
- `skip_if`, gate `rule` and decision `policy` expressions parse, and policies only read their own questions and state fields.
- `custom` self-improvement reviewers have at least one email.

Errors carry the file and line:

```text
agents/triage/agent.md:3: runner missing is not defined in runners/
pipelines/feature.yaml:4: stage spec uses unknown gate spec-approvl
```

Run `kiln validate [path]` locally or in CI. It exits non-zero on any error. See the [CLI reference](../developer-tools/cli.md).

## Applying a definition

Kiln stores each tree by its definition SHA, a 40-character hash of every path and file content. Applying a tree:

- **Valid tree.** Kiln stores it, makes it the applied definition, keeps the previous SHA, and records who applied it and the diff in the audit log. New work items use it. Work items already in flight keep the SHA they started with.
- **Invalid tree.** Kiln records the attempt and the errors, and the previous definition stays active. The factory shows the first error as its last error.

`kiln diff --against applied` asks the server what would change compared with the applied definition, by resource:

```text
+ agent/docs
~ agent/review
- automation/weekly
```

`kiln apply --dry-run` validates and shows the diff without applying.

## Canary apply

`kiln apply --canary 10%` applies a valid tree as a candidate for a share of new work items. The applied definition stays in place for the rest.

- Each new work item is assigned by a stable hash of its ID, so the split stays the same for that item.
- Metrics and scores are split by definition SHA, so you can compare the two.
- You can promote the candidate to 100% or roll it back at any time.
- Kiln checks canaries on its timer. After 7 days, it promotes the candidate if its pass rate is no more than 2 points below the applied definition's, and rolls it back otherwise, including when the candidate has no scores.

A canary only starts when the factory already has an applied definition and the share is below 100%. See [Replay and canary](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md).

## Config repos on GitHub

A factory can live in a GitHub repository, called its config repo. Use the layout above: `factory.yaml` at the repository root (or in a subdirectory), `agents/<name>/agent.md`, and so on. For example, `acme/web-factory-config`.

**Connect.** Connecting a config repo reads the tree at its branch (default `main`) and directory (default the root), applies it, and binds the factory to the repository. If `factory.yaml` says `schemaVersion: v1alpha1`, Kiln converts it first; see [Importing v1alpha1 definitions](../overview/importing-definitions.md).

**Sync on push.** When Kiln receives a GitHub `push` webhook for the config repo's branch, it reads the tree again and applies it. A push that breaks validation is recorded and rejected; the last valid definition stays active. You can also trigger a sync by hand.

One exception: when the pushed tree is exactly the candidate of an open self-improvement proposal, which is what merging that proposal's pull request produces, Kiln applies it as a canary (10% by default) and marks the proposal merged. See [Self-improvement](../measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md#reviewing-a-proposal).

**Changes from Kiln.** When Kiln itself proposes a definition change, such as a self-improvement, an accepted memory, an installed skill or a router from benchmarks, it commits to a `kiln/*` branch of the config repo and opens a pull request. A person merges it, and the push applies it.

Protect the config repo's default branch so that every change needs a review and a passing validation check.

### Validate pull requests with GitHub Actions

This workflow checks out the config repo inside a Kiln checkout, installs Kiln, and runs `pnpm kiln validate .` from the config repo's directory. The CLI resolves paths against the directory you ran `pnpm` from, so `.` is the config repo.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/validate.yml
name: Validate factory definition
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out Kiln
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: fishuke/kiln
          path: kiln

      - name: Check out the definition
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: kiln/definition

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: kiln/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install Kiln
        working-directory: kiln
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Validate
        working-directory: kiln/definition
        run: pnpm kiln validate .
```

The command prints `ok <name> (<sha>): <n> agents, <n> automations` on success, prints each error as `file:line: message` and exits 1 on failure. Make the `validate` job a required status check in the branch protection rules. The workflow file itself is outside the definition layout, so validation lists it as an `unknown-file` warning.

## Editing through the API

The web app edits definitions file by file:

- `GET /api/v1/factories/{id}/files` and `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/factories/{id}/files/{path}`.
- `POST /api/v1/factories/{id}/files:batch {changes: [{path, content | null}], message}` changes several files in one commit and returns `{applied: sha}` or `{pullRequest: url}`.
- Higher-level endpoints for agents, automations, runners, routers, skills and settings (`PATCH /factories/{id}/settings`: name, alias, description, repositories, credential strategy, agent and scorer defaults, self-improvement, benchmarking model).

A Kiln-managed factory validates the whole tree and applies it atomically; nothing changes on an error. A factory stored in a config repo gets a branch and a pull request instead, and the merge applies it. `POST /factories/{id}/migrate {owner, name}` moves a managed factory into a GitHub repo through a pull request; the factory switches over when it merges.

## Creating a factory

`POST /api/v1/factories` (and the MCP tool `create_factory`) is the setup wizard in one call: repositories, which of triage, spec, implement and review to include (the foreman is always there), Slack, a tracker (Linear or Jira, with teams or projects), a cost preset (`quality` uses Claude Fable 5.1 for the foreman and spec agents and Opus 5.5 to implement; `efficient` uses Sonnet and Haiku), self-improvement on or off, and starter automations. It writes default prompts for every agent, the `github`, `slack`, `linear`/`jira`, `code-review` and `ui-verification` skills, the default scorers and the automations for the connected tools. `dryRun: true` returns the files without creating anything. `POST /factories/{id}/learning` then starts a run that studies the repositories and tools and proposes memories and prompt changes for review.

## Schemas and validation for editors and CI

These need no token:

- `GET /api/v1/factory-files/schemas`, `/schemas/v1` (every document) and `/schemas/v1/{document}` (for example `agent.schema.json`), with `ETag` and `If-None-Match`.
- `POST /api/v1/factory-files/validate {files: [{path, content}]}` returns `diagnostics` (path, line, code, message, severity) and `deferredResolutions`: models, secrets, MCP servers, worker hosts and aliases that are only checked when the tree is applied. Limits: 256 files, 256 KB per file, 2 MB in total. `kiln files validate [path]` calls it.

## Blueprints

`blueprint` in factory.yaml replaces the foreman's own workflow with an explicit graph:

```yaml
blueprint:
  entry: draft
  stages:
    draft: { prompt: Write the change and its tests., outputs: The branch. }
    check: { prompt: Review the change against the issue. }
  edges:
    to-check: { from: draft, to: check, when: the change is written }
  staffing: { foreman: foreman, draft: implement, check: review }
```

Each stage runs its staffed agent with the stage prompt. The agent can name the edge that holds (`next` in its result); with several edges and no answer the foreman decides; with one edge it is taken. A stage with no edge that holds ends the workflow, with the pull request handed off to a person.

# Pipelines and gates

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md

A pipeline is an optional file that lists a work item's stages in order; a gate is a pause in that path where a person decides before the work goes on.

## When to use a pipeline

Without a pipeline, the foreman builds a path for each work item (see [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md#the-foremans-default-path)). Add a pipeline when your team wants the same stages every time, a gate in a specific place, or loop limits you choose.

A work item uses a pipeline when `factory.yaml` sets `defaultPipeline: <name>`, or when the work item is created with a pipeline name.

## A pipeline file

```yaml
# pipelines/feature.yaml
stages:
  - { id: triage,  agent: triage }
  - { id: spec,    agent: spec, skip_if: "triage.size in ['xs','s']", gate: spec-approval }
  - { id: build,   agent: implement, fan_out: per_user_story }
  - { id: verify,  agent: verify, requires: [ci_green, criteria_videos], on_fail: build, max_loops: 3 }
  - { id: preview, action: preview.deploy, gate: preview-acceptance }
  - { id: review,  agent: review }
  - { id: handoff, action: handoff }   # people merge through branch protection
```

| Key | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `description` | Optional. |
| `stages` | At least one. Run in order. |
| `budget.maxUsd` | Accepted by the schema. Not enforced yet; use `budgets.perWorkItemUsd` in `factory.yaml`. |

### Stage keys

| Key | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Unique in the pipeline. |
| `agent` | An agent name. Set exactly one of `agent` or `action`. |
| `action` | `preview.deploy` or `handoff`. |
| `skip_if` | An [expression](decisions.md#expression-language). When true, the stage is skipped. |
| `gate` | A gate name: a file in `gates/` or a built-in gate. |
| `fan_out` | `per_user_story`: one agent run per user story in the spec. |
| `requires` | Any of `ci_green`, `criteria_videos`, `tests_pass`. |
| `on_fail` | An earlier stage's `id` to go back to when this stage fails. |
| `max_loops` | 1–10. Default 3. |
| `advisory` | For review stages. When `true`, review findings never park the work item. See below. |

### What each stage does

A stage's behavior comes from its agent's `agentType` or its action:

| Agent type or action | Stage behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `TRIAGE` | Classifies kind and size. |
| `SPEC` | Writes the spec as a draft pull request, checks each criterion with the `spec-check` decision, rewrites failing criteria once, then opens the stage's gate. If the agent fails twice, it opens a `spec-failed` question with the reason and parks the item instead. A spec review or a `spec-failed` question can be retried: the spec is written again from scratch, optionally on another model for that run. See [Retrying a spec](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md#retrying-a-spec). |
| `IMPLEMENT` or `CUSTOM` | Builds the change. Two failed attempts open a `build-failed` question and park the item. |
| `VERIFY` | Runs the verify agent and checks `requires`. |
| `REVIEW` | Reviews the pull request. `changes_requested` with findings loops back with `on_fail`. For an advisory stage without `on_fail`, or with its loops used up, Kiln posts the findings on the pull request as "Advisory review findings:" and moves on. `needs_human` posts the findings for a person and moves on. |
| `preview.deploy` | Deploys a preview, posts a card to the pull request and opens the stage's gate. Skipped when no preview provider is set or there is no pull request. |
| `handoff` | Marks the pull request ready, labels it and opens the merge gate. |

### `requires`

| Value | Passes when |
| --- | --- |
| `ci_green` | Every check run on the branch succeeded (or was neutral or skipped). While checks are pending, the item waits and Kiln checks again on each timer tick. |
| `criteria_videos` | Every acceptance criterion in the spec has a passing Playwright test with a video. |
| `tests_pass` | The verify agent's result file says `"testsPassed": true`. |

When a stage fails, Kiln goes back to `on_fail`. After `max_loops` failures, or when the stage has no `on_fail`, Kiln opens a `<stage>-stuck` question and parks the item as `blocked`. The exception is a review stage with `advisory: true`: it posts its findings on the pull request and continues to hand-off instead of parking. Answering the question resets the loop counters and retries the stage that stopped; rejecting it cancels the item.

### Expressions in `skip_if`

`skip_if` reads these fields:

| Field | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `triage.kind`, `triage.size`, `triage.summary` | `triage.kind == 'chore'` |
| `spec.criteria`, `spec.stories`, `spec.openQuestions` | |
| `work_item.title`, `work_item.kind`, `work_item.size`, `work_item.source` | `work_item.source == 'slack'` |
| `loops.<stage>` | `loops.verify >= 2` |

## Gates

A gate pauses a work item until someone decides. Gate files live in `gates/<name>.yaml`.

```yaml
# gates/spec-approval.yaml
kind: approval
approvers: [requester, role:po]
evidence: [spec, open_questions]
nudge: 24h
expire: 72h -> park
```

| Key | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | `approval`, `question`, `preview`, `merge` or `custom`. |
| `approvers` | At least one. `requester` is the person who sent the work. `role:<name>` expands to the people in that role, set in Kiln's server configuration. Anything else is taken as a user ID or email. |
| `evidence` | Labels for the evidence a decider needs. |
| `nudge` | A duration (`30m`, `24h`, `3d`). Kiln reminds the approvers in the source thread at this interval. |
| `expire` | A duration, optionally followed by `-> park`, `-> reject` or `-> approve`. Without an action, the gate parks the item. |
| `rule` | An [expression](decisions.md#expression-language). Kiln checks its syntax; it is not evaluated at run time yet. |

### Built-in gates

You can use these names without a file. A file with the same name replaces the built-in one.

| Name | Kind | Approvers | Nudge | Expire |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spec-approval` | approval | `requester`, `role:po` | 24h | `72h -> park` |
| `preview-acceptance` | preview | `requester`, `role:po` | 24h | `72h -> park` |
| `merge` | merge | `role:code-owners`, `requester` | 48h | none |

The foreman's default path uses `spec-approval` and `preview-acceptance`. Hand-off always opens a `merge` gate.

### Deciding a gate

A gate can be approved or rejected from the [inbox](../management/inbox.md), a reply in the source thread, the API or the Kiln MCP. All of them use the same code path and record who decided and through which surface. A reply in a Slack thread or on an issue or pull request decides a gate only when its author is one of the gate's assignees, or the gate has none. See [Who may decide from a reply](automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply). Only question gates take free-text answers.

| Decision | Spec gate | Preview gate | Question gate | Merge gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approve | Build starts | Work moves on to the next stage | Resumes a blocked item at the stage that stopped. For a command approval, the command runs. | Marks the item complete by human confirmation |
| Reject | Spec is rewritten with your feedback | Back to build with your feedback | Cancels a blocked item. For a command approval, the command is blocked. | Gate closes |
| Answer | Not allowed | Not allowed | Your answer is added to the conversation and the blocked item resumes at the stage that stopped | Not allowed |

When a gate expires with `park`, it closes as `expired` and the item moves to `blocked`. A message on a blocked item with nothing left open (for example, a follow-up after its question expired) resumes it at the stage that stopped. The task page also shows why it stopped, with a **Retry** button that restarts it there without a message.

Runs live in the API process, so a restart (for example a deploy) cuts off whatever was running. On startup Kiln stops those runs as `blocked`, closes the command questions they were waiting on, and moves their tasks to `blocked` with the reason "Kiln restarted while this task was working". Retry, or a message, continues the task; a follow-up continues the run.

## Related pages

- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)
- [Typed decisions](decisions.md)
- [Policies and budgets](policies-and-budgets.md)
- [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md)
- [Inbox](../management/inbox.md)

# Policies and budgets

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/configuration/policies-and-budgets.md

Policies in `policies/<name>.yaml` set rules the factory cannot change on its own, and budgets in `factory.yaml` cap what each work item may spend.

## A policy file

```yaml
# policies/guard.yaml
description: Keep the factory from weakening its own checks
protectedPaths: [policies/**, gates/**, decisions/command-guard.yaml]
twoApprovalPaths: [agents/review/**]
```

A factory can have several policy files. Kiln combines the lists from all of them.

| Key | Enforced today | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `protectedPaths` | Yes | [Self-improvement](../measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md) drops any proposed change to a matching path and lists it in the proposal. |
| `twoApprovalPaths` | Yes | A self-improvement proposal that changes a matching path needs approvals from two different people before Kiln applies it. |
| `deniedActions` | Not yet | Accepted by the schema. |
| `allowedTriggerers` | Not yet | Accepted by the schema. |
| `maxUsdPerWorkItem` | Yes | A spending cap per work item. See [Budgets](#budgets). |
| `description` | Not applicable | |

Patterns are paths relative to the definition root. `*` matches within one directory level and `**` matches across levels.

Self-improvement never changes files under `policies/` or `gates/`, whether or not a policy lists them.

## Rules that do not need a policy

Some limits are built into Kiln and cannot be turned off:

- A run token can push only `kiln/*` branches of the factory's repositories, open pull requests, comment and add labels. It cannot approve or merge, and it expires after 60 minutes.
- Kiln pushes the agent's branch itself. The agent is told not to push, open pull requests or merge.
- A work item can only become `complete` after a merge event or a person's confirmation.
- Agents cannot approve self-improvement proposals.

## Budgets

```yaml
# factory.yaml
budgets:
  perWorkItemUsd: 40
  monthlyUsd: 6000
```

| Key | Enforced today | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `perWorkItemUsd` | Yes | The default budget of each new work item. |
| `monthlyUsd` | Yes | The most the factory may spend on runs in a calendar month. |

Before each agent run, Kiln checks two limits:

- **Per work item.** The cap is the lowest of the work item's budget and every policy's `maxUsdPerWorkItem`. A work item's budget is `perWorkItemUsd`, unless the work item was created through the API with its own budget, which replaces it. When the item's spend has reached the cap, it stops as `blocked` with the reason "budget of $40 reached ($41.20 spent)".
- **Per month.** Kiln adds up the cost of all the factory's runs since the 1st of the month (UTC). When that has reached `monthlyUsd`, the item stops as `blocked` with the reason "monthly budget of $6000 for webapp reached ($6012.40 spent)".

A pipeline's `budget.maxUsd` is accepted but not enforced yet.

Cost comes from each run's harness. Claude Code and OpenCode report cost directly. Codex reports tokens, and Kiln estimates the cost from them.

Because the check runs before a run starts, the last run can take spend past the budget.

## Who may decide

Who may approve a gate is set by the gate's `approvers` (see [Pipelines and gates](pipelines-and-gates.md#gates)) and by the scopes on the person's token (see [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md)).

## Related pages

- [Pipelines and gates](pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [Self-improvement](../measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md)
- [Architecture and security](../infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md)
- [Metrics](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md)

# Skills

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/configuration/skills.md

A skill is a `SKILL.md` file with a short frontmatter and Markdown instructions that Kiln hands to agents at the start of each run.

## Where skills live

| Path | Who gets it |
| --- | --- |
| `skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` | Every agent in the factory |
| `agents/<agent>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` | Only that agent |

If an agent skill has the same name as a shared skill, validation warns that it shadows the shared one. An agent skill under an agent directory that has no `agent.md` is an error.

Other files in a skill directory, such as scripts or examples, are allowed in the tree but are not sent to agents. Only the `SKILL.md` body is.

## A skill file

```markdown
---
name: house-style
description: Named exports, zod at boundaries
owner: platform
version: "2"
---
Use named exports. Validate every external input with zod.
```

| Key | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | |
| `description` | yes | Harnesses use it to decide when the skill applies. |
| `owner` | no | Shown in the skills catalog. |
| `version` | no | A string. Shown in the catalog and used when installing. |

## How agents receive skills

At the start of a run, Kiln writes each skill to the harness's skills folder in the repository working copy:

| Harness | Folder |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| Codex | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |

The run's start state records the skill names, so a [replay](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md) uses the same set.

## Sharing skills between factories

Kiln keeps an org-wide catalog of skills. It lists every skill in every factory's applied tree, plus published skills, with owner, version, the factories that use it and a usage count. Usage goes up by one each time a run receives the skill.

- **Publish** a shared skill from a factory to make it a catalog listing. Publishing again bumps the version unless the skill sets its own `version`.
- **Install** a listing into another factory. For a factory with a [config repo](definitions-as-code.md#config-repos-on-github), Kiln opens a pull request that adds `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, labeled `kiln:skills`. For a Kiln-managed factory, Kiln applies the change directly.

Installing is a definition change, so it goes through the same validation and review as any other.

## Memories

Memories are conventions and decisions a factory has learned, such as "Use named exports". They live in the definition tree as `memories/<slug>.md`:

```markdown
---
title: Use named exports
tags: [typescript]
author: implement
---
Learned while building "Add a logo".
```

How a memory gets there:

1. An agent proposes it by adding `memories: [{ "title": "...", "body": "..." }]` to its `.kiln/result.json`, or a person proposes one. A proposal with the same title as an existing one is not duplicated.
2. A person accepts or rejects it. Accepting a memory for a config-repo factory opens a pull request labeled `kiln:memory`. For a Kiln-managed factory, Kiln applies it directly.
3. On later work runs, Kiln ranks memories against the prompt and adds up to five of them to the agent's instructions under "Factory memories".

## Related pages

- [Factory agents](agents.md)
- [Definitions as code](definitions-as-code.md)
- [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md)
- [Self-improvement](../measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md)

# API reference

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/developer-tools/api.md

Kiln's REST API lives under `/api/v1`. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (a session token from login, an API key or a scoped token); each route needs the scope shown for the factory it touches (`admin` grants every scope). People's scopes come from their team and factory roles. Send `X-Kiln-Team: <team id or slug>` to act in a team other than your first. The machine-readable document is at `/api/v1/openapi.json`, and the TypeScript SDK (`@kiln/sdk-ts`) wraps every route.

## System

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/health` | — | Health check |
| POST | `/api/v1/guard` | — | Check a shell command against the guardrail (run token) |
| GET | `/metrics` | — | Prometheus metrics (KILN_METRICS_TOKEN protects it when set) |

## Users

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/me` | — | You: user, teams, current team, role, per-factory roles and grants |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/me` | — | Update your profile, email, appearance and notification preferences |
| PUT | `/api/v1/me/password` | — | Change your password |
| PUT | `/api/v1/me/avatar` | — | Upload your avatar (raw image body, at most 1 MiB) |
| GET | `/api/v1/users/{id}/avatar` | — | A user's uploaded avatar |
| GET | `/api/v1/me/notifications` | — | Recent notifications Kiln sent you (email, Slack, Discord) and their status |
| GET | `/api/v1/me/linked-accounts` | — | Your linked accounts (identity mapping) |
| POST | `/api/v1/me/linked-accounts` | — | Link a GitHub, Slack, Discord, Linear, Jira, Teams, GitLab or Azure DevOps identity |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/me/linked-accounts/{provider}` | — | Unlink an identity |
| GET | `/api/v1/api-keys` | — | Your API keys, plus the team's agent and worker keys for team admins |
| POST | `/api/v1/api-keys` | — | Create a personal, agent or worker API key (shown once) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/api-keys/{id}` | — | Revoke an API key |

## Auth

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/auth/providers` | — | Login methods and whether signup is open |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/signup` | — | Create an account (the first one owns the default team; later ones need an invite unless signup is open) |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/login` | — | Log in with email and password; returns a session token |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/logout` | — | Revoke the current session token |
| GET | `/api/v1/auth/github/start` | — | Start GitHub login (redirects, or JSON with Accept: application/json) |
| GET | `/api/v1/auth/github/callback` | — | GitHub login callback; returns or redirects with a session token |
| GET | `/api/v1/invites/{token}` | — | Look at an invite link |
| POST | `/api/v1/invites/accept` | — | Accept an invite with your account |

## Teams

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams` | — | Your teams with your role |
| POST | `/api/v1/teams` | — | Create a team (you become its owner) |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}` | — | A team with its settings and factories |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/teams/{team}` | — | Rename a team, change its slug or avatar URL (team admin) |
| PUT | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/avatar` | — | Upload the team avatar (team admin) |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/avatar` | — | The team's uploaded avatar |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/members` | — | Team members and roles |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/members/{userId}` | — | Change a member's role (only owners grant ownership) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/members/{userId}` | — | Remove a member, or leave the team |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/invites` | — | Pending invites (team admin) |
| POST | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/invites` | — | Invite by email; the link expires in 7 days |
| POST | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/invites/{inviteId}/resend` | — | New link and 7 more days; the old link stops working |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/invites/{inviteId}` | — | Revoke an invite |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/settings` | — | Spend limit, GitHub orgs, sandbox host, egress allowlist, data storage, default factory role |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/settings` | — | Change team settings (team admin) |
| POST | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/storage/{category}/test` | — | Check a storage target (artifacts, transcripts, attachments) by writing and reading an object |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/model-keys` | — | Which team-managed model keys are set |
| PUT | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/model-keys/{provider}` | — | Set the team's Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or Bedrock key |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/model-keys/{provider}` | — | Remove a team-managed model key |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/claude-tokens` | — | The team's Claude subscription tokens with status and 5-hour and 7-day usage |
| POST | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/claude-tokens/{name}/check` | — | Check a Claude token with one minimal run (uses a little of its quota) |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/chatgpt-logins` | — | The team's ChatGPT logins (and yours) with status and usage |
| POST | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/chatgpt-logins/sign-in` | — | Sign in with ChatGPT: returns a link and a one-time code to approve |
| GET | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/chatgpt-logins/sign-in/{id}` | — | A ChatGPT sign-in: pending, succeeded, failed or cancelled |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/chatgpt-logins/sign-in/{id}` | — | Cancel a pending ChatGPT sign-in |
| POST | `/api/v1/teams/{team}/chatgpt-logins/{name}/check` | — | Check a ChatGPT login with one minimal Codex run (uses a little of its quota) |

## Definitions

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/definition` | `read` | The definition tree at the applied (or given) sha |
| POST | `/api/v1/definitions/validate` | — | Validate a definition tree |
| POST | `/api/v1/definitions/diff` | `read` | Diff a tree against the applied definition |
| POST | `/api/v1/definitions/apply` | `definitions:write` | Apply a tree atomically, optionally as a canary or dry run |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/connect` | `definitions:write` | Bind a factory to a GitHub config repo and apply it |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/sync` | `definitions:write` | Pull the config repo and apply it |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/canary/{action}` | `definitions:write` | Promote or roll back the canary definition |
| GET | `/api/v1/factory-files/schemas` | — | Published definition schema versions (no token; ETag) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factory-files/schemas/{version}` | — | Every schema document of a version (no token; ETag) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factory-files/schemas/{version}/{document}` | — | One schema document, e.g. agent.schema.json (no token; ETag) |
| POST | `/api/v1/factory-files/validate` | — | Validate files without saving: diagnostics and deferred resolutions (no token; ≤256 files, ≤256 KB each, ≤2 MB) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/files` | `read` | Every file of the applied definition (path and size) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/files/{path}` | `read` | One definition file |
| PUT | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/files/{path}` | `definitions:write` | Write one file: managed factories validate and apply; repo-backed factories get a PR |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/files/{path}` | `definitions:write` | Delete one file (same rules as PUT) |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/files:batch` | `definitions:write` | Change several files in one commit: {changes:[{path, content|null}], message} → {applied: sha} or {pullRequest: url} |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/files/commit` | `definitions:write` | Change several files in one commit with a message (null deletes); dryRun validates only |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/agents` | `read` | Agents with their resolved settings and prompts |
| PUT | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/agents/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Create or update an agent (prompt, harness, model, runner, workerHost, MCPs, secrets, spawnableBy, idle timeout, computer use, network policy) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/agents/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Delete an agent (not the foreman) |
| PUT | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/automations/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Create or update an automation |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/automations/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Delete an automation |
| PUT | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/runners/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Create or update a runner (image or platform, shape, setup commands, egress, failure retention) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/runners/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Delete a runner |
| PUT | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/routers/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Create or replace a model router (complexity or prompt) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/routers/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Delete a router |
| PUT | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/skills/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Create or update a skill (shared, or one agent's with `agent`) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/skills/{name}` | `definitions:write` | Delete a skill (?agent= for an agent's own) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/settings` | `read` | Factory settings from factory.yaml plus the avatar and where the definition lives |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/settings` | `definitions:write` | Change name, alias, description, repositories, credential strategy, agent and scorer defaults, self-improvement, benchmarking model |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/avatar` | `definitions:write` | Set the avatar from an uploaded image (file key) |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/migrate` | `definitions:write` | Move a Kiln-managed factory to a GitHub repo (opens a PR; the merge switches it over) |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/migrate/complete` | `definitions:write` | Finish the move once the migration PR merged |

| POST | `/api/v1/work-items/{id}/cancel` | `send` | Cancel a work item |

| POST | `/api/v1/work-items/{id}/pull` | `send` | Take a task to a local worktree |
| POST | `/api/v1/work-items/{id}/handback` | `send` | Hand a local task back to the factory |

## Runs

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/runs` | `read` | List runs: state[], task_status[], source[], factory_uid[], ancestor_run_id, artifact_type, q, creator, mine, created/updated filters, metadata[key]=, sort_by, cursor |
| GET | `/api/v1/runs/{id}` | `read` | A run with its state, source, root run, task and scores |
| GET | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/events` | `read` | Run events after a sequence number |
| GET | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/stream` | `read` | Run events as server-sent events |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/steer` | `send` | Send a steering message to a running agent |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/replay` | `send` | Replay from the saved start state, optionally under another sha |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/pause` | `send` | Snapshot and pause a running agent |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/resume` | `send` | Resume a paused run on any node |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel` | `send` | Cancel a run |
| POST | `/api/v1/agent-runs` | `send` | Start a run of one agent directly (no task): prompt, mode, metadata, attachments, model, workerHost |
| GET | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/timeline` | `read` | Lifecycle, events and subagent starts/finishes in time order |
| GET | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/conversation` | `read` | The run as normalized messages (instructions, prompt, agent, tools, steering) |
| GET | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/transcript` | `read` | Plain-text transcript |
| GET | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/scores` | `read` | Every score of the run, with how it was triggered |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/followups` | `send` | Follow-up message (with attachments): steers a live run, continues a finished one |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/score` | `send` | Score the run now with the scorers that cover its agent (or `scorers`); re-scoring replaces |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/interrupt` | `send` | Stop what the agent is doing; the run waits (BLOCKED) for a follow-up |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/spawn` | `send` | Start a subagent (run token of this run, or send scope); spawnableBy decides who may start whom |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/run-agents` | `send` | Start several subagents at once |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/questions` | `send` | Ask the requester (single or multi select, recommended option); answer arrives on the gate |
| PUT | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/sharing` | `send` | Share the run with signed-in people as VIEWER or EDITOR (null stops sharing) |
| GET | `/api/v1/run-by-external-reference` | `read` | The run behind a PR, issue, thread or Kiln URL (?url=) |
| GET | `/api/v1/errors` | — | Error catalog: codes, HTTP status, retryable, FAILED vs ERROR |

| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/benchmark-suites/{suite}/runs` | `definitions:write` | Run the suite: configurations (harness/model/router/runner per agent), repetitions, scorers, tasks. Not idempotent |

| GET | `/api/v1/benchmark-runs/{id}` | `read` | A benchmark run |
| POST | `/api/v1/benchmark-runs/{id}/cancel` | `definitions:write` | Cancel while running or scoring |
| GET | `/api/v1/benchmark-runs/{id}/results` | `read` | Per-configuration metrics, recommendation, Pareto chart data, spend and narrative |
| GET | `/api/v1/benchmark-runs/{id}/trials` | `read` | Trials (?task, configuration, agent_run_id) |
| GET | `/api/v1/benchmark-trials/{id}` | `read` | One trial with its scores |
| POST | `/api/v1/runs/{id}/benchmark-task` | `definitions:write` | Turn a finished run into a benchmark task of a suite |

## Custom webhooks

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/webhooks` | `read` | A factory's custom webhooks (managed and file) |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/webhooks` | `definitions:write` | Create a webhook; the secret is shown once |
| GET | `/api/v1/webhooks/{uid}` | `read` | A webhook with its ingress URL |
