| DELETE | `/api/v1/webhooks/{uid}` | `definitions:write` | Delete a webhook (automations stay but stop firing) |
| POST | `/api/v1/webhooks/{uid}/rotate` | `definitions:write` | Rotate the secret immediately |
| POST | `/api/v1/webhooks/{uid}/finish` | `definitions:write` | Finish setup with the provider's secret and enable |
| GET | `/api/v1/webhooks/{uid}/deliveries` | `read` | Recent deliveries and their status |
| GET | `/api/v1/webhooks/{uid}/deliveries/{delivery}` | `read` | One delivery with its stored payload |

## Webhooks

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/webhooks/github` | — | GitHub App webhook (X-Hub-Signature-256) |
| POST | `/webhooks/gitlab` | — | GitLab group webhook (X-Gitlab-Token) |
| POST | `/webhooks/azure-devops` | — | Azure DevOps service hooks (basic auth) |
| POST | `/webhooks/bitbucket` | — | Bitbucket Cloud webhook (X-Hub-Signature) |
| POST | `/webhooks/slack` | — | Slack Events API (signing secret) |
| POST | `/webhooks/teams` | — | Microsoft Teams Bot Framework activities (JWT) |
| POST | `/webhooks/discord` | — | Discord interactions (Ed25519) |
| POST | `/webhooks/discord/events` | — | Discord gateway events from a bridge (bearer token) |
| POST | `/webhooks/linear` | — | Linear webhook (Linear-Signature) |
| POST | `/webhooks/jira` | — | Jira webhook (?token=) |
| POST | `/webhooks/w/{uid}` | — | Custom webhook ingress: 202 {delivery_id} |
| POST | `/webhooks/w/{uid}/{token}` | — | Custom webhook ingress with a URL token |
| POST | `/webhooks/{factory}/{name}` | — | A factory's file webhook by name (older URL) |
| GET | `/oauth/{provider}/callback` | — | OAuth / app install callback (browser redirect) |
| GET | `/connect/approve/{token}` | — | Open an approval link (browser redirect) |
| GET | `/oauth/github-user/callback` | — | GitHub account linking callback (browser redirect) |

## Files

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/v1/uploads` | `send` | Upload files (multipart, up to 25 files of 25 MB): {key, name, contentType, size} of the first plus `attachments` |
| GET | `/api/v1/files/{key}` | `read` | Download a stored file (uploads, run artifacts, evidence) with its content type; supports Range |

## Tasks

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/runs` | `send` | Dispatch a prompt to the factory's foreman (optional ticket_ref, ticket_url, branch, mode) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/tasks` | `read` | List tasks: stage[], created_by[], q, created/updated after/before, sort, cursor, include_current_run |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/tasks` | `send` | Create a task for a conversation without starting work (one live task per conversation) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/tasks/{taskId}` | `read` | A task with its stage, outputs and current run |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/tasks/{taskId}` | `send` | Change title, description or stage (any direction; COMPLETE and CANCELLED close it) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/tasks/{taskId}` | `send` | Soft-delete a task (cancels it first when it is still active) |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/tasks/{taskId}/cancel` | `send` | Cancel the task and every run and subagent of it that is still going |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/tasks/{taskId}/complete` | `send` | complete_task: close the task after its PR merged (agents) or as a person's confirmation (decide:merge) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/tasks/{taskId}/outputs` | `read` | Task outputs newest first: PLAN, PULL_REQUEST, SCREENSHOT, FILE, EXTERNAL_REFERENCE |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/task-by-run` | `read` | The task a run (any run in its tree) belongs to (?run_id=) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/task-by-conversation` | `read` | The task of a conversation (?conversation_id=) |
| GET | `/api/v1/tasks` | `read` | Tasks across the factories you can read (same filters as the factory list, plus factory) |
| GET | `/api/v1/tasks/lookup` | `read` | Find a task by id, run, PR or issue URL, tracker key or branch (?reference=, &start_working=true for local commands) |
| POST | `/api/v1/tasks/{taskId}/handback` | `send` | Hand a locally worked task back with a note and the pushed branch or PR |
| GET | `/api/v1/tasks/{id}/review` | `read` | The task's pull request for review: changed files with patches, review findings, and whether you can review as your linked GitHub account |
| POST | `/api/v1/tasks/{id}/review` | `decide:merge` | Submit a review (APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, COMMENT, line comments) as your linked GitHub account; requested changes go to the agents |
| POST | `/api/v1/tasks/{id}/merge` | `decide:merge` | Merge the task's pull request as your linked GitHub account |
| GET | `/api/v1/ready-to-merge` | — | Handed-off tasks that need no code review, only a person's merge (?factory=) |

## Scorers

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/scorers` | `read` | Scorers with result counts, last scored time and kind (user | benchmark_task_correctness) |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/scorers` | `definitions:write` | Create a scorer (writes scorers/<slug>/scorer.md; a PR for repo-backed factories). Does not score past runs |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/scorers/{slug}` | `read` | One scorer with its rubric |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/scorers/{slug}` | `definitions:write` | Update a scorer (bumps its version) |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/scorers/{slug}` | `definitions:write` | Delete a scorer and every score it recorded |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/scorers/{slug}/results` | `read` | Results (classification, score, outcome, reason with include_reasons, run_id filter, cursor) |
| GET | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/scorers/{slug}/metrics` | `read` | Pass/fail counts, pass rate and series; include_cost adds judge cost |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/scorers/{slug}/dispatch` | `send` | Score up to 100 runs now (bypasses sampling; re-scoring replaces) |
| POST | `/api/v1/factories/{id}/runs/{runId}/scorer-dispatch` | `send` | Score a run with up to 100 scorers now |

## Workers

| Method | Path | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/workers` | `read` | Connected self-hosted workers with their last heartbeat, and the run queue |
| POST | `/api/v1/workers/connect` | `worker` | A worker process connects (kiln worker) and gets its instance id |
| POST | `/api/v1/workers/{instance}/heartbeat` | `worker` | Heartbeat; the reply carries cancellations and steering for its runs |
| POST | `/api/v1/workers/{instance}/claim` | `worker` | Long-poll for a run routed to this worker id (?wait= seconds, default 25) |
| POST | `/api/v1/workers/{instance}/runs/{runId}/events` | `worker` | Stream a run's events back |
| POST | `/api/v1/workers/{instance}/runs/{runId}/complete` | `worker` | Report a run's result, artifacts and pushed branches |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/workers/{instance}` | `worker` | Disconnect; its running runs fail and are retried |

## Errors

Errors are JSON: `{ "error": "message" }` with status 400 (invalid request; `issues` lists the fields), 401 (missing or invalid token), 402 (`{ "error": "budget_exceeded", "message": ... }`: the team's spend limit is reached and auto-stop is on), 403 (token lacks the scope), 404 (unknown resource), 409 (wrong state or already exists), 410 (expired invite) or 413 (upload too large).

# CLI reference

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/developer-tools/cli.md

The `kiln` CLI validates and applies factory definitions locally and talks to a Kiln server for everything else.

Set `KILN_URL` (default `http://localhost:4000`) and `KILN_TOKEN`, or put `{ "url": "...", "token": "..." }` in `~/.kiln/config.json`. In this repository run it as `pnpm kiln <command>`; paths resolve from the directory you ran pnpm in.

```text
kiln — self-hostable software factories

Definitions (local)
  kiln init [dir] [--template sdlc|single-repo|po-feature|incident]   Scaffold a definition tree
  kiln validate [path]                                                Schema and reference checks; exit 1 on errors
  kiln diff [path] [--against applied|<path>] [--factory <id>]        What an apply would change
  kiln import <src> [out]                                             Convert a v1alpha1 tree to kiln/v1
  kiln schema <kind>                                                  JSON Schema for a file kind

Factory (needs KILN_URL and KILN_TOKEN)
  kiln apply [path] [--dry-run] [--canary 10%] [--factory <id>]       Apply atomically, or as a canary
  kiln connect <owner/repo> [--dir <path>] [--ref main]               Store a factory in a GitHub config repo
  kiln factories                                                      List factories
  kiln send "<task>" --factory <id> [--body <text>]                   Create a work item
  kiln pull <task>                                                    Take a task to a local worktree
  kiln handback <task> [message]                                      Return it to the factory
  kiln dispatch "<prompt>" --factory <id> [--ticket linear:ENG-1] [--mode plan|orchestrate]   Send a prompt to the foreman
  kiln tasks --factory <id> [--stage IMPLEMENT] [--q <text>]          List tasks
  kiln tasks get|cancel|outputs <task> --factory <id>                 One task: details, cancel it, its outputs
  kiln runs [--factory <id>] [--state FAILED] [--source SLACK] [--mine]   List runs
  kiln runs get|timeline|transcript <run>                             One run
  kiln runs followup <run> <message> | interrupt <run> | cancel <run>   Talk to or stop a run
  kiln upload <file...> [--factory <id>]                              Upload attachments; prints their keys
  kiln create-factory --name <n> --repo owner/name [--repo …] [--slack] [--tracker linear|jira] [--preset quality|efficient] [--dry-run]
  kiln files validate [path]                                          Validate a tree with the server's parser (no token needed)
  kiln inbox [--all]                                                  Decisions waiting on you
  kiln decide <gate> approve|reject|answer [text]                     Decide a gate
  kiln replay <run> [--with <sha>]                                    Replay a run, optionally under another definition
  kiln steer <run> <message>                                          Steer a running agent
  kiln bench run <suite> --factory <id>                               Run a benchmark suite
  kiln metrics --factory <id> [--since <iso>]                         Factory metrics
  kiln token create --name <n> --subject <email> --grants read:*,send:webapp

Self-hosted worker (connects out to KILN_URL with a token that has the worker scope)
  kiln worker --worker-id <id> [--api-key <key>] [--backend docker|kubernetes|direct]
              [--max-concurrent-tasks N] [--one-shot] [--idle-on-complete 45m]
              [-v HOST:CONTAINER[:ro]]… [-e KEY[=VALUE]]… [--config-file worker.yaml]
              [--no-cleanup] [--metrics-port 9464] [--log-level info]
```

## Exit codes

- `0` success.
- `1` validation errors (printed as `file:line: message`), API errors (`error <status>: <message>`) or bad arguments.

## Related pages

- [API reference](api.md)
- [Kiln MCP](mcp.md)
- [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md)

# Kiln MCP

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/developer-tools/mcp.md

The Kiln MCP server is served at `<public URL>/mcp` over streamable HTTP. Agents use it to send tasks, take them to a local worktree, hand them back, decide gates and query metrics. Every call goes through the API with the caller's token, so per-factory scopes apply: a token with only `decide:preview` cannot write definitions.

## Connect

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http kiln https://kiln.example.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $KILN_TOKEN"
```

```toml
# ~/.codex/config.toml
[mcp_servers.kiln]
url = "https://kiln.example.com/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "KILN_TOKEN"
```

## Setup prompt for an agent

```text
Connect to the Kiln MCP server at https://kiln.example.com/mcp with the bearer token in $KILN_TOKEN.
List my factories, then help me send a task to the right one and follow it through the inbox.
```

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `ask_user` | Ask the requester a question and get a gate id; read the answer with get_gate. Questions can be single or multi select with a recommended option. |
| `complete_task` | Close a task. Safe to call more than once. A factory agent may close it only after its pull request merged; a person (decide:merge) confirms completion. Pass task_id, or run_id to find the task. |
| `create_factory` | Create a factory: repos, agents to enable (the foreman is always there), Slack, tracker, cost preset, self-improvement and starter automations. Use dry_run first to show the files. |
| `create_team` | Create a team. You become its owner. Needs a user token (session or personal API key). |
| `decide_gate` | Approve, reject or answer a gate. Needs the decide scope for the gate's kind. |
| `follow_up_run` | Send a follow-up to a run: steers it while it runs, continues it when it finished. |
| `get_conversation` | A task's conversation (requests, foreman messages, agent summaries, decisions), or a run's normalized conversation. |
| `get_factory_file_schema` | The definition schema catalog, or one document (e.g. agent.schema.json, factory.schema.json). |
| `get_gate` | A gate (decision) and its answer. |
| `get_metrics` | Factory metrics: PRs opened and merged, autonomy, cycle time, cost and cost per merged PR by agent (`since`), plus the autonomy funnel, PR latency medians, human interactions and period-over-period deltas (`start_date`, `end_date`, `group_by_period`). Dates are ISO. |
| `get_run` | A run's state, summary, result, artifacts and children. With conversation=true, its messages too. |
| `get_task` | Get a task by id or reference (task or run URL, PR URL, issue URL or key, branch). With start_working=true, also returns git commands to continue it in a local worktree. |
| `join_team` | Join a team by accepting an invite. Takes the invite token or the whole invite link. |
| `list_factories` | List the factories this token can see. |
| `list_forge_repositories` | Repositories the code forge can reach, for picking a new factory's repos. |
| `list_inbox` | Your inbox: questions, spec and PR reviews, blocked and failed tasks, definition changes. all=true lists the team's. |
| `list_notification_routes` | Where updates about a task go: the originating thread, issue or PR. |
| `list_tasks` | List tasks, newest first. Filter by factory, stage, creator (email) and dates (ISO). |
| `list_teams` | List the teams you belong to, with your role in each. Pass a team's slug as X-Kiln-Team to act in it. |
| `list_tracker_scopes` | Teams (Linear) or projects (Jira) of the connected tracker. |
| `message_foreman` | Message the foreman of a task. Answers its open question if there is one. |
| `plan_project` | Turn a goal or PRD into a roadmap and tracker issues for a project. |
| `propose_definition_change` | Propose a change to a factory definition (prompts, skills, settings). People review it in the inbox and approve & merge it. Set a file to null to delete it. |
| `query_runs` | Runs with filters: factory, state (QUEUED…CANCELLED), source, agent, q, created_after. Or raw rows (runs, scores, work_items) with kind. |
| `run_agents` | Start several subagents at once (fan out). Returns their runs. |
| `search_task` | Search task titles and descriptions across factories. |
| `send_task` | Send new work to a factory's foreman (factory, title, note), or hand a task you worked on locally back (task_id, branch or pr_url, note). |
| `spawn_agent` | Start a subagent of your factory for part of the work. Returns at once with the child run; follow it with get_run. Only agents whose spawnableBy allows you can be started. |
| `steer_run` | Send a steering message to a running agent. |
| `validate_factory_files` | Validate a whole definition tree without saving it: diagnostics with file and line, plus what is resolved only when applied. With apply=true and a factory, applies it (definitions:write). |

## Related pages

- [API reference](api.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md)

# Tasks, runs and subagents

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/developer-tools/tasks-and-runs.md

A **task** is a work item seen through the API: one request with its conversation, runs and outputs. A **run** is one agent execution. The foreman path starts several runs per task; agents can start subagents, so runs form a tree whose first run is the task's root.

## Dispatching work

```bash
curl -X POST "$KILN_URL/api/v1/factories/webapp/runs" -H "authorization: Bearer $KILN_TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "Fix the rounding bug in invoices", "ticket_ref": "linear:PAY-123", "mode": "plan"}'
```

The reply has `taskId`, the first `runId` when one started, `runUrl`, `state` and `foremanAgent`. `ticket_ref` is `<source>:<id>` (`linear:`, `jira:`, `github:owner/repo#12`, or anything else, kept as is). `branch` makes the task work on that branch.

**One task per incident**: a report that matches an open task joins it instead of starting new work. The match is by identity first: `correlation_key` (an incident id or alert fingerprint), alert payload fields such as `fingerprint`, `dedup_key` or `incident_id`, the tracker issue, the source URL or the pull request. Reports from a different source (an alert and a Slack message) also match by content when they share enough salient words such as service names, hosts and error codes. The reply then carries `deduplicated: { into, reason, score }` (`POST /api/v1/work-items` answers 200 instead of 201), the report and its files are added to the task, and every place it was reported hears the updates. Pass `"dedupe": false` to always start a new task. The triage agent can also fold a task into an open one it recognises as the same work. Tune it per factory:

```yaml
deduplication: { enabled: true, windowHours: 24, threshold: 0.5 }
```

**Modes**: `normal`; `plan` (the factory always writes a plan or spec first and waits for a person to approve it before anything is built); `orchestrate` (the foreman and implement agents are told to split the work across subagents).

## Task stages

| Stage | Kiln states |
| --- | --- |
| `TRIAGE` | received, triaging |
| `SPEC` | planning, awaiting_spec |
| `IMPLEMENT` | building, awaiting_preview |
| `REVIEW` | reviewing, handed_off |
| `COMPLETE` | complete |
| `CANCELLED` | cancelled, failed |

`PATCH …/tasks/{id}` may set any stage. `COMPLETE` needs `decide:merge` and closes the task as a person's confirmation; `CANCELLED` cancels it and every run and subagent still going. `DELETE` is a soft delete. Task outputs (`PLAN`, `PULL_REQUEST`, `SCREENSHOT`, `FILE`, `EXTERNAL_REFERENCE`) come newest first.

## Run states and sources

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `QUEUED` | Waiting for a [self-hosted worker](../infrastructure/self-hosted-workers.md). |
| `CLAIMED` | A worker took it and is preparing the sandbox. |
| `INPROGRESS` | The agent is working. |
| `BLOCKED` | Waiting on a person: a command approval, an interrupt, or a paused run. |
| `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `ERROR`, `CANCELLED` | Finished. `FAILED` means the task could not be done as asked; `ERROR` means the platform failed. |

The coarse `task_status` filter groups them: `running`, `blocked`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `complete`. Each run also has a `source` (`LINEAR`, `SLACK`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK`, `API`, `CLI`, `MCP`, `WEB_APP`, `SCHEDULED_AGENT`, `ORCHESTRATION`, `SELF_IMPROVEMENT`, `BENCHMARK_TRIAL`, `CUSTOM_WEBHOOK`, …), a `title`, `creator` and `executor`, `rootRunId`, and up to 20 immutable `metadata` keys you can filter on with `metadata[key]=value`.

`GET /api/v1/runs` filters by `state`, `task_status`, `source`, `factory_uid`, `ancestor_run_id`, `artifact_type`, `q`, `creator`, `mine=true`, dates and metadata, sorts with `sort_by`, and pages with `cursor`.

## Errors

Errors carry a `code` from the catalog (`GET /api/v1/errors`): for example `budget_exceeded`, `insufficient_credits`, `integration_not_configured`, `environment_setup_failed` (FAILED) and `internal_error`, `resource_unavailable`, `infrastructure_timeout`, `agent_process_failed` (ERROR). Kiln retries `internal_error` and `resource_unavailable` on the same run up to three times before it reports the run.

## Talking to a run

- `POST /runs/{id}/followups {message, attachments}` steers a live run, or continues a finished one in a new run with the same agent, branch and task.
- `POST /runs/{id}/interrupt` stops what the agent is doing; the run is `BLOCKED` until a follow-up.
- `GET /runs/{id}/timeline`, `/conversation` and `/transcript` show what happened; `/scores` its scores.
- `PUT /runs/{id}/sharing {publicAccess: "VIEWER" | "EDITOR" | null}` shares the run with signed-in people who cannot otherwise see the factory.
- Agents stay alive for follow-ups for `idleTimeoutMinutes` (default 10, 60 for subagents).

## Subagents and run tokens

A running agent gets `KILN_RUN_TOKEN` and the Kiln MCP server. With it, it may:

- read its own task and the runs of its task or run tree, message its task, and upload files;
- start subagents: `POST /runs/{id}/spawn` (MCP `spawn_agent`) or several at once with `run-agents` (`run_agents`). The child's `spawnableBy` decides who may start it; nesting stops at five levels;
- ask the requester a question (`POST /runs/{id}/questions`, MCP `ask_user`) with single- or multi-select options and a recommended option, and read the answer from the gate;
- propose a definition change (`propose_definition_change`) that people review in the inbox;
- call `complete_task`, which closes the task only after its pull request merged.

A run token cannot decide gates, write definitions, see other tasks or factories, merge or approve.

## Related pages

- [API reference](api.md)
- [Kiln MCP](mcp.md)
- [Inbox](../management/inbox.md)

# Build an incident-response factory

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/guides/incident-response-factory.md

This guide builds a factory, `@oncall`, that turns an alert or a Slack message into a tested fix on a pull request within minutes, while a person still decides what merges.

## What you will build

```text
alert webhook ─┐
               ├─> foreman ─> triage ─> fix ─> verify (CI + tests) ─> review ─> hand-off
@oncall Slack ─┘
```

No spec stage, because incidents need speed. People still approve risky commands and merge the fix.

## 1. The factory

```yaml
# factory.yaml
schemaVersion: kiln/v1
name: incident-response
alias: oncall
repositories:
  - { owner: acme, name: web }
integrations: [slack]
agentDefaults:
  harness: { type: claude-code, model: claude-sonnet-5-5 }
  runner: linux-node
defaultPipeline: incident
budgets: { perWorkItemUsd: 25 }
```

## 2. The agents

`agents/foreman/agent.md`:

```markdown
---
agentType: FOREMAN
description: Coordinates incident work
---
Keep the thread short and factual. Ask instead of guessing.
```

`agents/triage/agent.md`:

```markdown
---
agentType: TRIAGE
---
Classify the alert. Name the most likely cause from the runbooks skill and quote the evidence.
```

`agents/fixer/agent.md`:

```markdown
---
agentType: IMPLEMENT
description: Smallest safe fix with a regression test
---
Make the smallest change that stops the incident. Add a test that fails without the fix.
Do not refactor. Do not touch infrastructure or data.
```

`agents/verify/agent.md`:

```markdown
---
agentType: VERIFY
---
Run the test suite. Report testsPassed in the result file.
```

`agents/review/agent.md`:

```markdown
---
agentType: REVIEW
---
Check that the fix is minimal and the new test covers the failure.
Use needs_human for anything that touches auth, payments or data.
```

## 3. Runbooks as a skill

`skills/runbooks/SKILL.md`:

```markdown
---
name: runbooks
description: Known incident causes and how to confirm each one
owner: sre
---
## 502s from the API
Check the last deploy and the connection pool size in config/db.ts.

## Login loop
Check the session cookie domain in config/session.ts.
```

Every agent receives it. See [Skills](../configuration/skills.md).

## 4. The pipeline

```yaml
# pipelines/incident.yaml
description: Fast path for incidents, no spec
stages:
  - { id: triage, agent: triage }
  - { id: build,  agent: fixer }
  - { id: verify, agent: verify, requires: [ci_green, tests_pass], on_fail: build, max_loops: 2 }
  - { id: review, agent: review, on_fail: build, max_loops: 1 }
  - { id: handoff, action: handoff }
```

After two failed verify loops, Kiln opens a `verify-stuck` question in the thread and parks the item, so a person takes over. See [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md).

## 5. A runner with a closed network

```yaml
# runners/linux-node.yaml
backend: docker
shape: { vcpus: 2, memoryGb: 4 }
setupCommands:
  - corepack enable
  - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
egress:
  - registry.npmjs.org
  - llm-gateway.internal.acme.com
```

Only these hosts and the hosts of the cloned repositories, here `github.com`, are reachable. See [Sandboxes](../infrastructure/sandboxes.md).

## 6. A stricter command guard

Incidents tempt people to touch production. Block anything that looks like it:

```yaml
# decisions/command-guard.yaml
state: [command, cwd, repo, branch]
questions:
  risk_level: { type: choice, options: [safe, risky, destructive] }
  remote_exec: { type: probability }
  deletes_files: { type: probability }
  touches_prod: { type: probability }
policy:
  block: "risk_level.destructive >= 0.6 or remote_exec >= 0.6 or touches_prod >= 0.5"
  ask_human: "risk_level.risky >= 0.3 or deletes_files >= 0.5"
on_error: deny
timeout_ms: 800
```

With `on_error: deny`, an unanswered decision takes the first policy entry, `block`. See [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md).

```yaml
# policies/guard.yaml
protectedPaths: [decisions/**, pipelines/**]
```

## 7. Alerts and Slack

```yaml
# webhooks/alerts.yaml
authMode: signature
signatureScheme: standard_webhooks
secretName: ALERTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET
deliveryIdHeader: webhook-id
```

`automations/alerts/automation.md`:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: webhook
    event: received
    filter: { webhook_ids: [alerts] }
---
An alert fired. Find the cause, then fix it with a regression test.
```

`automations/slack/automation.md`:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: slack
    event: app_mention
    filter: { channel: [C0INCIDENTS] }
---
Treat this as an incident report.
```

Store `ALERTS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in Kiln and point your alerting tool at `POST /webhooks/oncall/alerts`. The alert's `title` or `summary` field becomes the work item's title. See [Automations](../configuration/automations.md#webhooks).

## One task per incident

An alarm usually arrives from more than one place: the alert webhook fires, then someone posts in Slack. Kiln keeps one task for the incident. Alerts that carry the same `fingerprint`, `dedup_key` or `incident_id` join the open task, and a Slack report that names the same service and error code joins it by content. Both threads then get the updates. Set `deduplication: { windowHours: 6 }` in `factory.yaml` to compare only recent tasks, or `enabled: false` to turn it off. See [Tasks and runs](../developer-tools/tasks-and-runs.md#dispatching-work).

## 8. Validate and apply

```bash
kiln validate .
kiln apply --dry-run
kiln apply
```

## 9. Try it

Mention the factory in the incidents channel:

```text
@oncall users get a login loop after the 14:02 deploy
```

Follow the thread. You should see a "Ready to merge" message with the pull request, which has the fix, the regression test and the `factory:oncall` label. If the fixer wants to run a risky command, an approval request appears in the inbox.

## 10. Measure it

Add a scorer for the fixer, and watch cycle time and cost per merged PR on the dashboard. See [Scorers](../measure-and-improve/scorers.md) and [Dashboard metrics](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md).

## Related pages

- [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)
- [Slack](../integrations/slack.md)
- [Make a factory improve itself](make-a-factory-improve-itself.md)

# Kiln builds Kiln

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/guides/kiln-builds-kiln.md

Kiln's own repository is worked on by a Kiln factory, `kiln-self`: issues labeled `kiln-ready` go to its foreman, the factory opens pull requests, and people review and merge them.

## How work arrives

Work for Kiln is filed as GitHub issues in the Kiln repository. Labeling an issue `kiln-ready` sends it to the `kiln-self` factory, which triages it, writes a spec when needed, builds it and opens a pull request. People still review and merge every pull request.

## The definition

The factory lives in `factories/kiln-self/`. Apply it with `kiln apply factories/kiln-self`.

```yaml
# factories/kiln-self/factory.yaml
schemaVersion: kiln/v1
name: Kiln
alias: kiln
project: kiln
repositories:
  - { owner: fishuke, name: kiln }
integrations: [github, linear]
agentDefaults:
  harness: { type: claude-code, model: router:by-task }
  runner: linux-node
selfImprovement: { failedRunThreshold: 10, reviewers: { type: admins } }
defaultPipeline: feature
budgets: { perWorkItemUsd: 30, monthlyUsd: 3000 }
```

| Part | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Agents | `foreman`, `triage`, `spec`, `implement`, `verify`, `review`, plus `planner` (`PLAN`), `po-assistant` (`PO_ASSISTANT`) and `improver` (`CUSTOM`) |
| `pipelines/feature.yaml` | Triage, spec (skipped for `xs` and `s`), build per user story, verify with CI and a video per criterion (up to 3 loops), preview, an advisory review whose findings are posted on the pull request, hand-off |
| `gates/` | Spec approval and preview acceptance by the requester or the `po` role, nudged after 24h, parked after 72h |
| `routers/by-task.yaml` | A complexity router: Haiku for easy, Sonnet for medium and by default, Opus for hard |
| `runners/linux-node.yaml` | Kiln's runner image on Docker, 4 vCPUs and 8 GB, `pnpm install`, egress to the npm registry, `github.com` and `api.github.com` |
| `skills/repository-conventions` | Named exports, zod at every boundary, one behavior per test |
| `decisions/command-guard.yaml` | The command guard with the standard thresholds |
| `automations/` | `ready` (GitHub `issue_labeled` with `kiln-ready`) and `review-comments` (review submitted on a fishuke/kiln pull request) |

The `ready` automation filters on `repos: [fishuke/kiln]`. GitHub events carry both `repo` and `repos`.

## The rules it works under

The agents follow the same rules that `CLAUDE.md` sets for people and Claude Code in this repository: one task per branch, failing tests first, pull requests under about 400 changed lines, `packages/*` never import `apps/*`, every external system behind an interface with a fake, and docs pages updated with each task.

Kiln enforces what agents can do on GitHub: run tokens push only `kiln/*` branches and cannot approve or merge. People merge.

## Protecting the checks

A factory that improves itself must not loosen the checks that review it. `policies/self-protection.yaml` lists:

```yaml
protectedPaths:
  - packages/definitions/src/validate*
  - apps/api/src/app.ts
  - packages/auth/**
  - policies/**
  - gates/**
  - packages/engine/src/gates.ts
  - packages/engine/src/state.ts
  - .github/workflows/**
  - factories/kiln-self/policies/**
twoApprovalPaths:
  - packages/definitions/**
  - packages/engine/src/improvement.ts
```

`policies/default.yaml` also protects `policies/**`, `gates/**` and `.github/workflows/**`, and needs two approvals for `decisions/**`.

What Kiln enforces from these today:

- Self-improvement drops any proposed change to a protected path and never changes `policies/` or `gates/`.
- A self-improvement change to a two-approval path needs two different people.
- Kiln never opens a self-improvement proposal without a replay report, and agents cannot approve proposals.

Self-improvement changes definition files. Code changes to `packages/` and `apps/` arrive as ordinary pull requests from work items, so the protected code paths there also need branch protection and code owners in the repository. Spending is capped at the lowest of `budgets.perWorkItemUsd` (30) and the policies' `maxUsdPerWorkItem` (40 and 30), so $30 per work item, and at `monthlyUsd` (3000) per month. The `deniedActions` keys are accepted but not enforced yet.

## Scorers

| Scorer | Grades | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `criteria` | `implement`, 25% of runs | Passes only when every acceptance criterion is covered. Feeds self-improvement. |
| `docs-drift` | `implement` and `review`, 25% of runs | Flags runs where a docs page led the agent astray, so self-improvement can propose a docs fix. |
| `meta` | `improver`, every run | Passes only when a self-improvement pull request has a "## Replay" section with a before and after table. |

With `failedRunThreshold: 10`, a proposal starts once an agent's unreviewed failures cover 10 runs, or the oldest is 7 days old.

## Measuring the share

Every pull request the factory opens carries the `factory:kiln` label. The share of merged Kiln pull requests with that label shows how much of Kiln is built by Kiln. The factory's [dashboard](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md) adds autonomy, cycle time and cost per merged PR.

## Related pages

- [Make a factory improve itself](make-a-factory-improve-itself.md)
- [Self-improvement](../measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md)
- [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md)
- [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [GitHub](../integrations/github.md)

# Make a factory improve itself

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/guides/make-a-factory-improve-itself.md

This guide sets up the full improvement loop for a factory: scorers flag failures, Kiln proposes a definition change, replays prove it, a person reviews it, and a canary confirms it.

## Before you start

- The factory's definition lives in a [config repo](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#config-repos-on-github), so proposals arrive as pull requests.
- The factory has done some real work, so there are runs to score.

## 1. Decide what "good" means

Write a scorer for the agent you want to improve. Make the labels concrete, and describe each one so the judge and your reviewers read them the same way.

```markdown
---
name: criteria
description: Does the change meet every acceptance criterion?
agents: [implement]
labels:
  - { value: meets, score: 1, description: Every criterion has a passing test }
  - { value: partly, score: 0.5, description: Some criteria have no test }
  - { value: misses, score: 0, description: The change does not do what was asked }
passingScore: 1
samplingRate: 25
model: claude-haiku-5-5
selfImprovement: true
---
Compare the acceptance criteria with the tests the run added or changed.
```

Save it as `scorers/criteria/scorer.md`. With `passingScore: 1`, only `meets` passes. See [Scorers](../measure-and-improve/scorers.md).

## 2. Set the thresholds

```yaml
# factory.yaml
selfImprovement:
  failedRunThreshold: 10
  maxAgeDays: 7
```

The check starts a proposal for an agent once its unreviewed failures cover 10 distinct runs, or the oldest is 7 days old. The default threshold is 25. A lower number gives you proposals sooner, with less evidence in each.

## 3. Put up guard rails

```yaml
# policies/guard.yaml
description: Self-improvement may tune agents, not the rules that check them
protectedPaths: [policies/**, gates/**, decisions/**, scorers/**]
twoApprovalPaths: [agents/review/**]
```

- Changes to `protectedPaths` are dropped from proposals. Kiln always drops `policies/` and `gates/`.
- Changes to `twoApprovalPaths` need two different people to approve.
- Protecting `scorers/**` stops the factory from making its own grading easier.

See [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md).

## 4. Validate and merge

Open a pull request in the config repo with the three changes. The [validation workflow](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#validate-pull-requests-with-github-actions) runs `kiln validate`. Merge it; the push applies the definition.

## 5. Let failures build up

Work as usual. About a quarter of the `implement` runs get a score. Check the agent's pass rate on the [dashboard](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md).

To try the loop without waiting, use **Run now** for the factory's self-improvement. It starts a proposal for every agent with at least one unreviewed failure.

## 6. Review the proposal

Kiln opens a pull request titled "Self-improvement: implement (instructions)" or similar. Read it in this order:

1. **Regressions addressed.** Each failed run, with its score and the judge's rationale. Do the failures look real?
2. **Replay.** The pass rate before and after, and a pass or fail per replayed run. A proposal that does not improve the after rate is a warning sign.
3. **Changes.** The changed files. By default, a "Lessons from reviewed failures" section in the agent's instructions.
4. **Dropped changes.** Any changes to protected paths that Kiln removed.

Then either:

- **Merge it.** If you merge it unchanged, the push applies it as a 10% canary and marks the proposal merged. If you edited the branch first, the push applies it to all new work items.
- **Approve it in Kiln instead.** Kiln applies it as a 10% canary without merging. This needs `definitions:write` on the factory. The pull request stays open; merging it later applies the change to everyone.
- **Reject it, with a reason.** The improver will not repeat a rejected lesson.

## 7. Watch the canary

Compare the candidate with the applied definition in the per-definition metrics. After 7 days, Kiln promotes the candidate if its pass rate is within 2 points of the applied one, and rolls it back otherwise. You can promote or roll back sooner. See [Replay and canary](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md).

## 8. Keep the loop honest

- Read a sample of passing runs now and then, to catch a judge that is too lenient.
- When a scorer's labels change, expect a wave of new failures. Raise `failedRunThreshold` for a while if needed.
- Benchmark before and after big changes to models or skills. See [Benchmarks](../measure-and-improve/benchmarks.md).

## Related pages

- [Self-improvement](../measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md)
- [Scorers](../measure-and-improve/scorers.md)
- [Replay and canary](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md)
- [Kiln builds Kiln](kiln-builds-kiln.md)

# Architecture and security

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md

Kiln is a control plane that receives events, decides what to do, and launches agents in disposable sandboxes; agents never run inside the control plane, and no agent identity can merge.

## Services

| Service | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `api` | REST API under `/api/v1`, webhook endpoints, token auth and scopes, work items, gates, projects, definition apply |
| `orchestrator` | Drives work items through stages, gates, retries, budgets, the self-improvement schedule and benchmarks |
| `runner` | Launches sandboxes, issues run tokens, streams run events, collects artifacts |
| `integrations` | Adapters for GitHub, Linear, Jira and Slack; posts results back to the source |
| `mcp` | The Kiln MCP server, over streamable HTTP, with scoped tokens |
| `web` | Dashboard, inbox, product-owner workspace, definition viewer, portfolio |
| `scorer` | Runs judges on sampled runs, writes scores, groups failures |

Every external system sits behind an interface with a fake for tests: forge, tracker, chat, preview provider, sandbox provider, harness and decision provider.

## Where data lives

- **Definitions live in Git** or in Kiln's definition store, keyed by definition SHA. Runtime state never goes into the definition tree.
- **Runtime state** (work items, runs, run events, gates, scores, proposals, decision logs, audit entries, secrets, tokens) lives in Kiln's database.
- **Artifacts** (Playwright videos and reports, sandbox snapshots) go to object storage.
- **Events** go through an event bus with an outbox, so integrations, the scorer and the web app see them in order.

## How a run is isolated

1. Kiln issues a run token for the run's repositories.
2. The runner creates a sandbox from the agent's runner file: image, CPU and memory, setup commands and egress allowlist. See [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md).
3. Kiln clones the repositories with the run token and checks out the work item's `kiln/*` branch.
4. The harness starts inside the sandbox with the instructions, skills and a Kiln MCP connection that uses the same run token.
5. When the run ends, Kiln reads `.kiln/result.json`. If the run succeeded and the stage changes code, Kiln commits leftovers and pushes the branch with the run token. Then it destroys the sandbox. A paused run keeps a snapshot instead.

## Security controls

### No agent can merge

- A run token can push only `kiln/*` branches, open pull requests, comment and add labels, on the repositories of its run. It cannot approve or merge, and it expires after 60 minutes.
- Kiln checks the token before it pushes. A refused push fails the run.
- Agents are told not to push, open pull requests or merge. Kiln does those steps.
- Branch protection on your forge is the final control: require reviews on `main`, and do not give Kiln's GitHub identity a bypass.
- A work item cannot reach `complete` without a merge event or a person's confirmation. This rule is enforced in the state machine and covered by a property test.

### Commands are checked

The [command guard](../configuration/decisions.md#command-guard) rates shell commands before they run and blocks destructive ones or asks a person about risky ones. Claude Code checks every Bash call through a hook. Codex and OpenCode rely on the sandbox for isolation.

### Network is closed by default

Traffic from a sandbox goes through Kiln's egress proxy, which allows only the hosts of the run's repositories and the runner's `egress` list. Everything else is unreachable. On Kubernetes, a NetworkPolicy allows only DNS and the proxy.

### Sandboxes are locked down

Docker sandboxes drop all capabilities and set `no-new-privileges`. Kubernetes sandboxes run under gVisor (`runtimeClassName: gvisor`) as user 1000 (non-root), with no service account token mounted, privilege escalation off, all capabilities dropped and the default seccomp profile.

### Tokens are scoped per factory

API and MCP tokens carry scopes such as `read`, `send`, `decide:spec`, `decide:preview` and `definitions:write`, each for one factory or `*`. A product owner's token can approve previews without touching definitions. Tokens are stored as hashes. See [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md).

### Webhooks are verified

GitHub, Slack and Linear webhooks are checked against their signing secrets, Slack requests older than five minutes are refused, and Jira calls must carry the configured token. Custom webhooks use a bearer token, a URL token or a signature. Repeated deliveries are ignored.

### The factory cannot weaken its own checks

Self-improvement cannot change `policies/` or `gates/`, drops changes to any `protectedPaths`, needs two people for `twoApprovalPaths`, and never opens a proposal without a replay report. Agents cannot approve proposals. See [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md).

### Content is not a source of permissions

Text in issues, tickets and Slack messages becomes the work item's request, never its permissions. What an agent may do comes from the definition, the run token and the gates. A reply in a thread or comment decides a gate only when its author is one of the gate's assignees, matched through the server's `identities` map.

### Everything is audited

Definition applies and rejections, gate decisions, steering, cancellations, pauses, proposals, canary changes, token issues and secret changes are written to the audit log with the actor.

## Design records

The decisions behind this architecture are written down as ADRs in `docs/adr/`:

- [0001 TypeScript monorepo](../../adr/0001-typescript-monorepo.md)
- [0002 Orchestration](../../adr/0002-orchestration.md)
- [0003 Definition format](../../adr/0003-definition-format.md)
- [0004 Harness adapters](../../adr/0004-harness-adapters.md)
- [0005 Storage](../../adr/0005-storage.md)
- [0006 Decision layer](../../adr/0006-decision-layer.md)
- [0007 Open source and bring your own keys](../../adr/0007-open-source-byok.md)
- [0008 Humans merge](../../adr/0008-humans-merge.md)

The [threat model](../../security/threat-model.md) lists the threats these controls answer.

## Data sent to model providers

Harnesses send the prompt, instructions, skills and the code they read to the model they use. Typed decisions send only the fields listed in each decision's `state`. Route model traffic through your own gateway if you need EU endpoints or zero data retention.

## Related pages

- [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md)
- [Harnesses](harnesses.md)
- [Self-hosting](self-hosting.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md)
- [Threat model](../../security/threat-model.md)
- [Architecture decision records](../../adr/README.md)

# Harnesses

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/harnesses.md

A harness is the coding agent program that does the work in a run; Kiln supports Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode behind one adapter interface and does not write its own agent loop.

## Choosing a harness

Set `harness.type` in `agentDefaults`, on an agent or on an automation:

```yaml
harness: { type: claude-code, model: claude-sonnet-5-5 }
```

| `type` | Program | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-code` | `claude` | The default when nothing sets a harness. |
| `codex` | `codex` | |
| `opencode` | `opencode` | The `oz` harness type becomes `opencode` on import. |
| `gemini` | `gemini` | Gemini CLI in headless mode (`--output-format stream-json`). Reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. |
| `pi` | `pi` | The Pi coding agent in JSON mode. Reads Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or Gemini keys. |

`reasoningLevel` takes `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max` where the harness supports it. `auth` also accepts the v1alpha1 spellings `managedSecret` (same as `secret`) and `workerEnvironment` (same as `worker`). Claude Code thinking is recorded as `reasoning` run events with how long the model thought.

The harness program must be installed in the runner's image. Pin its version in the image, because flags and output formats change between releases.

## How each harness runs

| | Claude Code | Codex | OpenCode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command | `claude --output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions`, driven by the Claude Agent SDK (see below) | `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox <instructions + prompt>` | `opencode run --format json <prompt>` |
| Model flag | `--model` | `-m` | `-m` |
| Instructions | Appended to the system prompt | Sent before the prompt | Written to `AGENTS.md` |
| Skills folder | `.claude/skills/` | `.agents/skills/` | `.opencode/skills/` |
| Kiln MCP | `.kiln/mcp.json`, passed with `--mcp-config` (never committed: it holds the run token) | Not configured | Not configured |
| Command guard | `PreToolUse` hook on Bash in `.kiln/claude-settings.json`, passed with `--settings` | Not installed | Not installed |
| Cost | Reported by Claude Code | Estimated from token counts | Reported per step |

Kiln drives Claude Code with the [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview). The SDK runs in Kiln (the API or the worker), and the `claude` binary it talks to runs inside the run's sandbox with the run's environment only, so sandboxes, the egress allowlist and workers behave as for the other harnesses. The SDK sends the instructions and steering messages over the session's input. Its version is pinned to the release paired with the Claude Code version in the runner image (SDK `0.3.290` with Claude Code `2.1.290`), so bump both together. See [ADR-009](https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-claude-agent-sdk.md).

## Credentials

Kiln passes model credentials to the harness as environment variables of the run, read from Kiln's secrets. You bring your own keys. Set them with `harness.auth`:

```yaml
harness:
  type: claude-code
  auth: { source: secret, secretName: CLAUDE_TOKEN }
```

| `auth` | What the run gets |
| --- | --- |
| `{ source: secret, secretName: <name> }` | A typed secret (such as `claude_oauth_token` or `anthropic_bedrock_access_key`) gives its provider variables. Otherwise, the secret's value. For Claude Code it is set as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` when it is a subscription token from `claude setup-token` (it starts with `sk-ant-oat`), and as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` otherwise. For Codex it is `OPENAI_API_KEY`. For OpenCode the variable has the secret's name. Add `env: <VARIABLE>` to choose the variable yourself. A missing secret fails the run. |
| `{ source: worker }` | No credential from Kiln. The harness uses credentials already present on the worker or in the image. |
| not set | Kiln looks for default secrets, including typed team and personal secrets and the team-managed model keys. Claude Code gets the first of `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and Bedrock credentials that is set. Codex gets a [ChatGPT login](#chatgpt-logins) when there is one, else the first of `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CODEX_API_KEY`. OpenCode gets every one of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` that is set. |

The agent's `secrets` list is passed the same way, one variable per secret. Credentials go only to that run's sandbox, and personal secrets only to runs their owner triggered. Secret values are redacted from run output. See [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](../management/secrets-mcps-environments.md).

## ChatGPT logins

Codex can run OpenAI models on a ChatGPT plan instead of an API key. Under **Team settings → Model keys**, choose **Sign in with ChatGPT**, give the login a name, then open the link Kiln shows and enter the one-time code. Kiln runs `codex login --device-auth` in a throwaway sandbox for this and stores the resulting `auth.json` as a `chatgpt_auth` secret. Admins sign in for the team; anyone can sign in for their own runs only. A sign-in in progress is visible only to whoever started it and to team admins, because whoever enters its code chooses the account. A personal login shadows a team login of the same name. If your ChatGPT workspace is a Business or Enterprise one, an admin may first need to allow device code login in its settings.

| What | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| Which runs use it | Codex runs on a Kiln sandbox (not self-hosted workers) whose agent sets no `auth`. With several logins, each run gets the working one with the most left; your own come before the team's. |
| Where it lives in the run | `auth.json` in a `CODEX_HOME` under `/tmp`, outside the repositories, so it is never committed. Its tokens are redacted from run output. |
| Refreshes | Codex refreshes a login it has not refreshed for about 8 days and rewrites `auth.json`; the old refresh token then stops working. Kiln saves the refreshed file after every run (the audit log shows `chatgpt.refreshed` by the run). A login that is due for a refresh serves one run at a time; other runs wait and retry. Tokens a refresh produces mid-run are redacted from its output too. |
| Usage limits | When the plan's limit is reached, the login shows as limited until the time Codex reports and runs use another one. |
| Signed out | A login OpenAI rejects shows as invalid. Sign in again with the same name to replace it. |

To use ChatGPT logins, add `auth.openai.com` and `chatgpt.com` to `KILN_EGRESS_ALLOW` (they are not in the default list, because the list applies to every sandbox). Without them, sign-in fails with Codex's connection error.

A ChatGPT login is a whole ChatGPT session, not an inference-only key, and the agent in a run can read it. Use a dedicated ChatGPT account for team logins, use them for your own private work within OpenAI's terms, and prefer API keys for shared automation, as the Codex docs do. Kiln keeps the `auth.json` a run leaves behind only when it is a refresh of the same account (same account id, a new refresh token, a later refresh time), so an agent cannot swap the stored login for another account. See the [threat model](../../security/threat-model.md).

## Isolation

The sandbox is the security boundary for all three. Permission prompts are off because nobody is there to answer them; the [command guard](../configuration/decisions.md#command-guard) and the sandbox take their place.

## What a run receives

- **Instructions:** the agent's Markdown body, matching factory memories, any extra instructions, and a "Reporting back to Kiln" section.
- **Prompt:** the work item's title, body, triage result, acceptance criteria, review findings and messages from people, plus a line telling the agent what this stage needs.
- **Skills:** every shared skill plus the agent's own.
- **Environment:** `KILN_RUN_ID`, `KILN_RUN_TOKEN`, `KILN_FACTORY`, `KILN_AGENT_TYPE`, `KILN_WORK_ITEM` and `KILN_STAGE`.
- **Working directory:** the work item's repository (the one triage picked in a factory with several, else the first), checked out on the work item's `kiln/*` branch. When triage picked a repository, only it and any `required_repos` are cloned; otherwise all non-deferred repositories are cloned side by side.

## The result file

Agents report structured results by writing `.kiln/result.json` in the repository root. Kiln excludes `.kiln/` from git, so the file is never committed. Kiln reads it after the run; if the JSON does not parse, the run records an error event.

| `agentType` | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `TRIAGE` | `{"kind": "feature\|bug\|chore\|incident\|question", "size": "xs\|s\|m\|l\|xl", "summary": "...", "duplicateOf": "optional issue key"}` |
| `FOREMAN` | `{"dispatch": {"stage": "triage\|spec\|build\|review\|handoff", "agent": "name", "context": "..."}}` or `{"ask": "question for the requester"}` |
| `SPEC` | `{"specPath": "docs/specs/<id>.md", "why": "...", "goal": "...", "approach": "...", "criteria": ["AC1: ..."], "stories": ["..."], "outOfScope": ["..."], "risks": ["..."], "openQuestions": ["..."]}` |
| `IMPLEMENT` | `{"summary": "...", "testsPassed": true, "memories": [{"title": "...", "body": "..."}]}` |
| `VERIFY` | `{"testsPassed": true, "playwrightReport": "playwright-report/results.json"}` |
| `REVIEW` | `{"verdict": "accepted\|changes_requested\|needs_human", "findings": ["file:line — issue — fix"]}` |
| `PLAN` | `{"epics": [{"title": "...", "milestone": "...", "dependsOn": [], "issues": [{"title": "...", "body": "...", "criteria": ["..."], "factory": "alias"}]}]}` |
| Others | `{"summary": "..."}` |

What Kiln does with it:

- A review verdict of `changes_requested` with findings loops back to build. `needs_human` posts the findings on the pull request for a person.
- A spec without `specPath` is recorded as `docs/specs/<work item id>.md`.
- `memories` from any agent become memory proposals.
- `testsPassed` is checked when a pipeline stage requires `tests_pass`.

The agent commits on the current branch. It must not push, open pull requests or merge; Kiln does that with a scoped token.

## Run events

Kiln streams each harness's output as normalized events: `message`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `steer`, `error`, plus Kiln's own `started`, `guard`, `pushed`, `resumed` and `finished`. Events are stored in order, can be read after the fact, and can be followed live over server-sent events.

## Steering

Steering sends a message to a running agent.

| Harness | How the message arrives |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Written to the session's input as a new user message, so the agent reads it before its next step. |
| Codex | Queued. When the current turn ends, Kiln resumes the session (`codex exec resume --last`) with the message. |
| OpenCode | Queued. When the current turn ends, Kiln continues the session (`opencode run --continue`) with the message. |

You can steer from the run page, the task page, the API, the Kiln MCP, or by replying where the work started: a Slack thread, a Linear or Jira issue, or a GitHub issue or pull request. A reply steers the running agent when it does not decide a gate or answer an open question. When no agent is running, the reply is added to the conversation instead, and the next agent run sees it under "Messages from people".

On the task page, the running agent's activity (messages, commands, tool calls and thinking) appears live under its row, and the message box steers that agent while it works; when nothing is running, the message goes to the foreman.

Each steering message is kept on the run record, counted as a human touch on the work item, and written to the audit log. A resumed run gets the steering messages so far. Steering a run that has finished fails.

## Related pages

- [Factory agents](../configuration/agents.md)
- [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md)
- [Skills](../configuration/skills.md)
- [Replay and canary](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md)
- [API overview](../developer-tools/api.md)

# Sandboxes

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/sandboxes.md

Every agent run gets a fresh sandbox built from its runner file, and Kiln destroys the sandbox when the run ends.

## Runner files

```yaml
# runners/linux-node.yaml
description: Node 22 with pnpm
backend: docker
shape: { vcpus: 4, memoryGb: 8 }
setupCommands:
  - corepack enable
  - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
egress:
  - github.com
  - registry.npmjs.org
```

| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | Kiln's runner image | The container image. Docker pulls it if it is not cached. Without one, runs use the server's runner image (`KILN_RUNNER_IMAGE`), which has the agent CLIs. An image you name must have the harness CLI (`claude`, `codex` or `opencode`) on its `PATH`. |
| `backend` | `docker` | `docker`, `kubernetes` or `local`. |
| `shape` | none | `vcpus` and `memoryGb`. Sets CPU and memory limits. |
| `setupCommands` | `[]` | Run in order after the repositories are cloned, inside each repository (so `pnpm install` finds its `package.json` and the `packageManager` pin). A failing command fails the run. Kiln's runner image has a corepack that runs pnpm 11 and later. |
| `egress` | `[]` | Extra host names the sandbox may reach, such as package registries and your model gateway. The hosts of the repositories it clones are always allowed. |
| `platform.linux.registryCredentialSecretName` | none | A team `docker_registry` or `aws_ecr` secret for a private image. See [Private images](../management/secrets-mcps-environments.md#private-images). |
| `description` | none | |

An agent picks a runner with `runner: <name>`, usually inherited from `agentDefaults`. An agent without a runner uses the server's runner image on the server's default backend, which is `local` unless the server sets another. A run's image is the runner's own, else its [environment](../management/secrets-mcps-environments.md)'s, else `KILN_RUNNER_IMAGE`, else `node:22-bookworm`.

## Backends

### Local

The workspace is a temporary directory on the Kiln host. It runs setup commands and the command guard, but it cannot enforce egress, CPU or memory limits. Use it for development and tests only.

### Docker

Each run is a container started with `sleep infinity` and `/workspace` as its working directory:

- labels `kiln.sandbox=1`, `kiln.dev/run` and `kiln.dev/factory`,
- `--cpus` and `--memory` from `shape`,
- `--security-opt no-new-privileges` and `--cap-drop ALL`,
- the `kiln-egress` network with `HTTPS_PROXY` and `HTTP_PROXY` set to `http://kiln-egress-proxy:3128` (and `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, so Node's `fetch`, which corepack uses to download pnpm, goes through the proxy too) and `KILN_EGRESS_ALLOW` set to the allowed hosts: the runner's `egress` list plus the hosts of the cloned repositories. With no hosts at all, the container gets `--network none`.

### Kubernetes with gVisor

Each run is a pod in the `kiln-sandboxes` namespace, plus a NetworkPolicy for that pod:

- `runtimeClassName: gvisor`, so the pod runs in gVisor's user-space kernel,
- `runAsNonRoot` as user 1000, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped,
- no service account token mounted, `restartPolicy: Never`,
- requests and limits from `shape`,
- an `emptyDir` volume at `/workspace`.

The NetworkPolicy blocks all ingress. When there are no allowed hosts at all, it blocks all egress too. Otherwise it allows only DNS (UDP 53 to `kube-dns`) and TCP 3128 to the pod labeled `app.kubernetes.io/name: kiln-egress-proxy`, which enforces the host list.

Kiln waits up to 120 seconds for the pod to be ready. Your cluster needs a `gvisor` RuntimeClass and the egress proxy deployed.

## Egress

Agents need the network to clone, install packages and call model APIs. Kiln keeps that surface small:

- The hosts of the repositories the run clones, such as `github.com`, are always allowed.
- List every other host the run needs in `egress`, such as `registry.npmjs.org`. Nothing else is reachable.
- The proxy enforces host names, so you do not have to track IP addresses.
- Keep model traffic going to your model gateway, and list only the gateway.

## What Kiln does in the sandbox

Kiln runs its own commands as trusted, so the command guard does not check them:

- configure git as `kiln-agent[bot]` and exclude `.kiln/` from git,
- check out the work item's branch, or the pinned commit for replays and benchmarks,
- write skills and harness settings,
- after the run, commit leftovers and push the branch with the run token.

Commands the agent runs through the sandbox's command API pass the [command guard](../configuration/decisions.md#command-guard).

## Pause and resume

A running agent can be paused, for example while it waits at a gate, and resumed later on any node.

- **Pause** packs `/workspace` into a `.tgz` archive, stores it in object storage under `snapshots/<sandbox>/<time>.tgz`, and stops the agent. The run's status becomes `paused` and the sandbox is kept until it resumes.
- **Resume** starts a new sandbox from the same runner, possibly on another node or backend, unpacks the snapshot into `/workspace`, and starts the harness again with the original request and any steering messages so far.
- The run records the workspace hash at pause and at resume, so you can check the workspace is the same.

Snapshots hold files only. On Docker, the server can also be set to take a CRIU checkpoint that keeps processes; the snapshot records whether it did. Kubernetes snapshots never keep processes.

## Related pages

- [Harnesses](harnesses.md)
- [Architecture and security](architecture-and-security.md)
- [Self-hosting](self-hosting.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)

# Self-hosted workers

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/self-hosted-workers.md

A self-hosted worker runs agent runs on a machine you choose (a build server, a GPU box, a host inside a private network) while the Kiln server keeps coordinating the work. The worker connects out to the Kiln API; it needs no inbound ports.

## How it works

1. An agent (or automation, or `agentDefaults`) sets `workerHost: <id>`.
2. When that agent runs, the Kiln server prepares the run (prompt, instructions, skills, scoped run token) and queues it for the worker id. The run's state is `QUEUED`.
3. A `kiln worker --worker-id <id>` process long-polls the API, claims the run (`CLAIMED`), creates its sandbox (Docker, Kubernetes or a host directory), clones the repositories with the run token, starts the harness and streams events back (`INPROGRESS`).
4. At the end it reports the result, uploads artifacts from `.kiln/artifacts/` and pushes the `kiln/*` branch with the run token. The server records everything as for any other run.

Several processes can share one worker id; each run goes to the process with the most free capacity. Runs wait in the queue while no worker of that id is connected and fail with `infrastructure_timeout` after 30 minutes. A worker that stops sending heartbeats is dropped and its runs are retried.

## Start a worker

Create a key with the `worker` scope (a worker API key, or `kiln token create --grants worker:*`), then:

```bash
KILN_URL=https://kiln.example.com KILN_WORKER_KEY=kiln_tok_… \
  pnpm kiln worker --worker-id build-farm --backend docker --max-concurrent-tasks 4
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--worker-id` | (required) | The id agents name in `workerHost`. Letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; ids starting with `kiln` are reserved. |
| `--api-key` | `KILN_WORKER_KEY`, else `KILN_TOKEN` | The worker key. |
| `--backend` | `docker` | `docker` (a container per run), `kubernetes` (a pod per run) or `direct` (a directory on the host). |
| `--max-concurrent-tasks` | `0` (unlimited) | Runs at once. |
| `--one-shot` | off | Take one run, then exit (direct backend only). For CI jobs and ephemeral VMs. |
| `--idle-on-complete` | `45m` | How long a one-shot worker stays up after its run. |
| `-v`, `--volumes` | | `HOST:CONTAINER[:ro|rw]` mounts for Docker sandboxes. Repeatable. |
| `-e`, `--env` | | `KEY=VALUE` (or `KEY` to pass the worker's own value) added to every run. Repeatable. |
| `--config-file` | | A YAML or JSON file with the same settings (below). |
| `--no-cleanup` | off | Keep sandboxes after runs, for debugging. |
| `--metrics-port` | | Serve Prometheus metrics on this port at `/metrics`. |
| `--log-level` | `info` | `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. |

### Config file

```yaml
worker_id: build-farm
max_concurrent_tasks: 4
idle_on_complete: 10m
cleanup: true
metrics_port: 9464
backend:
  docker:
    volumes: [/var/cache/npm:/root/.npm]
    image_pull_policy: IfNotPresent   # Always | IfNotPresent | Never
    environment:
      - { name: NPM_TOKEN }             # inherit from the worker's environment
      - { name: CI, value: "true" }
```

The `kubernetes` backend takes `namespace`; the `direct` backend takes `workspace_root`.

## Route agents to a worker

```yaml
# agents/implement/agent.md
---
agentType: IMPLEMENT
workerHost: build-farm
harness:
  type: claude-code
  auth: { source: worker }   # use the credentials already on the worker
---
```

`workerHost` follows the usual inheritance: set it in `agentDefaults` to send every agent, override it per agent or automation, and set it to `""` or `null` to run on the Kiln server again. With `auth: { source: worker }` (or the v1alpha1 spelling `workerEnvironment`) the harness uses the credentials on the worker and Kiln sends none; otherwise Kiln sends the run's harness credential and the agent's secrets with the job.

## Watch workers

- `GET /api/v1/workers` (and `client.workers()`) lists connected processes with their last heartbeat, active runs, and the queue.
- The API's `/metrics` endpoint includes `kiln_workers_connected`, `kiln_worker_runs_active` and `kiln_worker_queue_depth`. Set `KILN_METRICS_TOKEN` to require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- A worker's own `/metrics` (with `--metrics-port`) has `kiln_worker_connected`, `kiln_worker_tasks_active`, `kiln_worker_tasks_max_concurrent`, `kiln_worker_tasks_claimed_total`, `kiln_worker_tasks_completed_total{result}`, `kiln_worker_task_duration_seconds_sum{result}`, `kiln_worker_reconnects_total` and `kiln_worker_info`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Runs stay `QUEUED` | Is a worker with exactly that id connected (`GET /api/v1/workers`)? Ids are case-sensitive. Is it at `--max-concurrent-tasks`? |
| The worker gets 403 | The key needs the `worker` scope or must be a worker key. |
| Runs fail with `environment_setup_failed` | The sandbox could not start or clone: check Docker on the worker, the image, and that the worker can reach the forge. |
| Every shell command is blocked | The worker could not reach `/api/v1/guard`; it blocks commands when the guard is unreachable. |

## Related pages

- [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md)
- [Harnesses](harnesses.md)
- [Agents](../configuration/agents.md)
- [Self-hosting](self-hosting.md)
