# Self-hosting

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/self-hosting.md

Kiln runs on your own infrastructure: a single host with Docker for small installs, or a Kubernetes cluster with gVisor for production.

## Requirements

| Component                                          | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node 22 and pnpm 10                                | Kiln's services are TypeScript on Node.                                                                                                                                 |
| A data directory (a volume)                        | Runtime state (work items, runs, gates, scores, tokens, audit log) in `kiln.json`, and objects (videos, reports, snapshots) under `objects/`. Back it up by copying it. |
| Docker, or Kubernetes with a `gvisor` RuntimeClass | Sandboxes for agent runs. Without either, runs use host directories (development only).                                                                                 |
| An egress proxy                                    | Enforces each runner's `egress` host list. Included in `docker-compose.yml` and the Helm chart. See [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md#egress).                                   |
| Optional: an OpenAI-compatible gateway (LiteLLM)   | The LLM fallback for typed decisions and judges.                                                                                                                        |

Postgres, Temporal, NATS and S3 are not required in v1; see ADR-002 and ADR-005 for why and for the path to them.

## Install

### Try it locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fishuke/kiln && cd kiln
pnpm install
pnpm dev            # API on :4000 with demo data, web app on :3000
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Demo factories run on a git-backed local forge with scripted agents, so nothing needs an account.

### One machine with Docker Compose

```bash
cp .env.example .env          # add your keys: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from `claude setup-token`, or API keys
echo KILN_AGENTS=real >> .env  # run Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode instead of scripted agents
docker build -t kiln-runner-node runners/images/node
docker compose up -d --build
pnpm health
```

The API prints a bootstrap admin token on first start (also in the data volume as `admin-token`). Put it in `.env` as `KILN_TOKEN` so the web app can call the API, then restart `web`.

Then create your account: the first signup (`POST /api/v1/auth/signup`) becomes the owner of the default team, and existing factories move into that team. Invite everyone else. See [Teams and users](../management/teams-and-users.md).

### A server: Coolify or any Docker host

`docker-compose.prod.yml` runs Kiln on a public URL with sign-in: the API, the web app, the sandbox image (built on the server), the egress proxy, and an optional Caddy for HTTPS. Demo data and dev auth are off, agents are real, and runs use Docker sandboxes through the host's Docker socket. That socket is root on the host, so give Kiln a server of its own.

Set these variables:

| Variable                                      | Value                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KILN_WEB_URL`                                | The web app's URL, for example `https://kiln.example.com`.                                                       |
| `KILN_PUBLIC_URL`                             | The API's URL, for example `https://api.kiln.example.com`. Webhooks from GitHub, Slack and the rest arrive here. |
| `KILN_OWNER_EMAIL`                            | Your email. Only this address can create the first account, which owns the server.                               |
| `KILN_SECRET_KEY`                             | A long random value (`openssl rand -hex 32`). It signs run tokens; keep it stable.                               |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`                     | From `claude setup-token`, or set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.                 |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` and the other integration keys | Optional; see [Connect your systems](#connect-your-systems).                                                     |

**Coolify.** Add a resource of type Docker Compose from this repository, with `docker-compose.prod.yml` as the compose file. Give the `web` service your web domain (port 3000) and the `api` service the API domain (port 4000), fill in the variables Coolify lists, and deploy. Coolify's proxy serves HTTPS, so leave the `proxy` profile off.

**Any other Docker host.** Point both domains at the server, then:

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # set the variables above
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --profile proxy up -d --build
```

Caddy gets certificates for both domains. Open the web URL and sign up with `KILN_OWNER_EMAIL`, then invite everyone else.

Sandboxes join the internal network `kiln-egress` and reach the internet only through the proxy. If your platform renames networks, set `KILN_EGRESS_NETWORK` to the name it uses. `KILN_RUNNER_IMAGE` picks another sandbox image; it needs git and the harness CLIs, like `runners/images/node`.

### Kubernetes with Helm

```bash
kubectl create secret generic kiln-env --from-env-file=.env
helm install kiln deploy/helm/kiln \
  --set publicUrl=https://kiln.example.com --set webUrl=https://kiln.example.com \
  --set ingress.host=kiln.example.com
```

The chart creates the `kiln-sandboxes` namespace with the restricted pod security level, a `gvisor` RuntimeClass (handler `runsc`, which your nodes must provide), the egress proxy, a default-deny NetworkPolicy, and a Role that lets the API create sandbox pods there.

### First factory

```bash
pnpm kiln init my-factory --template sdlc
# edit my-factory/factory.yaml: repositories, alias, integrations
pnpm kiln validate my-factory
KILN_URL=http://localhost:4000 KILN_TOKEN=... pnpm kiln apply my-factory
pnpm kiln send "Fix the typo in the README" --factory <alias>
```

Or push the folder to a GitHub repo and connect it under Create factory; merges to its default branch then apply automatically.

## Connect your systems

### Public URLs

Kiln needs two URLs:

- **Public URL:** where agents in sandboxes reach the API. Kiln uses it for the Claude Code command-guard hook (`/api/v1/guard`) and the Kiln MCP (`/mcp`). Without it, neither is installed in runs.
- **Web URL:** where people open links. Kiln uses it in the links it posts, such as `<web URL>/inbox/<gate>` and `<web URL>/runs/<work item>`.

### Webhooks and secrets

Point each provider's webhooks at Kiln and set the matching secret. For the provider endpoints, Kiln reads the server environment variable with the secret's name (for example `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) first, then its secrets store, then `KILN_SECRET_<NAME>`, then the provider's [connection](../integrations/connections.md). A custom webhook's secret comes from the secrets store or `KILN_SECRET_<secretName>`.

| Provider        | Endpoint                                                   | Secret                                       |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| GitHub          | `POST /webhooks/github`                                    | `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`                      |
| GitLab          | `POST /webhooks/gitlab`                                    | `GITLAB_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` (`X-Gitlab-Token`)    |
| Azure DevOps    | `POST /webhooks/azure-devops`                              | `AZURE_DEVOPS_WEBHOOK_PASSWORD` (basic auth) |
| Bitbucket       | `POST /webhooks/bitbucket`                                 | `BITBUCKET_WEBHOOK_SECRET`                   |
| Slack           | `POST /webhooks/slack`                                     | `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`                       |
| Microsoft Teams | `POST /webhooks/teams`                                     | Bot Framework token for `TEAMS_APP_ID`       |
| Discord         | `POST /webhooks/discord`                                   | Ed25519 with `DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY`            |
| Discord bridge  | `POST /webhooks/discord/events`                            | `DISCORD_EVENTS_TOKEN` (bearer)              |
| Linear          | `POST /webhooks/linear`                                    | `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET`                      |
| Jira            | `POST /webhooks/jira?token=<token>`                        | `JIRA_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`                         |
| Custom          | `POST /webhooks/w/<uid>` (or `/webhooks/<factory>/<name>`) | The webhook's secret                         |

GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket, Teams and Discord refuse every call until their secret is set. For GitHub, Slack, Linear and Jira, Kiln accepts webhooks without checking signatures when the secret is not set. Set every secret before you expose Kiln to the internet.

OAuth providers redirect to `GET /oauth/<provider>/callback` on the public URL; register that URL in each OAuth app. Every provider's variables are listed on [Connections](../integrations/connections.md#environment-variables).

Admins can set secrets through the API; values are never returned, only names. See the [API overview](../developer-tools/api.md).

### Model credentials

Runs use your own model keys. Store `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (a Claude subscription token from `claude setup-token`) or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for Claude Code, a ChatGPT login (Sign in with ChatGPT under Team settings), `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY` for Codex, and the keys OpenCode's providers need. You can store them as Kiln secrets or set them as plain environment variables on the server. Agents can also name their own secret with `harness.auth`. See [Harnesses](harnesses.md#credentials).

### Accounts and login

| Variable                                   | What it does                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KILN_OPEN_SIGNUP=1`                       | Anyone may sign up and join the default team. Otherwise, after the first owner, signup needs an invite.                                                                    |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | Turn on GitHub login. The OAuth app's callback URL is `<KILN_PUBLIC_URL>/api/v1/auth/github/callback`. `GITHUB_OAUTH_URL` and `GITHUB_API_URL` point at GitHub Enterprise. |
| `KILN_SECRET_KEY`                          | Seals team and personal secrets with AES-256-GCM, and signs run tokens. Set it, and keep it stable across restarts.                                                        |
| `KILN_ADMIN_EMAILS`                        | Comma-separated emails of server admins. They see every team's audit log, tokens and server secrets. Team owners and admins see only their own team.                       |
| `KILN_SMTP_URL`, `KILN_MAIL_FROM`          | Email notifications, for example `smtp://user:pass@mail.acme.test:587?from=kiln@acme.test`.                                                                                |
| `KILN_DEV_AUTH=1`                          | Local development only: requests without a token act as `dev@kiln.local`, owner of the default team.                                                                       |

### Identities

Gate assignees are people, such as `po@acme.test`. To let replies in Slack or on issues decide gates, people link their Slack, GitHub, Linear, Jira, Discord, Teams, GitLab or Azure DevOps accounts in user settings. See [Linked accounts](../management/teams-and-users.md#linked-accounts). The server option `identities` still works as a fallback. It is keyed by `<provider>:<user>`, for example `slack:U024BE7LH` → `po@acme.test`. See [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).

### Roles

Gates name approvers by role, such as `role:po` or `role:code-owners`. Kiln's server configuration maps each role to people. Kiln uses these roles:

| Role          | Used by                                        |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `po`          | Built-in spec and preview gates                |
| `code-owners` | The built-in merge gate, and high-risk reviews |
| `admins`      | Command approvals for runs without a requester |

### Sandboxes

- **Docker:** create the `kiln-egress` network and run the egress proxy on it as `kiln-egress-proxy`, listening on port 3128.
- **Kubernetes:** create the `kiln-sandboxes` namespace, install gVisor with a RuntimeClass named `gvisor`, and deploy the egress proxy with the label `app.kubernetes.io/name: kiln-egress-proxy` on port 3128.
- Build runner images with the harness programs (`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`), git and your toolchain installed.

### Cloud identity federation

When a factory sets `cloudProviders` in `factory.yaml`, its runs get the federation settings as environment variables and exchange their own identity token for short-lived cloud credentials. Kiln never holds long-lived cloud keys. See [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#cloud-identity-federation).

### Forge identity

Kiln talks to GitHub as a GitHub App (`GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`), minting a short-lived installation token for each call, or with a plain `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitLab, Azure DevOps and Bitbucket use the tokens on their pages. It needs to read repositories, push `kiln/*` branches, open and update pull requests, comment, add labels and read check runs. Do not give it a branch-protection bypass. Agents never see this token; each run gets its own short-lived run token instead.

## Timers

Kiln runs a timer pass that:

- sends gate nudges and applies gate expiry,
- fires due schedules,
- retries verify stages that wait for CI,
- promotes or rolls back canaries after 7 days,
- when self-improvement checks are switched on for the pass, runs the check for every factory.

## Monitoring

- `GET /api/v1/health` returns `ok`, the number of factories and the server time.
- Each run records a trace ID, so you can match its events with your logs and traces.
- The audit log lists who applied definitions, decided gates, steered runs, issued tokens and set secrets.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                                 | Check                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A definition push did not apply                         | The factory's last error shows the first validation error. Run `kiln validate`.                                                                |
| An automation never fires                               | The trigger's `provider` and `event` match the event name exactly, and every filter key matches (GitHub events carry both `repo` and `repos`). |
| A work item is `blocked`                                | Its blocked reason says why: an expired gate, a stage that failed too often, the budget, or an error. Answer the open question to resume.      |
| A run fails at install                                  | The runner's `egress` list is missing a package registry or another host the run needs. Repository hosts are always allowed.                   |
| Verify waits forever                                    | CI checks on the branch are still pending. Kiln checks again on each timer pass.                                                               |
| Every command is blocked                                | The Claude Code hook cannot reach the public URL, so it blocks by design.                                                                      |
| Webhooks return 401                                     | The secret in Kiln does not match the provider's, or (Teams, Discord, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket) it is not set.                          |
| An automation with `teams` or `channels` fails to apply | The names did not resolve. Connect the provider, or set its directory. See [Connections](../integrations/connections.md#alias-directory).      |

## OpenTelemetry

Set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (OTLP over HTTP, for example `https://otel.example.com`) and Kiln sends traces, metrics and logs there. `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` carries the collector's auth. Works with SigNoz, Grafana, Honeycomb and any OTLP collector; nothing is sent when the endpoint is unset.

| Service             | What it sends                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kiln-api`          | HTTP requests, outgoing calls (GitHub, model providers, webhooks), host metrics and every console line. `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` changes the name.                         |
| `kiln-api` (engine) | One trace per task: a span for each stage and each agent run, with the run's status, cost and failure reason. Every run event (messages, tool calls, errors, guard verdicts) is a log record on its run's span. Other events (gates, pull requests, decisions) are log records in the task's trace. |
| `kiln-web`          | Next.js routes and rendering, its calls to the API (which continue in the API's traces), metrics and console lines.                                                  |
| `kiln-egress-proxy` | Every request a sandbox made, allowed or denied, as a log record. A denied host is a warning.                                                                       |

Run event text is redacted the same way as in the run view. The proxy sends its log to the API over UDP (port `KILN_EGRESS_LOG_PORT`, default 5140); `docker-compose.prod.yml` wires this up when the endpoint is set.

## Workers and monitoring

Agents can also run on machines you choose, such as a build server or a host in a private network: start `kiln worker` there and set `workerHost` on the agent. See [Self-hosted workers](self-hosted-workers.md). The API serves Prometheus metrics at `/metrics` (runs by state, tasks, open gates, workers and the worker queue); set `KILN_METRICS_TOKEN` to require a bearer token.

- [Self-hosted workers](self-hosted-workers.md)
- [Architecture and security](architecture-and-security.md)
- [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md)
- [Harnesses](harnesses.md)
- [GitHub](../integrations/github.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md)

# Azure DevOps

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/azure-devops.md

Azure DevOps Services (`dev.azure.com`) works as a forge for Azure Repos and as a source of work from pull requests and Boards work items.

## Set up

1. Create an identity for the factory: a service principal with Basic access, or a user. Give it Contribute on the repositories the factory works on.
2. Create a personal access token for it with Code (read and write), Work items (read and write) and Pull request threads. Set `AZURE_DEVOPS_ORG` to your organization and `AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN` to the token.
3. In Project settings → Service hooks, add Web Hooks subscriptions to `POST /webhooks/azure-devops` for: pull request created, updated, merged and commented on; code pushed; work item created, updated and commented on. Use basic authentication with any user name and a password you choose, and set that password as `AZURE_DEVOPS_WEBHOOK_PASSWORD`. To check the user name too, set `AZURE_DEVOPS_WEBHOOK_USER`.
4. Set `AZURE_DEVOPS_IDENTITIES` (comma-separated) to the factory identity's display name, email or ID. Mentions of and assignments to these identities start work.
5. List the repositories in `factory.yaml` with `forge: azure_devops`. `owner` is the project:

```yaml
repositories:
  - { forge: azure_devops, owner: Shop, name: api }
```

You can also connect Azure DevOps from the API with the organization, token and identity; see [Connections](connections.md).

## Starting work

| Event | Fires when | Filters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pull_request_created` | A pull request is created. | `base_branches`, `repos`, `source_repos` |
| `pull_request_updated` | A pull request is updated. | the same |
| `pull_request_merged` | A pull request completes. | the same |
| `pull_request_closed` | A pull request is abandoned. | the same |
| `pull_request_commented` | Someone comments on a pull request. | the same |
| `pull_request_mentioned` | A comment mentions the factory identity. | `mentioned`, `repos` |
| `push` | Code is pushed. | `branches`, `repos` |
| `work_item_created` | A work item is created. | `assignees`, `authors`, `labels`, `work_item_types` |
| `work_item_assigned` | A work item is assigned (or created assigned) to someone. | the same |
| `work_item_labeled` | A work item's tags change. | the same |
| `work_item_mentioned` | A work item comment mentions the factory identity. | `mentioned` |

`repos` are `project/repo`. Tags are the work item's `labels`. See [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md).

The default templates cover pull request mentions, work item mentions and work item assignment:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: azure_devops
    event: work_item_assigned
    filter: { work_item_types: [Bug] }
---
Fix the assigned bug.
```

If mention autocomplete does not offer the factory identity, assign it to a work item once.

## What Kiln does in Azure DevOps

- Opens pull requests from `kiln/*` branches (as drafts until ready) with labels, and comments in new threads.
- Reads commit statuses for CI.
- Creates and reads work items for the forge's issue features.
- A completed pull request completes its work item. Kiln never completes or approves pull requests.

Azure DevOps Server is not supported directly; clone it with runner setup commands instead.

## Related pages

- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [GitHub](github.md)

# Bitbucket

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/bitbucket.md

Bitbucket Cloud works as a forge (branches, pull requests, comments) and can start work from pull request events.

## Set up

1. Create a workspace or repository access token with Repositories: write and Pull requests: write, and set it as `BITBUCKET_TOKEN`. With an app password instead, also set `BITBUCKET_USERNAME`.
2. Add a webhook to `POST /webhooks/bitbucket` with a secret, for Pull request created, Pull request comment created and Repository push. Set the secret as `BITBUCKET_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Kiln checks the `X-Hub-Signature` header.
3. Set `BITBUCKET_BOT_ACCOUNTS` (comma-separated) to the accounts Kiln posts as, so their own activity is recognized.
4. List the repositories in `factory.yaml` with `forge: bitbucket`. `owner` is the workspace.

## Starting work

| Event | Fires when | Filters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pull_request_created` | A pull request is created. | `repos`, `base_branches`, `authors`, `keywords` |
| `pull_request_commented` | Someone comments on a pull request. | `repos`, `authors`, `keywords`, `mentioned` |
| `push` | A branch is pushed. | `repos`, `branches` |

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: bitbucket
    event: pull_request_commented
    filter: { mentioned: [kiln] }
---
```

Bitbucket pull requests have no labels, so label filters and routing labels do not apply.

## Related pages

- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md)

# Connections

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/connections.md

Kiln connects to each external system once for the whole workspace. Each factory then opts in to the systems it uses in `factory.yaml`, with its own settings.

## Workspace connections

A connection holds a provider's account details, scopes and credentials. Credentials are stored as encrypted Kiln secrets named `KILN_CONN_<PROVIDER>_<KEY>` and are never returned by the API.

| Provider | How it connects |
| --- | --- |
| `github` | GitHub App installation. See [GitHub](github.md). |
| `gitlab` | Group manager token. See [GitLab](gitlab.md). |
| `azure_devops` | Organization and personal access token. See [Azure DevOps](azure-devops.md). |
| `bitbucket` | Workspace and access token. See [Bitbucket](bitbucket.md). |
| `slack` | "Add to Slack" OAuth, or a pasted bot token. See [Slack](slack.md). |
| `microsoft-teams` | Bot app id and client secret. See [Microsoft Teams](microsoft-teams.md). |
| `discord` | Application id, public key and bot token. See [Discord](discord.md). |
| `linear` | OAuth app. See [Linear](linear.md). |
| `jira` | OAuth 2.0 (3LO), optionally approved by a site admin. See [Jira](jira.md). |

A connection's status is `connected`, `pending_approval` (an approval link is out) or `error` (the last test or completion failed, with the message).

Admins manage connections through the API:

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/connections` | Every provider, whether it is available on this server, and its connection. |
| `POST /api/v1/connections/<provider>/start` | Returns a `state`, the setup steps, and an OAuth or install `url` when the provider has one, or the `fields` to fill in. |
| `POST /api/v1/connections/<provider>/complete` | Finishes with `{ code, state }` from OAuth, or `{ params }` with the fields. |
| `POST /api/v1/connections/<provider>/test` | Calls the provider with the stored credentials. |
| `DELETE /api/v1/connections/<provider>` | Disconnects and deletes the stored credentials. |

OAuth providers send the browser back to `GET /oauth/<provider>/callback`, which finishes the connection and redirects to the web app's integrations page. The `state` expires after 30 minutes and works once.

Kiln builds adapters from a connection's credentials as soon as it is connected, so you do not restart the server. Providers configured with environment variables work the same way and take precedence.

### Approval links

Some connections need an admin of the other system, such as a Jira site admin. Send them an approval link instead of connecting yourself:

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/v1/connections/<provider>/approval-links` | Creates a link, optionally for an `email`. Returns its `url`. The connection shows `pending_approval`. |
| `GET /api/v1/connections/<provider>/approval-links` | Lists links and their state: `open`, `used` or `revoked`. |
| `POST /api/v1/approval-links/<id>/resend` | Issues a new token and another 7 days. The old URL stops working. |
| `DELETE /api/v1/approval-links/<id>` | Revokes the link. |

A link expires 7 days after it is created or resent. The approver opens `/connect/approve/<token>`, which starts the provider's flow. When they finish, the connection is recorded as made by the person who created the link, and the link is used.

## Per-factory opt-in

List the integrations a factory uses in `factory.yaml`. Bare names still work; objects carry settings under a key named after the type.

```yaml
integrations:
  - type: slack
    slack: { autoRespondToThreadReplies: true, channels: [C0123ABCD] }
  - type: microsoft-teams
    microsoft-teams:
      autoRespondToThreadReplies: false
      teams:
        - { teamId: 6b1f…, channelIds: ["19:abc@thread.tacv2"] }
  - type: discord
    discord: { guildIds: ["123"], channelIds: ["456"] }
  - type: linear
    linear: { teams: [Engineering] }
```

| Setting | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `autoRespondToThreadReplies` | Slack, Teams, Discord. Default `true`: plain replies in a factory's thread continue the work. When `false`, a reply must mention the app. |
| `slack.channels` | Channel IDs the factory listens in. DMs always reach it. |
| `discord.guildIds`, `discord.channelIds` | Servers and channels the factory listens in. |
| `microsoft-teams.teams` | Teams and at least one standard channel per team. |
| `linear.teams`, `jira.projects` | The teams or projects the factory works in. Default automation templates use them. |

- A factory can use Linear or Jira, not both. Validation fails otherwise.
- GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps and Bitbucket come from `repositories`, not from `integrations`.
- Once a provider is connected for the workspace, its events reach only factories that list it. Providers configured only through environment variables reach every factory.

For factories managed in Kiln (not in a config repo), `PUT /api/v1/factories/<id>/integrations` with `{ integrations: [...] }` rewrites `factory.yaml` and applies it. `GET /api/v1/factories/<id>/integrations` returns the settings, the forges, `cloudProviders`, the `github` settings and each provider's connection status.

## Linked accounts

Gate assignees are people. Kiln maps provider users to people in three ways:

- **Chat sign-in.** `sign in` replies with a one-hour link: `@Kiln sign in` in Teams, a mention of the app or a DM saying `sign in` in Slack, and `/kiln prompt: sign in` in Discord (only you see the reply). Opening it and calling `POST /api/v1/me/linked-accounts/claim` with the token adds the chat account to your linked accounts.
- **GitHub.** `POST /api/v1/me/linked-accounts/github/start` returns a GitHub OAuth URL (needs `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`). The callback `/oauth/github-user/callback` links the GitHub login.
- **Email.** Linear and Jira users that report an email address map to the person with that email.

Everything ends up in your linked accounts: `GET /api/v1/me/linked-accounts` lists them, `POST` adds one by hand and `DELETE /api/v1/me/linked-accounts/<provider>` unlinks one. The server's static `identities` map still works as a fallback.

## Notification routes

`GET /api/v1/notification-routes` lists where a factory can reach a person, with `available` and a `reason` when it cannot. Query with `factory`, `workItem` and `subject` (admins only for someone else).

| Route | Needs |
| --- | --- |
| `slack_dm`, `discord_dm` | The chat connected and the person's account linked. |
| `slack_thread`, `discord_thread`, `teams_thread` | Work that started in that thread. Teams bots cannot send DMs. |
| `linear_issue`, `linear_session`, `jira_issue` | Work that started from that issue or session. |
| `github_comment`, `gitlab_comment`, `azure_devops_comment`, `bitbucket_comment` | A source issue or the work item's pull request on that forge. |

## Alias directory

Automation filters can name teams, projects, states, channels and users instead of IDs. Kiln resolves the names when you apply a definition, using each connection's directory, and rejects names it cannot resolve. See [Automations](../configuration/automations.md#alias-filters).

Kiln refreshes the Linear (teams, projects, states, users) and Jira (projects) directories when you connect or test. Set any directory yourself with `PUT /api/v1/connections/<provider>/directory`, for example `{ "channels": { "eng": "C0123ABCD" }, "users": { "ann": "U024BE7LH" } }`.

## Environment variables

| Provider | Variables |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub | `GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_SLUG`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, or `GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| GitLab | `GITLAB_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_BASE_URL`, `GITLAB_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_BOT_USERNAMES` |
| Azure DevOps | `AZURE_DEVOPS_ORG`, `AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN`, `AZURE_DEVOPS_WEBHOOK_PASSWORD`, `AZURE_DEVOPS_WEBHOOK_USER`, `AZURE_DEVOPS_IDENTITIES` |
| Bitbucket | `BITBUCKET_TOKEN`, `BITBUCKET_USERNAME`, `BITBUCKET_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `BITBUCKET_BOT_ACCOUNTS` |
| Slack | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`, `SLACK_CLIENT_ID`, `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET`, `KILN_FACTORY_AVATAR_URL` |
| Microsoft Teams | `TEAMS_APP_ID`, `TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD`, `TEAMS_TENANT_ID` |
| Discord | `DISCORD_APPLICATION_ID`, `DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY`, `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_EVENTS_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_BOT_USER_ID` |
| Linear | `LINEAR_CLIENT_ID`, `LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET`, `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `LINEAR_ACCESS_TOKEN` |
| Jira | `JIRA_CLIENT_ID`, `JIRA_CLIENT_SECRET`, `JIRA_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, `JIRA_BOT_ACCOUNT_ID`, `JIRA_CLOUD_ID`, `JIRA_ACCESS_TOKEN` |

Webhook secrets are read from the environment first, then from Kiln secrets, then from the connection.

- [Custom webhooks](custom-webhooks.md)
- [Self-hosting](../infrastructure/self-hosting.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md)

# Custom webhooks

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/custom-webhooks.md

A custom webhook gives any system a URL that starts factory work: alerting tools, deploy platforms, payment providers or your own services.

## Two kinds

- **Managed webhooks** are created through the API (or the web app). Kiln generates their secret and stores it.
- **File webhooks** are `webhooks/<name>.yaml` files in the definition. Their secret is a Kiln secret you create first; Kiln never generates one for them.

```yaml
# webhooks/sentry.yaml
authMode: signature
signatureScheme: sentry
secretName: SENTRY_WEBHOOK_SECRET
deliveryIdHeader: request-id
enabled: true
```

A factory can have at most 20 webhooks, both kinds together. Each has a UID (`wh_…`) and the ingress URL `POST /webhooks/w/<uid>`. File webhooks keep the older URL `POST /webhooks/<factory>/<name>` too.

## Authentication

| `authMode` | The caller sends |
| --- | --- |
| `token` (default) | `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` |
| `url_token` | The secret as the last path segment: `/webhooks/w/<uid>/<secret>`. The URL is the credential. On the older URL, use `?token=<secret>`. |
| `signature` | The provider's signature, checked by `signatureScheme`. |

| `signatureScheme` | Header and check |
| --- | --- |
| `github` | `X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body>` |
| `pagerduty` | `X-PagerDuty-Signature: v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>`, several comma-separated during rotation |
| `sentry` | `Sentry-Hook-Signature: <hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body>` |
| `standard_webhooks` | `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature` (`v1,<base64 HMAC>` over `<id>.<timestamp>.<body>`). Svix headers are accepted. Older than five minutes is refused. |
| `stripe` | `Stripe-Signature: t=<time>,v1=<hex HMAC>`. Older than five minutes is refused. |
| `vercel` | `x-vercel-signature: <hex HMAC-SHA1 of the body>` |

The auth mode and scheme can't change after creation.

## Managing webhooks

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/factories/<id>/webhooks` | Managed and file webhooks with their URLs. |
| `POST /api/v1/factories/<id>/webhooks` | Creates one: `name`, `authMode`, `signatureScheme`, `secret`, `deliveryIdHeader`. Returns the webhook, its URL and the generated `secret`, shown once. |
| `PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/<uid>` | `enabled` and `deliveryIdHeader`. A disabled webhook answers 404. |
| `POST /api/v1/webhooks/<uid>/rotate` | Replaces the secret at once, with no overlap. For a second secret during a migration, create a second webhook. |
| `POST /api/v1/webhooks/<uid>/finish` | Stores the provider's secret and enables the webhook. |
| `DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/<uid>` | Deletes it. Automations that name it stay but stop firing. |
| `GET /api/v1/webhooks/<uid>/deliveries` | Recent deliveries. |
| `GET /api/v1/webhooks/<uid>/deliveries/<id>` | One delivery with its stored payload. |

Generated secrets start with `whsec_`. For `token` and `url_token` webhooks Kiln always generates the secret. For `standard_webhooks`, leave the secret blank and Kiln generates one to give the sender.

Stripe, Vercel, PagerDuty and other providers issue their secret only after they know the URL. Create the webhook without a secret ("create and get URL"): it starts disabled. Give the URL to the provider, then call `finish` with the secret it shows. File webhooks change only through the definition.

## Delivery rules

- `POST` only (other methods get 405). The body must be JSON (object, array or scalar), at most 256 KB. `Content-Type` is not checked.
- `202 {"delivery_id": "..."}` when accepted, even when no automation matches.
- `401` for failed authentication, `400` for invalid JSON, `404` for an unknown, disabled or deleted webhook, `413` for a body over 256 KB.
- `429` with `Retry-After` above 60 accepted deliveries a minute per webhook. Failed authentication has its own, lower budget.

Kiln identifies a delivery, in order, by: the webhook's `deliveryIdHeader`; the provider's own delivery header for signed webhooks (`X-GitHub-Delivery`, `webhook-id`, `X-Webhook-Id`, `Request-ID`, `x-vercel-id`); `X-Kiln-Delivery-Id`; or a hash of the body. A repeated delivery returns 202 with `duplicate: true` and starts nothing. Deliveries have no order guarantee, and each starts new work or none; they never continue a work item.

`deliveryIdHeader` must be a valid header name of at most 64 characters, and not one that can carry a credential, such as `Authorization` or a signature header.

## Deliveries log

Each delivery is logged with its delivery ID, size, time and status: `accepted`, `duplicate`, `rejected_auth`, `rejected_invalid_json` or `rejected_too_large`. Kiln stores the payload of accepted deliveries only. It keeps at least the last 50 deliveries and everything from the last 7 days.

## What the run receives

The work item's title comes from the payload's `title`, `summary` or `message`, or is `<name> webhook`. The body is the automation prompt plus an envelope with the webhook name, UID and delivery ID. The request body is attached as `event-payload.json` and marked as untrusted: agents read it as data and never follow instructions inside it.

## Triggering automations

Name the webhook in `webhook_ids` by file name, managed name or UID, and filter on the body with `payload`:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: webhook
    event: received
    filter:
      webhook_ids: [sentry]
      payload:
        data:
          issue:
            level: [fatal, error]
            environment: { not_in: [staging] }
---
Investigate the error and open a fix.
```

Webhook events only reach the factory that owns the webhook. The older `filter: { webhook: sentry }` still works.

### Payload filters

- Keys mirror the JSON body and combine with AND. Nested objects nest.
- A bare list means `in`. An operator object takes `in`, `not_in` and `exists`. Any other object nests further.
- Strings match exactly and case-sensitively. Numbers match numerically, so `1` equals `1.0`. Booleans and `null` can be matched.
- A missing key fails `in` and passes `not_in`. A nested pattern needs its key to exist.
- In an array of objects, any element may match. In an array of scalars, `in` means any overlap and `not_in` means none.
- Limits: at most 10 levels deep, 64 leaf fields and 32 values per list. The same value in `in` and `not_in`, or `exists: false` with a non-empty `in`, is rejected.
- A pattern that breaks these rules never matches.

### Test filter

`POST /api/v1/factories/<id>/automations/<name>/test-filter` with `{ "deliveryId": "<id>" }` evaluates the automation's triggers against a stored delivery. It returns `wouldTrigger` and, per trigger, each check (`webhook_ids`, `payload`, …) with whether it passed.

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Incident-response factory](../guides/incident-response-factory.md)

# Discord

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/discord.md

In Discord, you run `/kiln` or mention the bot to start work, and the factory continues in a thread on that message.

## Set up

1. Create an application at the Discord developer portal and add a bot. Copy the application ID, the public key and the bot token.
2. Set the Interactions Endpoint URL to `POST /webhooks/discord`. Discord checks it with a signed ping, which Kiln answers.
3. Give Kiln `DISCORD_APPLICATION_ID`, `DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY` and `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, or connect Discord from the API with the same values; see [Connections](connections.md).
4. Register the command: `POST /api/v1/integrations/discord/commands` (admin). Pass `{ "guildId": "<server id>" }` to register it in one server right away; global registration can take up to an hour.
5. Add the bot to your server with the install link the connection returns. It asks for: view channels, send messages, send messages in threads, create public threads, read message history and add reactions.
6. Add `discord` to the factory's `integrations`, optionally limited to servers and channels:

```yaml
integrations:
  - type: discord
    discord: { guildIds: ["1180000000000000000"], channelIds: ["1180000000000000001"] }
```

Kiln verifies the `X-Signature-Ed25519` signature over `X-Signature-Timestamp` and the body, and refuses timestamps more than five minutes old.

## Starting work

```text
/kiln prompt: Fix the flaky checkout test  factory: webapp
```

`factory` is optional; use it when several factories listen in the channel. Kiln replies "On it: …" right away, starts the work, and opens a thread on its reply where the work continues. When no factory picks it up, it says so.

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `slash_command` | Someone runs `/kiln`. |
| `app_mention` | A message mentions the bot (gateway bridge). |
| `message_posted` | Another message in a channel the bot reads (gateway bridge). |
| `reaction_added` | Someone adds a reaction (gateway bridge). |

Filters: `guild_ids`, `channel_ids`, `user_ids`, `keywords`, and `emojis` for reactions. See [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md).

## Mentions, messages and reactions

Discord only sends slash commands to an interactions endpoint. For mentions, messages and reactions, run a small bridge on the Discord gateway that forwards `MESSAGE_CREATE` and `MESSAGE_REACTION_ADD` dispatches (`{ "t": ..., "d": ... }`) to `POST /webhooks/discord/events` with `Authorization: Bearer <DISCORD_EVENTS_TOKEN>`. Set `DISCORD_BOT_USER_ID` (or connect Discord) so Kiln can tell mentions of the bot apart. Kiln reacts with 👀 and starts a thread on a mention that starts work.

Replies in the work's thread continue it. With `autoRespondToThreadReplies: false`, a reply must mention the bot.

## Decisions

Buttons with the custom IDs `kiln:approve:<gate id>` and `kiln:reject:<gate id>` decide a gate. Only the gate's assignees can use them. Run `/kiln prompt: sign in` to link your Discord account so Kiln knows who you are.

## Related pages

- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Slack](slack.md)
- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)

---

# GitHub

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/github.md

GitHub is both a source of work and the place where Kiln delivers it: issues and comments start work items, Kiln opens pull requests on `kiln/*` branches, and a person's merge completes the work.

## Set up

### One click from the web app

An admin opens **Integrations → GitHub** and clicks **Create GitHub App**, optionally naming an organization. GitHub shows the app Kiln asks for (the permissions, events and webhook below); click **Create**. GitHub gives the app's private key and webhook secret to the Kiln server, and Kiln takes you to install the app on the repositories you pick. When you come back, GitHub is connected and Kiln uses the app from then on, without a restart.

This needs `KILN_PUBLIC_URL` (GitHub calls it) and `KILN_SECRET_KEY` (the key is stored encrypted with it). The key is kept apart from secrets: no agent can ask for it by name. `POST /api/v1/connections/github/app-manifest` returns the manifest and the URL to post it to; `GET /api/v1/connections/github/app` shows the app. Environment variables, below, take precedence.

### By hand

1. Create a GitHub App (Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps) with these repository permissions: Contents, Issues, Pull requests and Checks read and write, Metadata read.
2. Set its webhook URL to `POST /webhooks/github` with a secret, and subscribe to Issues, Issue comment, Pull request, Pull request review, Pull request review comment, Check suite, Check run, Status, Workflow run and Push.
3. Give Kiln the app's credentials and install the app on your organization:

| Variable | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `GITHUB_APP_ID` | The app's ID. |
| `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | The app's private key, as PEM (`\n` escapes are fine) or base64. |
| `GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` | The installation on your organization. Kiln mints a short-lived installation token for each call. |
| `GITHUB_APP_SLUG` | Lets Kiln link to the install page and recognize its own `<slug>[bot]` events. |
| `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | The webhook secret. |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | The app's OAuth credentials, for people to link their GitHub accounts. |

A plain `GITHUB_TOKEN` still works instead of an app. You can also connect GitHub from the API; see [Connections](connections.md).

4. List the repositories in `factory.yaml` under `repositories`.
5. Protect `main`: require reviews and status checks, and do not let Kiln's identity bypass them.

Kiln verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` on every call and ignores repeated `X-GitHub-Delivery` IDs.

Connect more accounts and organizations with **Add a GitHub account or organization** in the same panel: each gets its own private app, and Kiln uses the app installed on each repository's owner (`GET /api/v1/connections/github/apps` lists them). A public app installed on several accounts works the same way. A sandbox never gets the app's own credentials: it clones and pushes with an installation token limited to that one repository (contents write, metadata read) that expires within the hour. Protect your default branch, because contents write can push to any branch that is not protected.

## Mention the factory

Mention `@kiln-factory` in a new issue, pull request, comment or review. Edits and mentions inside code blocks are ignored.

- **With a `factory:<alias>` label**, the mention goes to that factory.
- **Without a label**, Kiln looks for factories whose `repositories` include the repo. With exactly one, it adds that factory's label and starts the work. With several, it comments asking you to add one of their labels and mention `@kiln-factory` again. With none, it comments that no factory works on the repo yet.

Kiln creates the `factory:<alias>` label on the factory's repositories whenever its definition is applied. Deleting the factory (`DELETE /api/v1/factories/<id>`, Admin role) removes the label again, cancels its open work and deletes its managed webhooks.

The default mentions template routes on both, and you can change the handle or label it filters on:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: github
    event: issue_mentioned
    filter: { mentioned: [kiln-factory], labels: ["factory:webapp"] }
  - provider: github
    event: issue_assigned
    filter: { assignees: [kiln-factory], labels: ["factory:webapp"] }
---
```

## Starting work

Add an automation for the events you want:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: github
    event: issue_labeled
    filter:
      repos: [acme/web]
      labels: [kiln-ready]
---
Take the labeled issue through the factory.
```

GitHub triggers cover issues (`issue_created`, `issue_labeled`, `issue_assigned`, `issue_commented`, `issue_mentioned`), pull requests (`pull_request_opened`, `_ready`, `_reopened`, `_labeled`, `_assigned`, `_synchronized`, `_enqueued`, `_dequeued`, `_review_requested`, `_review_submitted`, `_commented`, `_mentioned`, `_merged`, `_closed`), CI (`check_suite_completed`, `check_suite_rerequested`, `check_run_rerequested`, `commit_status`, `workflow_run_completed`) and `push`. The full list of events and filter keys is in [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md).

- One delivery can produce several events. A comment with a mention is both `issue_commented` and `issue_mentioned`; an automation that listens to both still fires once.
- `skip_bots` defaults to `all`: events from bots never start work. Use `self` to skip only Kiln's own app, or `none`. Admitting Kiln's own events can cause loops.
- On check suite and workflow run events, `number` is the linked pull request.

## What Kiln does on GitHub

- **Branches.** Each work item gets one branch, `kiln/<id>-<title-slug>`. Kiln pushes it with the run's token, which can push only `kiln/*` branches.
- **Spec pull request.** When the work needs a spec, Kiln opens a draft pull request with the spec and the acceptance criteria as a checklist.
- **Pull request body.** It links the work item, the source and the tracker issue, lists the acceptance criteria, and ends with "Opened by the Kiln factory `<alias>`. A person reviews and merges."
- **CI.** The verify stage waits for check runs on the branch. Failures, cancellations and timeouts loop the work back to build.
- **Preview card.** With a preview provider, Kiln comments a card with the preview URL, test counts and one video link per acceptance criterion.
- **Review findings.** Findings that need a person's judgment are posted as a comment.
- **Ready for review.** When the build stage succeeds, Kiln opens the pull request, or takes the spec pull request out of draft.
- **Attribution.** When Kiln opens a pull request, it comments which factory opened it, for whom, from where, and links the work item.
- **Hand-off.** Kiln adds the label `factory:<alias>` and posts "Ready to merge" with the pull request link where the work started, for example on the source issue.

## After hand-off

- **Merge.** When a person merges the pull request, the `pull_request` webhook completes the work item and closes its open gates.
- **Review comments.** A submitted review that is not an approval sends the work item back to build, with the review text as findings.
- **Comments.** Comments on the source issue or the pull request decide an open spec or preview gate, answer an open question, steer a running agent, or are added to the work item's conversation. Map GitHub logins to people with the server's `identities` option (`github:<login>`). Replies decide a gate only when their author is one of its assignees; see [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).

## Config repos

A factory's definition can live in a GitHub repository. Merges to its branch apply the new definition when Kiln receives the `push` webhook, so install the app on the config repo too. See [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#config-repos-on-github).

### The kiln/factory-config check

On pull requests to a config repo, Kiln reads the head commit, validates it and dry-runs the apply: missing runners and routers, schema errors and alias names that do not resolve all fail the check. The summary counts what would be created, updated and deleted. When nothing in the definition changed, the check passes right away.

- The check is named `kiln/factory-config`, or `kiln/factory-config (<dir>)` when the definition lives in a subdirectory.
- Require it in branch protection to block broken definitions.
- `github.factoryConfigChecks` in `factory.yaml` chooses which pull requests get it: `main` (default) checks only pull requests to the production branch, `all` checks every base branch.

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md)
- [Connections](connections.md)
- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)
- [Previews](previews.md)
- [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md)
- [Architecture and security](../infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md)

# GitLab

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/gitlab.md

GitLab works as a forge (branches, merge requests, labels, comments) and as a source of work: mention the factory's bot in a merge request comment and the factory replies in that discussion.

## Set up

1. Create a group access token or service account token with the Owner role and the `api` scope on your top-level group. This manager token maintains the group webhook and does the factory's forge work. Set it as `GITLAB_TOKEN`.
2. For self-managed GitLab, set `GITLAB_BASE_URL`, such as `https://gitlab.acme.test`. The default is `https://gitlab.com`.
3. Create a bot service account for each factory, named for example `webapp-kiln-ab12`, with the Developer role on the projects it works on. List the bot usernames in `GITLAB_BOT_USERNAMES` (comma-separated). Mentions of these usernames start work, and their own activity never triggers automations.
4. Add a group webhook to `POST /webhooks/gitlab` with a secret token, for Note (comments), Merge request and Push events. Set the same token as `GITLAB_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`. Kiln refuses calls whose `X-Gitlab-Token` does not match.
5. List the projects in `factory.yaml` with `forge: gitlab`. `owner` is the group path, which may include subgroups:

```yaml
repositories:
  - { forge: gitlab, owner: acme/platform, name: api }
```

You can also connect GitLab from the API with the group path and manager token; see [Connections](connections.md). Per-factory bot tokens are not used yet: forge work uses the one manager token.

## Starting work

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `bot_mentioned` | A new comment on a merge request or issue mentions a factory bot. Edits never fire. |
| `merge_request` | A merge request is opened, updated, closed, reopened, merged or approved. `action` holds which. |
| `push` | A branch is pushed. |

| Event | Filters |
| --- | --- |
| `bot_mentioned` | `repos`. The bot username is managed by Kiln; a definition that sets `mentioned` is rejected. |
| `merge_request` | `actions`, `base_branches`, `repos` |
| `push` | `branches`, `repos` |

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: gitlab
    event: merge_request
    filter: { actions: [open], base_branches: [main] }
---
Review the merge request.
```

The `gitlab-bot-mentions` template starts work from every bot mention. See [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md).

## What Kiln does on GitLab

- **Replies** go to the discussion where the bot was mentioned, or as a note on the merge request.
- **Merge requests** are opened from `kiln/*` branches, as drafts (`Draft: ` prefix) until the work is ready, with the factory's labels.
- **Labels.** Kiln creates the `factory:<alias>` label on the factory's projects.
- **Checks.** CI status comes from the project's pipelines. The `kiln/factory-config` check is reported as a commit status.
- **Merges.** A merged merge request completes its work item. Kiln never merges or approves.

GitLab is not supported as a config repo for factory definitions.

## Related pages

- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [GitHub](github.md)
- [Self-hosting](../infrastructure/self-hosting.md)

# Jira

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/jira.md

Jira works like Linear in Kiln: issues and comments start or continue work items, updates go back as comments, and the planning agent can create its roadmap in a Jira project.

## Set up

Jira Cloud only.

1. Create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app in the Atlassian developer console with the callback URL `<public URL>/oauth/jira/callback` and the scopes `read:jira-work`, `write:jira-work`, `read:jira-user`, `manage:jira-webhook` and `offline_access`. Set `JIRA_CLIENT_ID` and `JIRA_CLIENT_SECRET`.
2. Connect Jira for the workspace. A Jira site admin approves the app. If that is someone else, send them an approval link: it expires in 7 days, and you can resend or revoke it. See [Connections](connections.md#approval-links).
3. Add a Jira webhook pointing at `POST /webhooks/jira?token=<token>` for issue created, issue updated and comment created events, and store the token as `JIRA_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`. Once it is set, Kiln refuses calls that do not carry it. Kiln also ignores repeated `X-Atlassian-Webhook-Identifier` values.
4. Set `JIRA_BOT_ACCOUNT_ID` to the Atlassian account ID that represents the factory. Assigning it, or mentioning it, starts an agent session.
5. Add `jira` to the factory's `integrations`, with its projects. A factory uses Linear or Jira, not both:

```yaml
integrations:
  - type: jira
    jira: { projects: [ENG] }
```

For the tracker features below (comments, states, planning), Kiln reads `JIRA_BASE_URL`, `JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN` and `JIRA_PROJECT_KEY` and calls Jira's REST API v3 with basic auth. With `JIRA_CLOUD_ID` and `JIRA_ACCESS_TOKEN` (or the OAuth connection), Kiln can also comment, transition and change labels through the Atlassian API.

## Starting work

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `agent_session_created` | Someone assigns the factory's account, or mentions it in an issue or comment. |
| `issue_created` | An issue is created. |
| `issue_labeled` | Labels are added. |
| `status_changed` | An issue changes status. `status_id` is the new status. |

Filter on `project_keys` and `labels`; sessions also take `keywords` (case-insensitive), and `status_changed` takes `status_ids`. See [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md).

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: jira
    event: agent_session_created
    filter:
      project_keys: [ENG]
      keywords: [investigate, fix]
---
```

The issue key, such as `ENG-42`, links the work item to the issue. Other comments on that issue continue the work item. Jira events reach every factory that opted in to Jira, so filter on `project_keys`.

## What Kiln does in Jira

- **Updates.** Gate requests, reminders, "Ready to merge" and "Done" are posted as comments.
- **Actions.** Through the Atlassian API Kiln can post comments, transition an issue by status name, and add or remove labels.
- **Replies.** Comments on the issue continue the work item. They decide an open spec or preview gate, answer an open question, steer a running agent, or are added to the conversation. Jira users with an email map to the person with that email; the server's `identities` option (`jira:<user>`) also works. Replies decide a gate only when their author is one of its assignees; see [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).
- **States.** At hand-off, Kiln moves the issue through the first transition into the "In Progress" status category. On completion, it uses the first transition into the "Done" category.
- **Duplicates.** Triage reads the project's 20 most recently created issues to spot duplicates.
- **Text.** Kiln writes descriptions and comments in Atlassian Document Format, one paragraph per blank-line-separated block.

## Planning

The [planning agent](../product-owners/planning.md) can create its roadmap in the Jira project: a Task per epic, labeled `epic`, with a Sub-task for each piece of work. Each sub-task has an acceptance criteria checklist and a `factory:<alias>` label.

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Linear](linear.md)
- [Planning](../product-owners/planning.md)
- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)

---

# Linear

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/linear.md

Linear can start work items, receives the factory's updates as comments on the issue, and is where the planning agent creates roadmap issues.

## Set up

1. Create an OAuth application in Linear (Settings → API) with the redirect URL `<public URL>/oauth/linear/callback` and set `LINEAR_CLIENT_ID` and `LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET`. Kiln asks for `actor=app`, so the factory appears in Linear as an app you can assign, mention and delegate to.
2. Enable the app's webhook to `POST /webhooks/linear` for Issues, Comments and Agent session events, and store its signing secret as `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Kiln checks the `Linear-Signature` header and ignores repeated `Linear-Delivery` IDs.
3. Connect Linear once for the workspace. See [Connections](connections.md). Instead of the OAuth flow you can set `LINEAR_ACCESS_TOKEN` to an app token.
4. Add `linear` to the factory's `integrations`, with the teams it works in:

```yaml
integrations:
  - type: linear
    linear: { teams: [Engineering] }
```

A factory uses Linear or Jira, not both.

To limit who can start work from Linear, list people by Linear user id, email or name. `allowUsers` lets only them in, and `blockUsers` keeps them out. Without either list, everyone in the factory's teams can. When someone who is not allowed delegates or mentions the factory in an agent session, no work starts and the session tells them why:

```yaml
integrations:
  - type: linear
    linear: { teams: [Engineering], allowUsers: [ann@acme.com, Bob Smith] }
```

For the tracker features below (comments, states, planning), Kiln also reads `LINEAR_API_KEY` and `LINEAR_TEAM_ID`.

## Starting work

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `agent_session_created` | Someone assigns, mentions or delegates to the factory's app. |
| `issue_created` | An issue is created. |
| `issue_assigned` | An issue gets an assignee. |
| `issue_labeled` | A label is added. |
| `issue_state_changed` | An issue moves to another workflow state. |
| `comment_created` | A comment is added. |

Filter on `team_ids`, `project_ids`, `state_ids`, `assignee_ids`, `creator_ids`, `labels`, `mentioned_user_ids`, `keywords` (sessions) and `issue_ids` (comments). `teams`, `projects`, `states` and `issues` take names (or issue numbers) instead of IDs; Kiln resolves them when you apply the definition and rejects names it does not know. See [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md).

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: linear
    event: agent_session_created
    filter: { teams: [Engineering] }
---
```

The factory's own activity in Linear never triggers automations.

Listening to both `agent_session_created` and `comment_created` can start two runs for one mention. Use sessions for routing and comments for follow-ups.

## Agent sessions

When work starts from a session, Kiln keeps the session up to date:

- a thought right after the session is created, and one each time the work moves to another stage,
- every agent run's work as it happens: what the agent says and thinks as thoughts, each tool call as an action with its main argument (the file, command, pattern or URL) and a short result, and errors, including why a run failed,
- the factory's messages (questions, gate requests, "Ready to merge") as responses. A question with one single-select question (an agent's `ask_user` with options) is asked with Linear's select signal instead: the person picks an option, and the pick answers the question,
- an action and an attachment on the issue when the pull request opens.

Run activity is posted in the order the run produced it. Long text is shortened, secrets are redacted as in the run log, and a failure to reach Linear never fails the run. Bookkeeping events, such as queueing, costs and steering, are not posted.

Replies in the session continue the same work item.

## What Kiln does in Linear

- **Updates.** Gate requests, reminders, "Ready to merge" and "Done" are posted as comments on the issue.
- **Replies.** Comments on the issue continue the work item. A comment starting with `approve` or `reject` decides an open spec or preview gate, and other text answers an open question, steers a running agent, or is added to the conversation. Linear users with an email map to the person with that email; the server's `identities` option (`linear:<user>`) also works. Replies decide a gate only when their author is one of its assignees; see [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).
- **States.** At hand-off, Kiln moves the issue to the team's first `started` state. When the work completes, it moves it to the first `completed` state. To use your own workflow states, name them in the factory's Linear settings. Kiln then moves issues that came from Linear to those states by name, and tells the requester if a name does not exist on the team:

  ```yaml
  integrations:
    - type: linear
      linear: { teams: [Engineering], states: { handoff: "UAT Test", done: Released } }
  ```
- **Duplicates.** Triage reads the team's 20 most recent issues to spot duplicates.

## Planning

The [planning agent](../product-owners/planning.md) creates its roadmap in Linear: one issue per epic, with a sub-issue for each piece of work. The epic is labeled `epic`. Each sub-issue has an "Acceptance criteria" checklist, a `factory:<alias>` label and a "Factory: @<alias>" line. Kiln looks labels up by name and creates any that are missing on the team.

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Planning](../product-owners/planning.md)
- [Jira](jira.md)
- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)

# Microsoft Teams

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/microsoft-teams.md

In Microsoft Teams, you mention the Kiln bot in a connected channel to start work, and the work item lives in that thread.

## Set up

Three people are usually involved: a Kiln admin connects the bot, a Teams admin or team owner uploads and approves the app, and a factory editor picks the teams and channels.

1. Register a bot in Azure (an Azure Bot resource, single or multi tenant) and create a client secret.
2. Set its messaging endpoint to `POST /webhooks/teams` and enable the Microsoft Teams channel.
3. Give Kiln `TEAMS_APP_ID` (the bot's app ID) and `TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD` (the client secret). For a single-tenant bot, also set `TEAMS_TENANT_ID`. Or connect it from the API; see [Connections](connections.md).
4. Download the app package: `GET /api/v1/integrations/teams/app-package` (admin). It is a zip with `manifest.json` and two icons, `color.png` (192×192) and `outline.png` (32×32), and no executables. Query `name`, `developer`, `website` and `color` to customize it.
5. In the Teams admin center, choose Teams apps → Manage apps → Upload new app, upload the zip, and approve it.
6. Add the app to each team (Apps → Built for your org).
7. In each factory, select the teams and at least one standard channel per team:

```yaml
integrations:
  - type: microsoft-teams
    microsoft-teams:
      autoRespondToThreadReplies: true
      teams:
        - { teamId: 6b1f0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001, channelIds: ["19:abc@thread.tacv2"] }
```

Kiln validates every call's Bot Framework token: the signature against Microsoft's published keys, the issuer, the audience (your app ID), the expiry, and that the token's service URL matches the activity.

## Starting work

Mention the bot with your request:

```text
@Kiln the export button times out on large reports
```

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `app_mention` | The bot is mentioned in a connected channel. |
| `message_posted` | Another message the bot can see in that channel. |

Filters: `team_ids` (exactly one Teams team ID), `channel_ids` (at least one `19:…@thread.tacv2` ID), `keywords` and `user_ids`. `team_ids` and `channel_ids` take only `in`. See [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md).

Replies in the thread continue the work. With `autoRespondToThreadReplies: false`, a reply must mention the bot.

If a channel isn't connected to any factory, the bot answers: "This Microsoft Teams channel isn't connected to a Kiln factory. Connect this team to a factory, then mention this bot again."

## Commands

| Message | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Kiln sign in` | Replies with a one-hour link that connects your Teams account to your Kiln account, so your replies can decide gates. |
| `@Kiln sign out` | Unlinks your account from every factory in that Microsoft organization. |
| `@Kiln help` | Explains how to use the bot and lists the factories connected to the channel. |

## Scope and limits

- Standard and shared channels only: no private channels and no DMs. Add shared channels by channel ID in `factory.yaml`.
- The bot replies in the thread where the work started and can post top-level messages. It cannot DM people, react to messages or upload files.

## Related pages

- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Slack](slack.md)
- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)

---

# Previews

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/previews.md

A preview provider deploys each factory pull request to its own URL, so a person can try the change and accept it before review and merge.

## How previews fit in

When a preview provider is configured, the foreman's default path adds a preview stage after verify. In a [pipeline](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md), add it yourself:

```yaml
- { id: preview, action: preview.deploy, gate: preview-acceptance }
```

The preview stage:

1. Deploys the work item's branch.
2. Comments a card on the pull request with the preview URL, the pull request link, the test counts and a table of acceptance criteria with their result and a video link.
3. Moves the work item to `awaiting_preview` and opens the stage's gate with the card, the preview URL and each video as evidence.

The stage is skipped when no provider is configured or the work item has no pull request. Without a `gate`, the stage deploys and moves on.

Approving the gate moves the work on. Rejecting it sends the work back to build with your feedback. When it comes back, Kiln deploys again and asks again. See [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md).

## Providers

Kiln uses one preview provider per installation.

### Vercel

Kiln creates a preview deployment through Vercel's API from the GitHub branch. It needs:

| Setting | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Token | A Vercel access token. |
| Project | The Vercel project name. |
| Team ID | Optional. For projects owned by a team. |

The preview URL is the deployment's URL.

### Kubernetes

Kiln applies one namespace per pull request with `kubectl apply`:

- a Namespace named `preview-<repo>-pr-<number>` (lowercased, at most 63 characters), labeled `kiln.dev/preview: "true"`,
- a Deployment `app` with one replica of your image,
- a Service `app` on port 80,
- an Ingress for the host `pr-<number>.<repo>.<domain>`.

| Setting | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | The base domain for preview hosts. Point a wildcard DNS record and certificate at your ingress controller. |
| Image | How to name the image for a repository and branch. Your CI must build and push that image. |
| Port | The container port. Default 3000. |

The preview URL is `https://pr-<number>.<repo>.<domain>`. Destroying a preview deletes its namespace.

## Evidence on the card

The card's criteria table comes from the verify stage. The verify agent runs Playwright with video on and writes a JSON report to `playwright-report/results.json`. Kiln matches tests to criteria by the `AC<number>` in each test title, such as `AC1: the settings page has a dark mode switch`, and uploads one video per criterion to object storage. See [Writing acceptance criteria](../product-owners/acceptance-criteria.md).

## Related pages

- [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md)
- [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [GitHub](github.md)
- [Self-hosting](../infrastructure/self-hosting.md)

---

# Slack

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/slack.md

In Slack, you mention a factory's alias to start work, and the whole work item then lives in that thread: questions, approvals, the preview and the pull request link.

## Set up

1. Create a Slack app with a bot user and these bot scopes: `app_mentions:read`, `channels:history`, `channels:read`, `chat:write`, `chat:write.customize`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `im:write`, `mpim:history`, `reactions:read`, `reactions:write`, `users:read`, `users:read.email`.
2. Turn on Event Subscriptions with the request URL `POST /webhooks/slack`. Kiln answers Slack's URL verification challenge.
3. Subscribe to the bot events `app_mention`, `message.channels`, `message.groups`, `message.im`, `message.mpim`, `member_joined_channel`, `reaction_added` and `app_home_opened`, and enable the Home tab.
4. Store the app's signing secret in Kiln as `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`.
5. Install the app:
   - **Add to Slack.** Set `SLACK_CLIENT_ID` and `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET`, add `<public URL>/oauth/slack/callback` as a redirect URL, and start the connection. If your workspace requires admin approval, an admin approves the request first. See [Connections](connections.md).
   - **Or a token.** Install the app yourself and set `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, or paste the token and signing secret when you connect.
6. Add `slack` to the factory's `integrations` and invite the bot to the channels you use. Private channels always need an invite.

Kiln checks Slack's signature and refuses requests whose timestamp is more than five minutes old. It answers Slack right away and does the work in the background. Retries with the same `event_id` are ignored.

## Starting work

Mention the factory's alias:

```text
@webapp the footer link to /pricing is broken
```

The first line becomes the work item's title, and the rest becomes its body. Kiln reacts with 👀 to the message that started or continued work.

A factory with no automations answers mentions of its alias. To control it, add an automation:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: slack
    event: app_mention
    filter: { channel_ids: [C0123ABCD], keywords: [bug] }
---
```

When a message names a factory's alias, only that factory gets it. A message that only mentions the bot reaches every factory listening in that channel.

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `app_mention` | The bot is mentioned. |
| `message_dm`, `message_im` | Someone sends the bot a direct message. Both fire for the same message. |
| `message_mpim` | A message in a group DM the bot is in. |
| `message_posted` | A message in a channel the bot is in, including thread replies. |
| `member_joined_channel` | Someone joins a channel. |
| `reaction_added` | Someone adds a reaction. `emoji` holds its name. |

Filters: `channel_ids`, `user_ids`, `keywords`, and for reactions `emojis` and `item_user_ids` (who wrote the message). `channels`, `users` and `itemUsers` take names instead of IDs and are resolved when you apply the definition. See [Automation triggers](../configuration/automation-triggers.md).

Messages from bots are ignored. An app mention in a channel where you also listen to `message_posted` produces two events; Kiln continues work once, but two automations can both fire.

## Factory settings

```yaml
integrations:
  - type: slack
    slack: { autoRespondToThreadReplies: false, channels: [C0123ABCD] }
```

- `autoRespondToThreadReplies` (default `true`): plain replies in a factory's thread continue the work. When `false`, replies must mention the app. DMs are unchanged.
- `channels`: the channel IDs this factory listens in. DMs always reach it.

Kiln posts as the factory, using its name. Set `KILN_FACTORY_AVATAR_URL` to a URL template with `{alias}`, such as `https://cdn.acme.test/factories/{alias}.png`, to give each factory its own avatar.

## Home tab

Opening the app's Home tab shows the work you asked for, grouped by stage (Triage, Planning, Building, Reviewing, Complete, Cancelled), newest first, with links to the web app.

## Working in the thread

Kiln posts to the thread where the work started:

- questions and gate requests, such as "Approve the spec", with the details and a link to decide in the inbox,
- reminders when a gate waits past its nudge time,
- "Ready to merge" with the pull request and preview links,
- "Done" when the pull request is merged.

Reply in the thread to act on the work item:

| Reply starts with | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `approve`, `approved`, `lgtm`, `ship it` or `accept` | Approves the open spec or preview gate. |
| `reject`, `changes:` or `request changes` | Rejects it. The rest of your message is the feedback. |
| Anything else | Answers an open question. If there is none and an agent is running on the work item, it steers that agent. Otherwise it is added to the conversation for the next agent run. |

Approve, reject and answer only count when you are one of the gate's assignees, or the gate has none. Kiln matches your Slack user to a person through a [linked account](connections.md#linked-accounts) (mention the app with `sign in`, or DM it `sign in`) or the server's `identities` map, for example `slack:U024BE7LH` to `po@acme.test`. Without a mapping, your Slack user ID must itself be an assignee. Replies that cannot decide the gate are handled like other text. See [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).

Decisions from Slack are recorded with your person (or Slack user ID) and `slack` as the surface, exactly like decisions from the web.

Steering from the thread works like steering from the run page. See [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md#steering).

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Connections](connections.md)
- [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md)
- [Inbox](../management/inbox.md)
- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)
