# Admin, RBAC and audit

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/management/admin-rbac-audit.md

Access to Kiln's API and MCP is controlled by tokens whose scopes are granted per factory, and every change people or Kiln make is written to the audit log.

## Tokens

A token belongs to a subject (a person or a service), has a name, a list of grants and an optional lifetime in hours. Kiln shows the token once, when it is issued, and stores only its hash. Tokens can be revoked; a revoked or expired token is refused.

Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the API, and configure it in your MCP client for the Kiln MCP. See the [API overview](../developer-tools/api.md) and the [MCP reference](../developer-tools/mcp.md).

Only server admins and team owners and admins can issue scoped tokens, list them, manage secrets and read the audit log.

### Server admins and team admins

| Who | Audit log | Token list | `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/secrets` | Issuing scoped tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Server admin: the bootstrap admin token (`admin` on `*`), dev auth, or a user listed in `KILN_ADMIN_EMAILS` | Every team | Every token | The server's secret store | Any grants |
| Team owner or admin | Their current team only | Tokens of their team and its members | The team's raw secrets | Only on their team's factories, never `*`. The token belongs to the team. |

Kiln records the team of each audit entry from what it is about: the factory, work item, run, gate, secret, token, team or user. When a factory moves to another team, its history moves with it.

### Token types

| Type | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `scoped` | The explicit grants it was issued with (`POST /api/v1/tokens`). The bootstrap admin token is one. |
| `session` | A login. Grants come from the user's team and factory roles, computed on every request. |
| `personal` | An API key that acts as its user, like a session. |
| `agent` | A team service account: `read` and `send` on the team's factories. |
| `worker` | A self-hosted worker. It has no API scopes. |

Sessions and personal, agent and worker keys are covered in [Teams and users](teams-and-users.md).

## Scopes

Each grant pairs one scope with one factory ID, or `*` for all factories.

| Scope | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | See factories, definitions, work items, runs, gates, scores, metrics, self-improvement proposals, benchmarks and memories. |
| `send` | Send work items, post messages, cancel work, pull a task to a local worktree and hand it back, steer, replay, pause, resume and cancel runs, propose memories, and create and plan projects. |
| `decide:spec` | Approve or reject spec gates. |
| `decide:preview` | Approve or reject preview gates. |
| `decide:question` | Answer, approve or reject question gates. |
| `decide:merge` | Decide merge and custom gates, and confirm a handed-off work item complete without a merge. |
| `definitions:write` | Apply, sync and connect definitions, promote or roll back canaries, run self-improvement and benchmarks, approve or reject proposals, accept or reject memories, save benchmark tasks, publish and install skills. |
| `admin` | Everything above on the granted factories, plus tokens, secrets and the audit log when granted on `*`. |

Rules:

- `admin` implies every other scope.
- There are no wildcard scopes such as `decide:*`. Grant each one you need.
- A grant for one factory never covers another. Only `*` covers all.
- Connecting a new config repo needs `definitions:write` on `*`, because the factory does not exist yet.

### Grant strings

Grants can be written as a comma-separated string of `<scope>:<factory>`:

```text
read:*,send:webapp,decide:spec:webapp,decide:preview:webapp
```

An unknown scope is an error.

### Typical tokens

| Who | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| Product owner | `read:*`, `send:<factory>`, `decide:spec:<factory>`, `decide:preview:<factory>`, `decide:question:<factory>` |
| Engineer | `read:*`, `send:<factory>`, `decide:question:<factory>`, `decide:merge:<factory>` |
| Factory engineer | `read:*`, `send:<factory>`, `definitions:write:<factory>` |
| CI validating definitions | Any valid token; validation needs no scope. Add `definitions:write:<factory>` to apply. |
| Admin | `admin:*` |

A product owner's token cannot touch definitions, and a `decide:preview` token cannot apply definition changes.

### Roles map onto scopes

People do not need hand-made grants. Their factory role (User, Editor or Admin) gives them the scopes in [Factory roles](teams-and-users.md#factory-roles), and team owners and admins are Admin on every factory in their team. A team-wide check (`*`), or a factory that does not exist yet, is decided by the team role. Members may `read` and `send`. Owners and admins may do everything.

## Run tokens are different

Agents never get API tokens. Each run gets its own run token, valid for 60 minutes, that can only push `kiln/*` branches of the run's repositories, open pull requests, comment and add labels. It can never approve or merge. See [Architecture and security](../infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md).

## Secrets

Server admins store named secrets, such as webhook secrets and API keys, in Kiln. (For a team admin, the same endpoints read and write the team's raw secrets.) Listing secrets returns names only; values never leave the server through the API. When a secret is not in the store, Kiln looks for the server environment variable `KILN_SECRET_<NAME>`. The only plain environment variables Kiln reads as secrets are model-provider keys: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`. This way an agent definition cannot ask for the server's own credentials by name. Listing secrets includes names found in the environment.

These server secrets are the last place Kiln looks. Typed team and personal secrets, which most teams should use, are described in [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](secrets-mcps-environments.md).

## Audit log

Kiln writes an entry with the time, the actor, the action and the target for:

| Area | Actions |
| --- | --- |
| Definitions | `definition.applied` (with SHA, diff and canary share), `definition.rejected` (with errors), `canary.promoted`, `canary.rolled_back` |
| Work items | `work_item.created`, `work_item.cancelled`, `notify.failed` (posting back to a thread or issue, or a notification to a person), `transcript.failed` |
| Gates | `gate.approve`, `gate.reject`, `gate.answer`, with the surface used |
| Runs | `run.steered` (with the message), `run.cancelled`, `run.paused`, `run.resumed` |
| Self-improvement | `proposal.opened`, `proposal.approved`, `proposal.force_approved`, `proposal.rejected`, `proposal.empty`, `proposal.invalid` |
| Accounts | `user.created`, `user.password_changed`, `user.email_changed`, `user.account_linked`, `user.account_unlinked`, `auth.login`, `auth.login_failed`, `auth.logout`, `api_key.created`, `api_key.revoked` |
| Teams | `team.created`, `team.updated`, `team.avatar_changed`, `team.settings_changed`, `team.member_added`, `team.member_role_changed`, `team.member_removed`, `team.invite_created`, `team.invite_resent`, `team.invite_revoked`, `team.invite_accepted` |
| Factory roles | `factory.team_assigned`, `factory.member_added`, `factory.member_role_changed`, `factory.member_removed` |
| Secrets, MCP servers and environments | `secret.created`, `secret.updated`, `secret.deleted`, `mcp.created`, `mcp.updated`, `mcp.deleted`, `environment.created`, `environment.updated`, `environment.deleted` |
| Skills, memories and routers | `skill.published`, `skill.installed`, `memory.accepted`, `memory.rejected`, `router.proposed` |
| Planning and benchmarks | `project.created`, `roadmap.created`, `benchmark.ran` |
| Scoring | `score.invalid_label` |
| Admin | `token.issued`, `secret.set` |

The audit log returns the newest entries first, 200 by default.

Typed decisions have their own log with inputs, answers, action, provider, fallback and latency. See [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md#logs).

## Related pages

- [Teams and users](teams-and-users.md)
- [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](secrets-mcps-environments.md)

# Inbox

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/management/inbox.md

The inbox lists every open gate assigned to you across all factories, most urgent first, so you can approve, reject or answer in one place.

## What appears in the inbox

Each item is an open gate:

| Kind | Example title | You can |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spec | Approve the spec for "Team invites" | Approve or reject with feedback |
| Preview | Accept the preview of "Team invites" | Approve or reject with feedback. Only when a preview provider (Vercel) is configured. |
| Question | verify keeps failing on "Fix the nav" | Answer, approve to resume, or reject to cancel |
| Command approval | Allow implement to run a risky command? | Approve to run it, reject to block it |
| Review | Review "Team invites" | Read the diff, comment on lines, approve, request changes or merge, as your GitHub account |
| Custom | Legal sign-off | Approve or reject |

Each item shows its work item (title, state, factory, pull request, preview URL and spec), the question or details, and evidence links such as the spec pull request, the preview and the videos.

You see gates assigned to you, plus gates with no assignee. Assignees come from the gate's `approvers`; see [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md#gates).

## Reviewing a pull request

A Review item opens the diff in the side pane, file by file. Hover a line and click the comment button to leave a line comment; your comments go out together when you submit:

- **Approve** posts an approving review.
- **Request changes** posts the review and sends your summary and line comments to the agents, which revise the pull request.
- **Comment only** posts the line comments without a verdict.
- **Merge** merges the pull request; the task completes.

Kiln acts as your own GitHub account, never as the Kiln app (agents never approve or merge; see ADR-010). Link GitHub once from the pane or your linked accounts. If you merged elsewhere, **Confirm it landed** closes the task. On the run page, **Request changes** on the merge gate (or a follow-up message) sends your note to the agents without a GitHub review.

## Ready to merge

When the `review-risk` decision finds a change low risk and the reviewer agent has no findings, nobody needs to read the code, so no inbox item opens. The pull request appears under **Ready to merge** at the top of the inbox, and one click merges it as you. See [Decisions](../configuration/decisions.md).

## Order

The `inbox-urgency` decision gives each gate an urgency score when it opens. The inbox sorts by urgency, highest first, then by age, oldest first. If the decision is not available, questions get 0.7 and other gates 0.5.

## Deciding

The inbox, Slack and issue replies, the API and the Kiln MCP all call the same decision code. Each decision records:

- the decision (`approve`, `reject` or `answer`),
- your answer or feedback,
- who decided and through which surface (`web`, `slack`, `linear`, `jira`, `github`, `mcp`),
- when.

The decision is added to the work item's conversation and counted as a human touch, and the audit log gets an entry. Deciding a gate that is already closed changes nothing.

A reply in Slack or on an issue or pull request decides a gate only when its author is one of the gate's assignees, or the gate has none. See [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).

Only question gates take free-text answers. To decide through the inbox, the API or the MCP, your token needs the matching scope for the factory:

| Gate kind | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Spec | `decide:spec` |
| Preview | `decide:preview` |
| Question | `decide:question` |
| Merge and custom | `decide:merge` |

## Reminders and expiry

Gates with a `nudge` time post a reminder in the source thread at that interval, naming who the gate waits on. Gates with an `expire` time park, approve or reject on their own when it passes. The built-in spec and preview gates nudge every 24 hours and park after 72 hours. The merge gate nudges every 48 hours.

A command approval waits up to 30 minutes, then expires and the command is blocked.

## From the command line and MCP

`kiln inbox` lists your open gates. The Kiln MCP has `list_inbox` and `decide_gate`. See the [CLI reference](../developer-tools/cli.md) and the [MCP reference](../developer-tools/mcp.md).

## Weekly digest

The digest groups open gates by person, oldest first, with each one's age in hours and a link to it in the inbox.

## Inbox items API

`GET /api/v1/inbox/items` lists your inbox across factories as items of six kinds:

| Kind | When |
| --- | --- |
| `question` | An agent or the foreman asked you something. Questions can be single or multi select, with a recommended option. |
| `answer_question` | A question on your task was answered (for your information, for a week). |
| `spec_review` | A spec or plan waits for approval; also definition changes proposed by agents and self-improvement proposals, with their diff. |
| `pr_review` | A pull request or preview waits on you. |
| `blocked`, `failed` | A task of yours is stuck, when nothing else on it needs you. |

Filter with `scope=mine|team`, `factory`, `kind`, `read=true|false` and `q`. `POST /api/v1/inbox/read`, `/unread`, `/resolve` and `/unresolve` take `{ids}` (item ids, or plain gate ids). Items clear themselves when they stop being relevant: the question was answered, the spec approved, the PR merged.

Definition changes have their own actions: `POST /definition-changes/{id}/approve` (Approve & merge: applied at once for Kiln-managed factories, a pull request on the config repo otherwise), `/request-changes` (the comments go back to the agent that proposed it), `/comments` and `/reject`. Agents can never approve.

## Related pages

- [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md)
- [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md)

# Portfolio and projects

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/management/portfolio.md

A project groups the factories that serve one product or goal, and the portfolio rolls up their work, cost and pending decisions across every project. Projects and the portfolio are per team: a project's factories belong to one team, and you see the current team's projects. See [Teams and users](teams-and-users.md#current-team).

## Projects

A project has a name, an owner and a list of factories, for example "Customer portal" with `webapp`, `api` and `mobile`. Creating a project links each listed factory to it.

To create a project through the API, your token needs `send` on every factory in it. The creator becomes the owner.

A work item sent through the API can name a project.

Each project can hold one roadmap from the [plan agent](../product-owners/planning.md). Making a new plan replaces the project's current roadmap.

## The portfolio

For each project, the portfolio shows each factory's [metrics](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md) and these totals:

| Total | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| PRs opened | Work items with a pull request, across the project's factories |
| PRs merged | Work items completed by a merge |
| Cost | Run costs in USD |
| Active work items | Work items not yet complete, cancelled or failed |
| Pending decisions | Open gates in the project's factories |

Across all factories it also shows the number of factories, PRs merged, cost and active work items.

Metrics cover the last 30 days by default. You can pass another start date.

## Weekly digest

The digest tells each person which decisions are waiting on them, oldest first, with a link to each one. See [Inbox](inbox.md#weekly-digest).

## Related pages

- [Planning](../product-owners/planning.md)
- [Dashboard metrics](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md)
- [Inbox](inbox.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md)

# Secrets, MCP servers and environments

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/management/secrets-mcps-environments.md

Secrets, MCP servers and environments belong to a team. Agents use them by name, and Kiln resolves them for each run.

## Secrets

A secret has a scope, a name, a type, an optional description, and who created and last changed it and when. Values are write-only: the API returns metadata, never values. A value can be at most 128 KiB.

| Scope | Who manages it | Which runs get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `team` | Team owners and admins | Runs of the team's factories, when the agent asks for it |
| `personal` | You | Only runs you triggered: work you sent, or work whose requester resolves to your account |

When both scopes have a secret with the same name, a run you triggered gets your personal one.

### Types

| Type | Value | Gives the run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw` | a string | An environment variable named after the secret |
| `docker_registry` | `{ host, username, password }` | Nothing in the environment. It is a private image credential. See [Private images](#private-images). |
| `aws_ecr` | `{ roleArn, region }` (team scope only) | Nothing in the environment. It is an image credential. See [Private images](#private-images). |
| `anthropic_api_key` | a string | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `claude_oauth_token` | a string from `claude setup-token` | `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` |
| `chatgpt_auth` | Codex's `auth.json` from a ChatGPT sign-in (use **Sign in with ChatGPT** under Team settings → Model keys) | Nothing in the environment. Codex runs get it as their `auth.json`. See [ChatGPT logins](../infrastructure/harnesses.md#chatgpt-logins). |
| `anthropic_bedrock_api_key` | a string, or `{ apiKey, region }` | `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_REGION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` |
| `anthropic_bedrock_access_key` | `{ accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken?, region }` | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, `AWS_REGION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` |
| `openai_api_key` | a string | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `openrouter_api_key` | a string | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `google_api_key` | a string | `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` |

Kiln checks each value against its type. Secret names use letters, digits and underscores.

Manage secrets with `GET /api/v1/managed-secrets`, `POST /api/v1/managed-secrets`, `PATCH /api/v1/managed-secrets/<scope>/<name>` (new value or description) and `DELETE /api/v1/managed-secrets/<scope>/<name>`.

### How runs get secrets

- **Agent secrets:** an agent's `secrets` list names the secrets its runs get. Typed secrets give their provider variables. Agents get no secrets they do not list.
- **Harness credentials:** with `harness.auth: { source: secret, secretName: X }`, a typed secret `X` gives its provider variables. A raw secret goes to the harness's usual variable. Without `harness.auth`, Kiln picks the first credential the harness can use, from typed secrets and the names in [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md#credentials). Claude Code also accepts Bedrock credentials.
- **Lookup order** for a name: your personal secret (for runs you triggered), then the team secret, then the server's secrets (the older admin `PUT /api/v1/secrets/<name>` store, model-provider environment variables and `KILN_SECRET_<NAME>`).
- **Redaction:** Kiln replaces every secret value a run could see with `[redacted]` in its events, tool output and summary.
- **Encryption:** with `KILN_SECRET_KEY` set, values are sealed with AES-256-GCM in the store. Without it they are stored in plain text, so set it on any shared server.

### Team-managed model keys

Team owners and admins set one key per provider with `PUT /api/v1/teams/<team>/model-keys/<provider>`:

| Provider | Team secret | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | `KILN_MODEL_ANTHROPIC` | `anthropic_api_key` |
| `openai` | `KILN_MODEL_OPENAI` | `openai_api_key` |
| `openrouter` | `KILN_MODEL_OPENROUTER` | `openrouter_api_key` |
| `bedrock` | `KILN_MODEL_BEDROCK` | `anthropic_bedrock_access_key`, or `anthropic_bedrock_api_key` when you send an API key |

Runs without their own harness credential use these. `GET /api/v1/teams/<team>/model-keys` shows which keys are set.

## MCP servers ("MCPs and apps")

Team owners and admins register MCP servers for the team. Agents name them in `mcpServers`, by name or id.

```json
{ "name": "figma", "url": "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {{FIGMA_TOKEN}}" } }
{ "name": "sentry", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@sentry/mcp-server"], "env": { "SENTRY_TOKEN": "{{SENTRY_TOKEN}}" }, "mode": "direct" }
```

- A server has either `command` with `args` and `env`, or `url` with `headers`.
- `{{NAME}}` refers to a secret, looked up the same way as agent secrets.
- **Connection mode `managed`** (the default for URL servers): Kiln puts the secret values into the harness's MCP config.
- **Connection mode `direct`** (the default for command servers): the config keeps `${NAME}` references, and the values go into the run's environment. Values are never written to disk.
- A server whose secrets are missing, or a name Kiln does not know, is skipped. The run shows an `mcp_skipped` event.
- A run may reach the servers it gets: the host of a URL server, and the host of any URL-valued secret a server uses (such as `JIRA_BASE_URL`), are added to its egress allowlist.

### Templates

**New** under MCPs and apps, or **Add MCP** on an agent, offers templates for common servers: observability (SigNoz, Datadog, New Relic, Better Stack), Sentry, Figma, Linear, GitHub, Playwright and Postgres. A template asks for what the server needs, one labeled field each, with where to find the value. Keys are saved as team secrets and the server is registered for the team under the template's name, so any agent can list it. Anything else is a custom server: paste its JSON.

### Testing servers

**Test** connects to a server with the team's secrets the way a harness would (MCP `initialize`, then `tools/list`) and shows its tools, or what went wrong: refused credentials, a wrong path, an unreachable host or a missing secret. The same test runs in every scope:

| Where | What it tests |
| --- | --- |
| MCPs and apps → **Test all**, or **Test** on a row | The team's servers, or one of them |
| Factory settings → agent and scorer defaults | The servers in the list, with the factory team's secrets |
| An agent's settings | That agent's servers |

API: `POST /api/v1/mcp-servers/test` with `{}` (the team, admins only), `{ "factory": "<id>" }`, `{ "factory": "<id>", "agent": "<name>" }`, and optionally `"servers": ["<name>"]` to narrow any of them. Command servers start only inside a run's sandbox, so their test checks their secrets and reports `untested`. Kiln never tests servers on `localhost`, loopback or link-local addresses (such as the cloud metadata service).

### Built-in integration servers

These servers can be referenced by id without registering them. They are listed as connected once their secrets exist in the team or on the server.

| `kiln_id` | Server | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `linear` | Linear's hosted MCP | `LINEAR_API_KEY` |
| `slack` | `@modelcontextprotocol/server-slack` | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` |
| `jira` | `mcp-atlassian` | `JIRA_BASE_URL`, `JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN` |
| `github` | GitHub's hosted MCP | `GITHUB_MCP_TOKEN` (use a read-mostly token; agents never get merge rights) |
| `discord` | `mcp-discord` | `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` |

Every run also gets the Kiln MCP server with its own run token.

## Environments

An environment is a team template: a Docker image, repositories, setup commands and secrets. Point a factory at one with `environmentId` in `agentDefaults`, an agent or an automation. You can use the id or the name. The most specific setting wins.

```yaml
# factory.yaml
agentDefaults:
  harness: { type: claude-code }
  environmentId: node-24
```

At run time:

- The image is used when the agent names no runner.
- The environment's repositories are cloned next to the factory's.
- Its setup commands run after the runner's setup commands.
- Its secrets are added to the agent's secrets.
- An `environmentId` that the team does not have stops the run with a clear error.

Manage environments with `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/v1/environments`.

## Private images

A runner pulls a private image with a team secret of type `docker_registry` or `aws_ecr`:

```yaml
# runners/private.yaml
image: ghcr.io/acme/runner:2
backend: docker
platform:
  linux:
    registryCredentialSecretName: GHCR
```

An environment does the same with `registryCredentialSecretName` next to its `image`. That credential is used when the agent names no runner.

- **`docker_registry`:** the secret's `host` must be the image's registry. Bare names such as `acme/runner` are on Docker Hub (`docker.io`).
- **`aws_ecr`:** the image must be on an ECR registry (`<account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com`). Kiln gets a short-lived password by running `aws ecr get-login-password --region <region>` on the server, with `AWS_ROLE_ARN` set to the secret's role. The server's AWS credentials must be allowed to call `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken`.
- **Docker** pulls with a temporary `DOCKER_CONFIG` that is deleted right after the pull. The credential never enters the container.
- **Kubernetes** gets a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret as the pod's `imagePullSecrets`. Kiln deletes it with the sandbox.

## Related pages

- [Teams and users](teams-and-users.md)
- [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md)
- [Agents](../configuration/agents.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md)

# Teams and users

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/management/teams-and-users.md

People sign in to Kiln with an account, work in one or more teams, and get a role on each factory. Every API request acts as a user, a team service account or a scoped token.

## Accounts and login

An account has a name, an email, an optional avatar and a password (stored as a salted scrypt hash) or a linked GitHub login.

- **Sign up:** `POST /api/v1/auth/signup` with `email`, `password` (at least 8 characters) and optionally `name` and `invite`.
- **Log in:** `POST /api/v1/auth/login` returns a session token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Sessions last 30 days.
- **Log out:** `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` revokes the session token.
- **GitHub login:** set `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` on the server, and use `<public URL>/api/v1/auth/github/callback` as the OAuth app's callback URL. `GET /api/v1/auth/github/start?redirect=<web URL>` sends people to GitHub. They come back to the web app with the session token in the URL fragment. Kiln finds the account by the linked GitHub id, then by verified email. If neither matches, it signs the person up under the rules below.

`GET /api/v1/auth/providers` tells a login page which methods are on and whether signup is open.

### Who may sign up

1. The first person to sign up becomes the owner of the default team.
2. After that, signing up needs an invite for the same email address.
3. With `KILN_OPEN_SIGNUP=1`, anyone may sign up and joins the default team as a member.

### Local development

With `KILN_DEV_AUTH=1`, requests without a token act as the seeded user `dev@kiln.local`. That user owns the default team and has `admin` on every factory. Requests that do send a token still act as that token, so you can try logins locally. Never turn dev auth on for a server others can reach.

The bootstrap admin token that the server prints on first start keeps working. It is a scoped token with `admin` on every factory, not a user.

## Teams

A team has a name, a slug, an avatar and settings. Each factory belongs to one team. Factories created before teams existed move into the default team on start.

| Team role | Can                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `owner`   | Everything an admin can, plus grant or take away ownership. A team always keeps at least one owner.                                                                               |
| `admin`   | Rename the team, manage members, invites, settings, team secrets, MCP servers, environments and model keys, and create agent and worker keys. Admin on every factory in the team. |
| `member`  | Use the team's factories with the team's default factory role, add personal secrets, create personal API keys.                                                                    |

Anyone with an account can create a team (`POST /api/v1/teams`) and becomes its owner.

### Current team

Requests act in one team at a time. Send `X-Kiln-Team: <team id or slug>` to choose it. Without the header, Kiln uses your first team. Factory lists, projects, the portfolio, the digest, the skills catalog, decision logs, secrets, MCP servers, environments and usage show the current team only. A project's factories must all belong to one team, and skills install only into factories of the publishing factory's team. Agent and worker keys always act in their own team.

The SDK sets the header with `client.withTeam("payments")`.

### Invites

Owners and admins invite people by email with a role (`POST /api/v1/teams/<team>/invites`). The response holds the invite link, `<web URL>/join?invite=<token>`. Kiln stores only a hash of the token.

- An invite expires after 7 days.
- **Resend** issues a new link and 7 more days. The old link stops working.
- **Revoke** cancels the invite.
- `GET /api/v1/invites/<token>` shows the team, email and role without logging in.
- People with an account accept with `POST /api/v1/invites/accept`. New people sign up with the `invite` field.
- Only owners can invite owners.

### Team settings

| Setting                                                           | Default           | What it does                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `spendLimit.monthlyUsd`                                           | `200`             | The monthly spend limit. See [Usage and spend limits](usage-and-spend-limits.md).                                           |
| `spendLimit.autoStop`                                             | `false`           | Refuse new runs once the limit is reached. When off, the limit is a soft warning.                                           |
| `githubOrgs`                                                      | `[]`              | Enabled GitHub orgs. When the list is not empty, the team's factories may only use GitHub repositories owned by these orgs. |
| `defaultSandboxHost`                                              | not set           | `local`, `docker` or `kubernetes`. Used for runs whose agent names no runner.                                               |
| `egressAllowlist`                                                 | `[]`              | Hosts added to every run's egress allowlist.                                                                                |
| `storage.artifacts`, `storage.transcripts`, `storage.attachments` | `{ kind: local }` | Where each kind of data goes. See [Data storage](#data-storage).                                                            |
| `defaultFactoryRole`                                              | `user`            | The factory role every member has on the team's factories: `none`, `user` or `editor`.                                      |

### Data storage

Each team chooses where three kinds of data go:

| Category      | What                                                           | Object keys                  |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `artifacts`   | Screenshots, recordings and reports that runs save             | `runs/<run id>/<file>`       |
| `transcripts` | Each run's events as JSON lines, written when the run finishes | `transcripts/<run id>.jsonl` |
| `attachments` | Files people attach to requests                                | `attachments/<team id>/…`    |

A target is one of:

- `{ kind: local }`: the server's object store (`KILN_DATA_DIR/objects`). This is the default.
- `{ kind: local, path: "acme/artifacts" }`: a folder under the server's storage root (`KILN_DATA_DIR/storage`). The path must stay inside the root.
- `{ kind: s3, bucket, region, endpoint?, prefix?, forcePathStyle?, accessKeyIdSecret?, secretAccessKeySecret? }`: an S3-compatible bucket, such as AWS S3, MinIO or Cloudflare R2. Kiln signs requests itself (SigV4). Put the access key in two team secrets and name them here. Without them Kiln uses the server's `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`. With an `endpoint`, Kiln uses path-style URLs unless `forcePathStyle: false`.

Kiln remembers where each object went, so changing the settings later does not lose anything. Existing objects are not moved. Check a target with `POST /api/v1/teams/<team>/storage/<category>/test`, which writes a small object and reads it back.

Team-managed model keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Bedrock) are team secrets with fixed names. See [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](secrets-mcps-environments.md#team-managed-model-keys).

## Factory roles

| Factory role | Can                                                                                                                                                                      | Scopes                                                             |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| User         | See the factory, send work, decide spec, preview and question gates, propose memories.                                                                                   | `read`, `send`, `decide:spec`, `decide:preview`, `decide:question` |
| Editor       | Everything a User can, plus edit the definition, agents, repos and automations, attach secrets, MCP servers and runners, and confirm merges.                             | adds `definitions:write`, `decide:merge`                           |
| Admin        | Everything, including factory members and forcing a definition change that waits for a second approval (`POST /api/v1/proposals/<id>/approve` with `{ "force": true }`). | `admin`                                                            |

Team owners and admins are always Admin. Members get the team's `defaultFactoryRole`, or a higher role from a factory membership. Manage factory memberships with `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/v1/factories/<id>/members`. The person must be in the factory's team first.

Kiln turns roles into the same per-factory scopes that tokens use, when each request arrives. Every route checks scopes the same way for users and tokens. See [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md).

Team-wide actions, and applying a definition for a factory that does not exist yet, are decided by the team role. Members may read and send. Owners and admins may do everything.

## API keys

Create keys in user settings (`POST /api/v1/api-keys`). Keys use the `kiln_` format and are shown once.

| Type       | Acts as                                                                                                               | Who creates it         |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `personal` | You, with your roles. Usage counts as yours.                                                                          | Anyone                 |
| `agent`    | A team service account: `read` and `send` on the team's factories, never decide or merge. Usage counts as the team's. | Team owners and admins |
| `worker`   | A self-hosted worker. It has no API scopes.                                                                           | Team owners and admins |

Expiry is `1d`, `30d` (the default), `90d` or `never`. The key list shows when each key was last used. Revoke a key with `DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/<id>`. Team owners and admins also see and revoke the team's agent and worker keys.

## User settings

`PATCH /api/v1/me` changes:

- `name` and `email`.
- `avatar`: a URL, or `null` to clear it. You can also upload an image with `PUT /api/v1/me/avatar` (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG, at most 1 MiB).
- `appearance`: `light`, `dark` or `system`.
- `notifications`: for each kind (`spec`, `preview`, `question`, `merge` (pull request review), `custom`, `blocked`, `failed`), whether to notify by `email`, `slack` and `discord`.
- `digest`: `{ daily, hourUtc, channels, only }`. With `daily: true`, Kiln sends one summary of the decisions waiting on you each day at or after `hourUtc`. With `only: true`, it sends nothing right away.

Change your password with `PUT /api/v1/me/password`.

### Notifications

When a gate opens (a spec, preview, question, pull request review or custom decision), Kiln notifies its assignees. When work moves to `blocked` or `failed`, it notifies the requester. Only people with an account are notified, and only on the channels their preferences allow:

- **Email:** set `KILN_SMTP_URL` on the server, for example `smtp://user:password@mail.acme.test:587?from=kiln@acme.test`, or `smtps://…:465` for implicit TLS. Kiln upgrades to STARTTLS when the server offers it. `KILN_MAIL_FROM` sets the sender.
- **Slack and Discord:** a direct message to your linked account, through the chat integration for that provider.

`GET /api/v1/me/notifications` lists what Kiln sent you and whether it arrived. Failed deliveries are also in the audit log as `notify.failed`.

In the web app, **Settings → Notifications** has the same controls: a channel grid for each kind, the daily digest (on or off, the hour in UTC, its channels, and digest only), and the 20 most recent deliveries with their status. The Appearance choice in the account menu is saved to your account too, so another browser picks it up.

`GET /api/v1/me` returns your user, your teams, the current team, your role in it, your role on each factory, and the token's grants.

### Linked accounts

Linked accounts tell Kiln who you are on other systems. Supported providers: `github`, `slack`, `discord`, `linear`, `jira`, `teams`, `gitlab` and `azure_devops`.

- Link one with `POST /api/v1/me/linked-accounts` and `{ "provider": "slack", "externalId": "U024BE7LH" }`. Add `handle` for a login name such as a GitHub username.
- Unlink with `DELETE /api/v1/me/linked-accounts/<provider>`.
- One external account belongs to one user.

When an event arrives, for example a Slack reply in a work item's thread, Kiln looks up the author:

1. A linked account.
2. The server's `identities` option.
3. An email that matches an account. Linear and Jira send emails.

The result becomes the work item's requester and the person who decides a gate from a reply. GitHub login links your GitHub account automatically.

## Related pages

- [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md)
- [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](secrets-mcps-environments.md)
- [Usage and spend limits](usage-and-spend-limits.md)

# Usage and spend limits

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/management/usage-and-spend-limits.md

Kiln is self-hosted, so there are no plans or credits. It records what runs cost and lets each team set a monthly spend limit.

## Usage

Every run records its cost, its factory, agent and model, the team it counts toward and, when there is one, the user who triggered it. Runs started by agent keys, schedules or people without an account count as `team`.

`GET /api/v1/usage` returns the current team's usage for the current calendar month (UTC), or for `since` and `until`:

| Field | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `totalUsd`, `runs` | Totals for the period |
| `limit` | `monthlyUsd`, `autoStop`, `spentThisMonthUsd`, `remainingUsd`, `exceeded` |
| `byDay` | Cost and runs per day |
| `byFactory`, `byAgent`, `byModel`, `byUser` | Cost and runs per factory, `factory/agent`, model and user, highest first |
| `entries` | With `entries=1`: the ledger rows, one per run, newest first (at most 1000) |

Filter with `factory=<id>` and `user=<email or user id>`. Costs are what the harness reports. They are for comparing, not invoices.

## Spend limit

Each team has a monthly spend limit, $200 by default. Team owners and admins change it in the team settings:

```json
{ "spendLimit": { "monthlyUsd": 500, "autoStop": true } }
```

- With `autoStop` off (the default), the limit is soft. Runs continue, and `limit.exceeded` shows it was passed.
- With `autoStop` on, once the month's spend reaches the limit, Kiln refuses new runs, and the API refuses new work items with `402`:

```json
{ "error": "budget_exceeded", "message": "Monthly spending budget of $500 has been reached ($512.40 spent)", "limitUsd": 500, "spentUsd": 512.4 }
```

Work items already in progress, or started by webhooks and schedules, move to `blocked` before their next run, with the same message as the reason. Raise the limit or turn off auto-stop to continue. Factory budgets (`budgets.perWorkItemUsd`, `budgets.monthlyUsd`) and policy caps still apply as well. See [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md).

## Related pages

- [Teams and users](teams-and-users.md)
- [Metrics](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md)
- [API reference](../developer-tools/api.md)

# Benchmarks

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/measure-and-improve/benchmarks.md

A benchmark runs the same tasks, each pinned to exact commits, under up to six configurations of one agent, so you can compare success rate and cost before changing models or skills.

## A suite

```text
benchmarks/core/suite.yaml
benchmarks/core/tasks/t0.yaml
benchmarks/core/tasks/t1.yaml
```

```yaml
# benchmarks/core/suite.yaml
name: core
agent: implement
configurations:
  - { name: sonnet }
  - { name: haiku, agents: [{ agent: implement, model: claude-haiku-5-5 }] }
  - { name: codex, agents: [{ agent: implement, harness: { type: codex } }] }
tasks: [t0, t1]
```

| Key | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `name`, `description` | |
| `agent` | The agent under test. Must exist. |
| `configurations` | 1 to 6, with unique names. A configuration without `agents` uses the agent as defined. An entry for the suite's agent overrides its `model` or `harness`. `runner` names the runner for agents that do not set one. |
| `tasks` | Task names. Each needs `tasks/<name>.yaml` in the suite folder. |

## A task

```yaml
# benchmarks/core/tasks/t0.yaml
title: Add a footer link to the pricing page
prompt: "# Add a footer link to the pricing page"
successCriteria:
  - The footer links to /pricing
  - The link test passes
startingRepoRefs:
  - github.com:acme/web@3f2c1a9e5b7d4c6a8e0f1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e
sourceRunId: run_abc123
tags: [easy]
```

| Key | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `title`, `prompt` | Required. |
| `successCriteria` | At least one. |
| `startingRepoRefs` | At least one, in the form `github.com:<owner>/<repo>@<40-character commit SHA>` (or `gitlab.com:`). |
| `sourceRunId` | Optional. The run the task was saved from. |
| `tags` | Optional. Used to group tasks when suggesting routing rules. |

## Saving tasks from real work

Any finished run can be saved as a benchmark task. Kiln takes the run's prompt, the exact commit each repository started at, and the work item's acceptance criteria as success criteria (or a default criterion when there are none). It returns the task file for you to add to your suite.

## Running a suite

`kiln bench run <suite>` runs every task under every configuration, at the pinned commits, without pushing anything. Each run is judged against the task's success criteria with the labels `success` and `failure`. A task succeeds when the run succeeded and the judge says `success`.

For each configuration, Kiln reports the number of tasks, the success rate, the average cost and the average duration, and marks whether it is on the **Pareto frontier**: no other configuration is at least as good on both success rate and cost and better on one.

Benchmarks cost real money. Run them when models, skills or instructions change, not on every commit.

## From results to routing rules

Kiln can suggest routing rules from a suite's results. For each task tag, it takes the cheapest configuration that matches the best success rate for that tag. When that configuration uses a different model than the agent's default, it becomes a rule in a `prompt` router:

```yaml
# routers/by-task.yaml
name: by-task
type: prompt
default: claude-sonnet-5-5
routing:
  - { description: easy tasks, model: claude-haiku-5-5 }
```

For a config-repo factory, Kiln opens this as a pull request labeled `kiln:benchmarks`. To use it, point the agent at it with `model: router:by-task`.

## Benchmark runs, trials and results

The benchmarks page and API run suites with more control than `kiln bench run`:

- Suites and tasks: `GET|POST /factories/{id}/benchmark-suites`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE …/benchmark-suites/{suite}`, and `…/{suite}/tasks[/{task}]`. Adding a task with the same content again is a no-op; another task with the same title is a conflict. `POST /runs/{id}/benchmark-task` turns a finished run into a task.
- `POST …/benchmark-suites/{suite}/runs {configurations, repetitions, scorers, tasks}` starts a benchmark run. Each configuration sets, per agent, the harness and model (or a `router:<slug>`) and the runner. Every task × configuration × repetition is a **trial**: an agent run of kind `benchmark` with source `BENCHMARK_TRIAL`. The run freezes its inputs; it is not idempotent.
- After the trials, each is scored for task correctness and with the scorers you picked. `GET /benchmark-runs/{id}/results` returns per-configuration averages, an overall score, cost and duration, the Pareto frontier, chart points (quality against cost), spend (execution and judging), coverage and a short narrative, plus a recommendation: **highest quality**, **most efficient** (quality per second) and **lowest cost**.
- `GET /benchmark-runs/{id}/trials` (filter by task, configuration or `agent_run_id`) and `POST /benchmark-runs/{id}/cancel`.

## Related pages

- [Scorers](scorers.md)
- [Replay and canary](replay-and-canary.md)
- [Factory agents](../configuration/agents.md#routers)
- [CLI reference](../developer-tools/cli.md)

# Dashboard metrics

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/measure-and-improve/metrics.md

Kiln computes every factory metric from stored work items, runs and scores, so the dashboard, the API and the Kiln MCP always show the same numbers.

## The window

Metrics cover work items and runs created in a window, by default the last 30 days. You can pass another start date. You can also limit run metrics to one agent.

## Factory metrics

| Metric | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| PRs opened | Work items in the window that have a pull request. |
| PRs merged | Work items that are `complete` because their pull request merged. |
| Autonomy | The share of merged work items whose only human touch was the original request. |
| Autonomous merged | The number of those work items. |
| Human touches per PR | The average number of human touches on work items with a pull request. |
| Cycle time (median) | The median hours from a merged work item's creation to its completion. |
| Cost | The sum of run costs in the window, in USD. |
| Cost per merged PR | Cost divided by PRs merged. Empty when nothing merged. |
| Work items | Total, active, complete, blocked and cancelled counts. |

A **human touch** is the original request, every message a person adds, every gate decision and every steering message.

Values are rounded to two decimals.

## Per agent

For each agent with runs in the window:

| Metric | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Runs | Number of runs. |
| Cost | Sum of the agent's run costs. |
| Cost per merged PR | The agent's cost divided by the number of merged work items it worked on. |
| Scored | Number of scores for the agent's runs. |
| Pass rate | Share of those scores that passed. |

## Per definition

For each definition SHA used by work items in the window: the number of work items, the pass rate of scores recorded under it, and the cost of runs under it. During a [canary](replay-and-canary.md), this is how you compare the candidate with the applied definition.

## Across factories

The [portfolio](../management/portfolio.md) adds these metrics up per project and across all factories.

## Raw data

For your own views, Kiln returns the raw rows for runs, scores or work items of a factory since a date. An agent can use the Kiln MCP's metrics tools to answer questions such as "cost per merged PR by agent last week". See the [API overview](../developer-tools/api.md) and the [MCP reference](../developer-tools/mcp.md).

## Dashboard API

The dashboard reads these endpoints. All take `start_date` (inclusive) and `end_date` (exclusive) as RFC 3339 times, default to the last 30 days, and with `group_by_period=day|week|month` (weeks start on Sunday) add a `series`. Most add `deltas` against the previous period of the same length.

| Endpoint | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /factories/{id}/metrics` | `runCount`, `prCount`, `mergedPrCount`, `autonomy`, the autonomy funnel (merged, merged without a human code change, per repo), impact (additions and deletions of merged PRs), PR latency medians (kickoff → PR → first review → merge), average human interactions per PR. |
| `GET /factories/{id}/costs/per-pr` | PRs opened in the range, total, mean and median cost. With your own keys all spend is `inference`. |
| `GET /factories/{id}/costs/breakdown?group_by=source\|user\|agent\|model` | Spend per group. `source` and `user` roll up to the root run. |
| `GET /factories/{id}/costs/per-pr/top?limit=20` | The most expensive PRs. |
| `GET /factories/{id}/costs/per-pr/by-size` | Cost by PR size: S < 100, M < 500, L < 1000, XL ≥ 1000 changed lines. |
| `GET /factories/{id}/metrics/run-breakdown?group_by=agent_type\|status\|source\|root_vs_subrun\|model\|harness` | Run counts per group (source counts top-level runs only). |
| `GET /factories/{id}/pull-requests` | Every PR the factory produced: state, timing, size, human interactions, runs and cycle times; filter by `repo`, `state`, opened/merged dates and `updated_after` for incremental sync. |

A PR counts as autonomous when no person pushed code to it; handing a task back from a local worktree marks its PR as changed by a person.

## Related pages

- [Scorers](scorers.md)
- [Replay and canary](replay-and-canary.md)
- [Portfolio and projects](../management/portfolio.md)
- [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md)

# Replay and canary

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md

Replay re-runs a past agent run from exactly where it started, optionally under a different definition, and canary apply sends only a share of new work items to a candidate definition so you can compare it with the current one.

## What a run saves

Every run records:

- the definition SHA it ran under,
- the agent, harness and model,
- the prompt and the full instructions the agent received,
- the skills it received,
- for each repository, the branch and the exact commit it started at,
- for local sandboxes, a hash of the starting workspace.

This is the run's start state.

## Replay

`kiln replay <run> --with <sha>` starts a new run of the same agent with the same prompt, checked out at the same commits. Without `--with`, it uses the run's own definition SHA. See the [CLI reference](../developer-tools/cli.md).

- The replay is a run of kind `replay` that links back to the original.
- It does not push anything.
- A replay of a local-sandbox run starts from a workspace with the same hash as the original.

Use replay to:

- check whether a definition change fixes a failure, before you apply it,
- reproduce a bad run while you debug,
- compare two definitions on the same inputs.

[Self-improvement](self-improvement.md) uses replay to prove every proposal: it replays up to 30 failing runs under the applied and the proposed definition and reports both pass rates.

## Canary apply

`kiln apply --canary 10%` applies a valid tree as a candidate for 10% of new work items. The rest keep the applied definition.

- Each work item is assigned once, when it is created, by a stable hash of its ID. It keeps that definition for its whole life.
- A canary needs an applied definition to compare against, and a share below 100%. Otherwise the tree is applied normally.
- Applying another canary replaces the current one.

### Watching a canary

[Dashboard metrics](metrics.md) split work items, pass rate and cost by definition SHA. Compare the candidate's row with the applied one.

### Promote or roll back

You can promote the candidate to 100%, or roll it back, at any time.

Kiln also decides on its own after 7 days:

| Candidate's pass rate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| At least the applied definition's pass rate minus 2 points | Promoted. It becomes the applied definition. |
| Lower | Rolled back. New work items go back to the applied definition. |
| No scores yet | Rolled back. |

If the applied definition has no scores, a candidate with scores is promoted.

Approving a self-improvement proposal in Kiln, or merging its pull request unchanged in a config repo, starts a 10% canary in the same way.

## Related pages

- [Self-improvement](self-improvement.md)
- [Dashboard metrics](metrics.md)
- [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#canary-apply)
- [Scorers](scorers.md)

# Scorers

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/measure-and-improve/scorers.md

A scorer is a rubric in `scorers/<name>/scorer.md` that grades a share of an agent's finished runs with one of a fixed set of labels.

## A scorer file

```markdown
---
name: acceptance-criteria
description: Checks whether the change meets its acceptance criteria
agents: [implement]
labels:
  - { value: meets, score: 1, description: Every criterion has a passing test }
  - { value: partly, score: 0.5 }
  - { value: misses, score: 0 }
passingScore: 0.8
samplingRate: 25
model: claude-haiku-5-5
selfImprovement: true
---
Pass "meets" only if every acceptance criterion has a passing test or evidence.
Use "partly" when some criteria are covered. Use "misses" when a criterion has no evidence.
```

| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | The scorer's name on scores. |
| `description` | none | |
| `agents` | required | Agents whose runs it grades. Each must exist. |
| `labels` | required | 1 to 20 labels, each with a unique `value`, a `score` from 0 to 1 and an optional `description`. |
| `passingScore` | required | 0 to 1. A label passes when its score is at least this. |
| `samplingRate` | 25 | Percent of runs to grade, 0 to 100. |
| `model` | required | The model for an LLM judge. The default typed-decision judge does not use it. |
| `selfImprovement` | `false` | When true, failed scores feed [self-improvement](self-improvement.md). |

The body is the rubric the judge reads.

## Which runs are scored

When a work run finishes, Kiln scores it with every scorer that lists its agent.

- Sampling is by a stable hash of the run ID and the scorer name, so the same run is always in or out of the sample for that scorer. About `samplingRate` percent of runs are scored.
- Replays and benchmark runs ignore sampling: when Kiln scores them, every scorer for the agent grades them.
- The server can be set to score every run, ignoring `samplingRate`.
- A run is scored at most once per scorer.

## How a run is judged

The judge gets the rubric, the run's summary, its result file, the last part of its event transcript and the agent's name, and picks one label.

By default the judge is a [typed decision](../configuration/decisions.md): the labels become the options of one choice question, so judging is cheap enough to score many more runs. When the top label's probability is below 0.7 and an LLM judge is configured, the run goes to the LLM judge instead.

A label that is not in the scorer's list is not recorded; Kiln writes an `invalid_label` entry to the audit log.

## Scores

Each score records the run, factory, agent, scorer, label, numeric score, pass or fail, the judge's rationale, which judge decided, and the definition SHA the run used. Scores from work runs of a scorer with `selfImprovement: true` count toward self-improvement until a proposal marks them reviewed.

Use scores in:

- [Dashboard metrics](metrics.md): pass rate per agent and per definition,
- [Self-improvement](self-improvement.md): unreviewed failures trigger a proposal,
- [Replay and canary](replay-and-canary.md): pass rates before and after a change.

## Default scorers

A factory made with the setup wizard starts with five scorers, each with a written rubric you can edit: **Verbosity**, **Task Compliance**, **Procedure Compliance**, **Efficiency** and **Code Quality** (implement agent only). Task Compliance, Procedure Compliance and Code Quality feed self-improvement. A sixth, **Task Correctness** (`kind: benchmark_task_correctness`), grades benchmark trials against their success criteria and never scores everyday runs.

Two more scorer keys: `agents` entries may be `{ name, includeDescendants: true }` to include a run's subagents as evidence, and `runner`, `secrets` and `mcpServers` set up the judge.

## Scorers API

- `GET|POST /factories/{id}/scorers`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /factories/{id}/scorers/{slug}`: the UI's scorer editor. Writes go into `scorers/<slug>/scorer.md` (a pull request for config-repo factories). Each update bumps the scorer's `version`; deleting removes its scores too. Creating a scorer does not score past runs.
- `GET …/scorers/{slug}/results` (with `include_reasons=true`, `run_id=`) and `GET …/scorers/{slug}/metrics` (pass rate and series; `include_cost=true` adds judge cost).
- Manual scoring, which ignores sampling and replaces earlier scores: `POST …/scorers/{slug}/dispatch {runIds}`, `POST /factories/{id}/runs/{runId}/scorer-dispatch {scorers}`, or `POST /runs/{id}/score` for every scorer that covers the run's agent.
- `GET /runs/{id}/scores` lists a run's scores with `triggerSource` (`automatic` or `manual`).

## Related pages

- [Self-improvement](self-improvement.md)
- [Dashboard metrics](metrics.md)
- [Benchmarks](benchmarks.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)

# Self-improvement

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md

Self-improvement turns an agent's repeated failures into a proposed change to the factory's definition, replays the failing runs to show whether the change helps, and opens it for a person to review.

## Turn it on

1. Add a scorer with `selfImprovement: true` for the agents you want to improve. See [Scorers](scorers.md).
2. Optionally tune `selfImprovement` in `factory.yaml`:

```yaml
selfImprovement:
  failedRunThreshold: 25   # 1–50, default 25
  maxAgeDays: 7            # 1–90, default 7
  reviewers: { type: team }
```

`reviewers` is validated (`custom` needs at least one email) but does not assign reviewers to proposals yet. Use your config repo's code owners for that.

3. Protect what the loop must not touch with a [policy](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md).

## When it runs

A scheduled check looks at each agent's unreviewed failed scores from scorers with `selfImprovement: true`. It starts a proposal for an agent when either:

- the failures cover at least `failedRunThreshold` distinct runs, or
- the oldest failure is at least `maxAgeDays` days old.

**Run now** skips the wait and starts a proposal for every agent with at least one failure.

## How a proposal is made

1. **Cluster.** The `failure-category` decision tags each failed run as `instructions`, `skills`, `tooling`, `model`, `app_code` or `flaky`. Kiln takes the largest group.
2. **Propose.** The improver reads that group and the reviewers' earlier rejections for this agent, and proposes file changes. By default it adds a "Lessons from reviewed failures" section to the agent's instructions and never repeats a lesson a reviewer rejected. It can also be the factory's `improver` agent, which edits a copy of the definition tree in its sandbox.
3. **Guard.** Kiln drops changes to `policies/`, `gates/` and any `protectedPaths`, and lists what it dropped. If nothing is left, or the changed tree does not validate, there is no proposal.
4. **Replay.** Kiln replays up to 30 of the failing runs twice from their saved start state: once under the applied definition and once under the proposed one. Each replay is scored, and a replay passes when all its scores pass.
5. **Open.** The proposal body has the rationale, a "Regressions addressed" list linking each failed run and its score, a "Replay" table with pass or fail before and after and the two pass rates, and the list of changed files. Kiln never opens a proposal without the replay report.

The failures in the proposal are marked reviewed, so they do not trigger another proposal.

## Reviewing a proposal

For a factory with a [config repo](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#config-repos-on-github), Kiln commits the change to a `kiln/self-improve-<agent>-<id>` branch and opens a pull request titled "Self-improvement: <agent> (<category>)", labeled `kiln:self-improvement`. Merging it ships the change as a [canary](replay-and-canary.md): when the pushed tree is exactly the proposal's candidate, the push sync applies it to 10% of new work items (the server's default share) and marks the proposal merged. If the branch was edited before the merge, the tree no longer matches and the push applies it to all new work items, like any other change.

In Kiln, you can approve or reject any proposal:

- **Approve.** Kiln applies the proposed tree as a 10% [canary](replay-and-canary.md). If the change touches a `twoApprovalPaths` path, two different people must approve first. Agents cannot approve.
- **Reject**, with a reason. Rejected proposals are kept as negative examples for the improver.

Nothing is adopted without a person's review.

## Improving Kiln's own factory

The same loop runs on the factory that builds Kiln. See [Kiln builds Kiln](../guides/kiln-builds-kiln.md).

## Settings

| Key (`selfImprovement` in factory.yaml) | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Scheduled checks run. "Run now" works either way. |
| `failedRunThreshold` | `25` | Distinct unreviewed failures (1–50) of one agent that start a proposal. |
| `maxAgeDays` | `7` | Or when the oldest unreviewed failure is this old. |
| `reviewers` | `admins` | Pool for the one reviewer each proposal asks: `admins`, `team`, `custom` (with `emails`) or `none`. |
| `model` | the improver agent's | Model for the analysis run. |

Which scorers feed it is each scorer's `selfImprovement` toggle. `GET|PUT /factories/{id}/self-improvement/settings` reads and changes all of these in one change. Proposals show up in the inbox as spec reviews, and every proposal's description has a **Regressions addressed** section linking the failing runs and scores.

## Related pages

- [Scorers](scorers.md)
- [Replay and canary](replay-and-canary.md)
- [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md)
- [Make a factory improve itself](../guides/make-a-factory-improve-itself.md)

# Concepts

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/overview/concepts.md

This glossary defines each Kiln term in one or two sentences and links to the page that covers it.

## Factories and work

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| **Factory** | A team of agents attached to the repositories that ship together, defined by a tree rooted at `factory.yaml`. See [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md). |
| **Alias** | The factory's handle, such as `webapp`. People reach the foreman with `@webapp` in Slack, GitHub, Linear or Jira. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 60 characters. |
| **Work item** | One request, from intake to completion. It keeps its source, conversation, branch, pull request, cost and the definition SHA it runs under. See [How Kiln works](how-kiln-works.md). |
| **Foreman** | The agent with `agentType: FOREMAN`. It coordinates work items and chooses the path when no pipeline is set. A factory has exactly one. |
| **Agent** | A role in the factory, defined in `agents/<name>/agent.md` with an `agentType`, a harness or model, and instructions. See [Factory agents](../configuration/agents.md). |
| **Stage** | One step of a work item's path: triage, spec, build, verify, preview, review or hand-off. |
| **Pipeline** | An optional, fixed list of stages in `pipelines/<name>.yaml`. See [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md). |
| **Gate** | A pause where a person decides: spec approval, preview acceptance, a question, command approval or merge. Open gates make up the [inbox](../management/inbox.md). |
| **Hand-off** | The last stage. The pull request is marked ready and a person is asked to merge it. |
| **Project** | A group of factories for planning and reporting. See [Portfolio and projects](../management/portfolio.md). |
| **Roadmap** | Epics and issues the planning agent produces from a goal or PRD. See [Planning](../product-owners/planning.md). |

## Configuration

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| **Definition tree** | All files that define a factory: `factory.yaml`, `agents/`, `automations/`, `pipelines/`, `gates/`, `policies/`, `decisions/`, `runners/`, `routers/`, `scorers/`, `benchmarks/`, `skills/`, `webhooks/` and `memories/`. |
| **Definition SHA** | A 40-character content hash of the whole tree. Kiln stores every applied tree by this SHA, and every run records it. |
| **Applied definition** | The tree new work items use. Kiln applies a tree whole or not at all; an invalid tree leaves the previous one active. |
| **Config repo** | A GitHub repository that holds the definition tree. Merges to its branch apply the new tree. |
| **Automation** | A trigger file that starts work from an event. See [Automations](../configuration/automations.md). |
| **Skill** | A `SKILL.md` file with know-how that Kiln hands to agents. See [Skills](../configuration/skills.md). |
| **Memory** | A learned convention stored as `memories/<slug>.md` and added to later runs. See [Skills](../configuration/skills.md#memories). |
| **Runner** | Compute settings for an agent's sandbox: image, backend, shape, setup commands and egress. See [Sandboxes](../infrastructure/sandboxes.md). |
| **Router** | A file in `routers/` that picks a model per task, by complexity or by prompt. Agents use it with `model: router:<name>`. |
| **Policy** | Rules in `policies/<name>.yaml`, such as paths self-improvement may not change. See [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md). |
| **Decision** | A typed question set with thresholds, in `decisions/<name>.yaml`. See [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md). |
| **Expression** | The small language used by `skip_if`, gate rules and decision policies. See [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md#expression-language). |

## Runs and safety

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| **Run** | One agent session in one sandbox. It records the agent, harness, model, definition SHA, start state, events, cost and outcome. |
| **Harness** | The coding agent program a run uses: `claude-code`, `codex` or `opencode`. See [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md). |
| **Sandbox** | The disposable environment a run works in: local directory, Docker container or Kubernetes pod. |
| **Start state** | What a run started from: prompt, instructions, skills and the exact commit of each repository. Replays start from it. |
| **Result file** | `.kiln/result.json`, which the agent writes at the end of a run to report structured results. See [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md#the-result-file). |
| **Run token** | A short-lived token for one run. It can push only `kiln/*` branches of the factory's repositories, open pull requests, comment and label. It can never approve or merge. |
| **Command guard** | The check that rates shell commands before they run and allows, asks a person or blocks. |
| **Steering** | A message sent to a running agent that it reads before its next step. |
| **Scope** | A permission on an API or MCP token, granted per factory. See [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md). |

## Measure and improve

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| **Scorer** | A rubric with labels that grades a share of an agent's runs. See [Scorers](../measure-and-improve/scorers.md). |
| **Score** | One scorer's label for one run, with a pass or fail against the scorer's `passingScore`. |
| **Self-improvement** | The loop that turns unreviewed failures into a proposed definition change, proven by replay. See [Self-improvement](../measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md). |
| **Proposal** | A self-improvement change with its replay report, opened as a pull request or kept for review in Kiln. |
| **Replay** | A new run from a saved start state, optionally under another definition. |
| **Canary** | A candidate definition that only a share of new work items use, so you can compare it to the applied one. |
| **Benchmark** | A suite of tasks pinned to exact commits, run under up to six configurations. See [Benchmarks](../measure-and-improve/benchmarks.md). |
| **Autonomy** | The share of merged pull requests whose only human touch was the original request. See [Metrics](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md). |

## Related pages

- [What is Kiln](what-is-kiln.md)
- [How Kiln works](how-kiln-works.md)
- [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md)

---

# How Kiln works

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/kiln/blob/main/docs/site/overview/how-kiln-works.md

Every request becomes a work item that moves through a fixed set of states, from `received` to `complete`, and only a merge or a person's confirmation can complete it.

## Intake

A work item starts when an automation trigger matches an event, for example a GitHub issue labeled `kiln-ready`, a Slack mention of `@webapp`, a Linear agent session, a Jira issue, a schedule or a webhook. It can also start from the API, the CLI (`kiln send`) or the Kiln MCP (`send_task`).

The work item keeps its source: the Slack channel and thread, the issue, or the pull request. Kiln posts updates there. Replies in the same thread or on the same issue continue the same work item instead of starting a new one.

Each work item records the definition SHA it runs under. During a [canary](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md), some new work items get the candidate definition and the rest get the applied one.

## The foreman's default path

When the factory has no pipeline, or the work item names none, the foreman builds the path:

1. **Triage.** Kiln asks the `triage` decision for the kind (`feature`, `bug`, `chore`, `incident`, `question`) and size (`xs` to `xl`). If both answers have a probability of at least 0.6, Kiln uses them. Otherwise the `TRIAGE` agent classifies the request.
2. **Spec, when needed.** The `foreman-routing` decision answers `needs_spec`. At 0.85 or more, the item gets a spec. At 0.15 or less, it skips the spec. In between, the `FOREMAN` agent decides. If no answer comes back, sizes `m`, `l` and `xl` get a spec.
3. **Build.** The `IMPLEMENT` agent makes the change on a `kiln/<id>-<title>` branch.
4. **Verify.** The `VERIFY` agent checks the change, and Kiln waits for CI to pass. A failure loops back to build, up to 3 times.
5. **Preview.** If a preview provider is configured, Kiln deploys the branch and asks for preview acceptance.
6. **Review.** The `REVIEW` agent reviews the pull request. The review is advisory: `changes_requested` with findings loops back to build, up to 2 times. After that, Kiln posts the remaining findings on the pull request as "Advisory review findings:" and goes on to hand-off.
7. **Hand-off.** Kiln marks the pull request ready, labels it `factory:<alias>`, posts "Ready to merge" to the source thread, and opens a merge gate.

Spec and review are left out when the factory has no `SPEC` or `REVIEW` agent. Without a `VERIFY` agent, the verify stage only waits for CI. Build falls back to a `CUSTOM` agent, then to the foreman. A [pipeline](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md) replaces this path with stages you list.

## States

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> received
    received --> triaging
    triaging --> planning: spec needed
    triaging --> building: spec skipped
    planning --> awaiting_spec: spec ready
    awaiting_spec --> building: approved
    awaiting_spec --> planning: changes requested
    building --> reviewing
    building --> awaiting_preview
    building --> handed_off
    awaiting_preview --> reviewing: accepted
    awaiting_preview --> building: rejected
    reviewing --> building: changes requested
    reviewing --> handed_off
    handed_off --> building: review comments on the PR
    handed_off --> complete: merged or confirmed
    complete --> [*]
```

Three more states sit beside the main path:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked` | The item is parked. Causes: a gate expired, a stage failed more than its `max_loops`, the build agent failed twice, the budget ran out, or an error stopped the run. Any active state can move here. |
| `cancelled` | A person cancelled the item, or rejected a question gate on a blocked item. Final. |
| `failed` | Reserved for work that cannot continue. The current workflow parks errors as `blocked` instead. A failed item can be retried from `received` or `building`. |

Every transition emits a `work_item.stage_changed` event with `from`, `to` and a reason.

## Where people decide

The factory pauses at gates. Each gate appears in the [inbox](../management/inbox.md) and in the source thread.

| Gate | Opens when | Built-in timing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spec approval | The spec is written | Nudge every 24h, park after 72h |
| Preview acceptance | The preview is deployed | Nudge every 24h, park after 72h |
| Question | A stage keeps failing, or the build agent fails twice | None |
| Command approval | The guardrail rates a shell command as risky | Waits up to 30 minutes, then blocks the command |
| Merge | The pull request is handed off | Nudge every 48h |

Rejecting a spec sends the item back to the spec stage with your feedback. Rejecting a preview sends it back to build.

## Completion

The factory never merges. A run token can push only `kiln/*` branches and cannot approve or merge. Your branch protection and reviewers do the rest. When the pull request merges, GitHub's `pull_request` webhook completes the work item. **Approve** on the merge gate instead marks it complete by human confirmation. **Request changes** on the merge gate, or a follow-up message while the work waits for its merge, sends your note to the agents: the work goes back to the build stage and returns with an updated pull request and a new merge gate. A linked Linear or Jira issue moves to its done state.

New review comments on a handed-off pull request (any review that is not an approval) send the item back to build with the comments as findings.

## Related pages

- [Concepts](concepts.md)
- [Factory agents](../configuration/agents.md)
- [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)
- [Inbox](../management/inbox.md)
